row.export_notes: The ONNX repo (created 2026-01-28 by the automatic convert-to-onnx Space for transformers.js) has one combined graph, onnx/model.onnx, not separate vision and text models. Variants and sizes: fp32 94.1 MB, fp16 47.2 MB, int8/uint8/quantized 24.3 MB, q4f16 32.1 MB, q4 58.7 MB, bnb4 58.0 MB. For the app you would re-export the vision and text towers separately (get_image_features / get_text_features) and convert to TFLite yourself. A plain ViT has standard ops (LayerNorm, GELU, softmax attention), so it should work with the GPU delegate and XNNPACK. Estimated int8 sizes: image tower about 8-9 MB, text tower about 15 MB, or about 3 MB if the token embedding is kept as a lookup. I found no TFLite/CoreML export and no mobile latency report. By MAC count it should run about as fast as the shipped 45M/32 (1.9 vs 2.0 GMACs per pair), since the 16px patches give 197 tokens against 50 for /32. So it saves download size but not speed, and gives up about 21.6 IN-1k points. Not a good upgrade candidate. It only makes sense as an ultra-light fallback.

row.name: PE-Core-S16-384 (Perception Encoder Core, Small/16, 384px)
row.arch: ViT-S/16 image tower: width 384, 12 layers, 6 heads, MLP ratio 4. It has a CLS token, absolute position embeddings plus 2D RoPE (use_rope2d=True by default), and an attention-pooling (MAP, 8 heads) head that projects to a 512-d CLIP space. Input is 384px, which gives 576 patch tokens plus CLS (577), and the position embedding has shape [1,577,384]. Text tower: CLIP-style transformer with width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, context 32 tokens, vocabulary 49,408 (CLIP BPE), projecting to 512-d. Config is from core/vision_encoder/config.py in facebookresearch/perception_models and open_clip_config.json in timm/PE-Core-S-16-384. Preprocessing: mean and std 0.5, bilinear squash resize.
row.image_params_M: 23.78M. I counted this exactly from the tensor shapes in the timm/PE-Core-S-16-384 safetensors header ('visual.*' tensors), because the official model card does not state it. That is about 48 MB fp32 and about 24-26 MB int8 (estimate).
row.text_params_M: 63.41M, counted exactly from the safetensors header (all non-visual tensors, including logit_scale). 25.3M of this is the token embedding (49408x512). The 349 MB .pt file matches the full model at about 87.2M fp32. The text tower is roughly 127 MB in fp16 or about 64 MB in int8 (estimate).
row.image_gmacs: About 15.7 GMACs at 384px. I computed this by hand and it is not reported anywhere: 12 layers x (577 x 12 x 384^2 linear + 2 x 577^2 x 384 attention) ≈ 15.3G, plus about 0.17G for patch embedding and about 0.17G for the attention-pool K/V. That is roughly 3.5x ViT-B/32@224 (about 4.4 GMACs) and several times TinyCLIP-45M/32, even though this model has half the parameters. The 576 tokens make attention cost (N^2) significant.
row.resolution: 384x384 (native and only released resolution; 576 patch tokens + CLS)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 72.7%. Source: the official perception_models GitHub README (Vision-Language Benchmarks table) and the timm/PE-Core-S-16-384 model card. The facebook/PE-Core-S16-384 HF card does NOT list S16. It is a copy of the B/L/G card with only the B/L/G tables. The arXiv 2504.13181 tables I checked do not include S/T, so the GitHub README is the primary source for this number.
row.other_zeroshot: From the same GitHub README table: IN-v2 65.0, IN-A 49.5, ObjectNet 60.0, COCO T2I retrieval 42.6, Kinetics-400 55.0, MSR-VTT T2V 39.3. The sibling T16-384 scores 62.1 IN-1k and 33.0 COCO T2I. No COCO I2T figure is reported.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The HF repo facebook/PE-Core-S16-384 has YAML license: apache-2.0. The GitHub README carries the badges 'Code License: Apache 2.0' and 'Model License: Apache 2.0' for PE. The repo file LICENSE.PE is the full Apache License 2.0 text. The timm/open_clip remap (timm/PE-Core-S-16-384) is also apache-2.0. The weights license and the code license are the same. The model card adds no use restrictions or acceptable-use policy, and the HF repo is not gated. row.load_id: open_clip: 'hf-hub:timm/PE-Core-S-16-384' (image + text, safetensors). timm image trunk only: 'vit_pe_core_small_patch16_384.fb'. Original: perception_models `pe.CLIP.from_config('PE-Core-S16-384', pretrained=True)` (HF facebook/PE-Core-S16-384, file PE-Core-S16-384.pt). An MLX port also exists at mlx-community/PE-Core-S16-384.
row.export_notes:
No TFLite/LiteRT or ONNX export exists on HF; I searched the HF API and the web. Existing ports: mlx-community/PE-Core-S16-384 (MLX), and SashimiSaketoro/PE-Core-ANE (CoreML, MIT-labelled conversion, a 45 MB fp16 S-16-384 image model). The ANE port outputs a 384-d embedding, which looks like trunk features rather than the 512-d CLIP projection, so it may not be usable for text matching. It reports no S16 latency (only B/L/G on an M3). There is also a Huawei Ascend NPU deployment guide on gitcode. I found no Android or mobile latency reports.

GPU-delegate and conversion risks for LiteRT:
- 2D RoPE: at a fixed resolution the sin/cos tables can be baked in as constants. That leaves elementwise mul/add plus rotate-half (strided slice/concat/neg), which should be delegate-friendly but needs verifying.
- The attention-pool head (1 query, 8 heads) is plain matmul/softmax.
- The 577-token sequence makes the attention matmuls and the softmax over 577x577 the dominant cost.
- My estimate (not measured) is several times TinyCLIP-45M/32's 73 ms on an A54, at about 15.7 GMACs vs about 3-4.
- Running below 384px would need position-embedding interpolation plus RoPE at the new grid; quality there is unreported.

The int8 image tower would be about 25 MB, half the current 46 MB. Path: export with open_clip/timm then convert via litert-torch (ai-edge-torch) or onnx2tf.

verdicts.corrections:
No substantive corrections; I could not refute the row. I re-checked it independently from primary sources:
(a) License. HF API: facebook/PE-Core-S16-384 has gated=False and cardData.license=apache-2.0, createdAt 2025-07-01T21:55:23Z. timm/PE-Core-S-16-384 has gated=False and is apache-2.0. GitHub README badges say Code License Apache 2.0 and Model License Apache 2.0. LICENSE.PE is the full Apache 2.0 text. The FAIR Research License (LICENSE.PLM) is attached only to the PLM section. The HF card has no use restrictions or AUP; its only "research" mention is the citation request.
(b) Numbers. Safetensors header of timm/PE-Core-S-16-384/open_clip_model.safetensors: visual.* = 23.783M and non-visual = 63.405M, matching the row exactly. Shapes confirmed: pos_embed [1,577,384], 12 trunk blocks, head [512,384], text token_embedding [49408,512], text positional_embedding [32,512]. config.py PE-Core-S16-384: image 384, patch 16, width 384, layers 12, heads 6, mlp 4.0, pool attn, output_dim 512, cls token. Text: ctx 32, width 512, heads 8, layers 12, out 512. GitHub README table for S/16 384px: IN-1k 72.7, IN-v2 65.0, IN-A 49.5, ObjectNet 60.0, COCO-T2I 42.6, K400 55.0, VTT-T2V 39.3. T/16: 62.1 and 33.0 COCO-T2I. I recomputed the GMAC estimate (12.25G linear + 3.07G attention + ~0.17G patch ≈ 15.5-15.7G) and it holds.
Minor nits:
- The attention-pool head also has a LayerNorm and an MLP (fc1 384->1536, fc2), so it is not only matmul/softmax. This is still delegate-friendly.
- Release date: the README news item says S/T were released Jul-11-25, while the HF repo createdAt is 2025-07-01.
- The facebook HF card is indeed the B/L/G card (lists B/16 0.09B etc.), with no S16 figures.

I found nothing to correct, and every claim I re-checked holds.

- **License:** The HF API for facebook/PE-Core-S16-384 returns license: apache-2.0. Its gated flag is False, and createdAt is 2025-07-01T21:55:23Z. The timm/PE-Core-S-16-384 card is also apache-2.0 and not gated. The GitHub README badges say Code License Apache 2.0 and Model License Apache 2.0. The FAIR Research License badge points to LICENSE.PLM and applies only to the PLM section. LICENSE.PE is the full Apache License 2.0 text. I grepped the HF card for research-only, non-commercial or other restriction wording and found none; its only "research" text is the citation request.
- **Param counts:** I re-counted from the timm open_clip_model.safetensors header. The visual.* tensors total 23,783,168, which matches the row's 23.78M. The remaining tensors total 63,405,057, which matches 63.41M. The full model is 87,188,225 params, and at 4 bytes each that matches the 348,852,712-byte .pt file.
- **Shapes:** pos_embed is [1,577,384], token_embedding is [49408,512], and text positional_embedding is [32,512].
- **Configs:** config.py has vision width 384, 12 layers, 6 heads, MLP ratio 4, pool_type attn, output_dim 512 and CLS token on. The text config there is context 32, width 512, 8 heads, 12 layers. open_clip_config.json matches, with timm_pool map, mean and std 0.5, bilinear, and squash resize.
- **Zero-shot numbers:** The GitHub README row for S/16 384px reads IN-1k 72.7, IN-v2 65.0, IN-A 49.5, ObjectNet 60.0, COCO-T2I 42.6, K400 55.0 and VTT-T2V 39.3. The T16 row reads 62.1 and 33.0. All of these match the row.

Not checked: I did not verify the GMAC estimate, the int8 size estimates or the export or port claims. They are labelled as estimates and do not affect the license or the numbers.

row.org: Microsoft (Cream / TinyCLIP, ICCV 2023); HF weights uploaded by author wkcn (Kan Wu)

row.license_notes: The HF model card metadata says license: mit, but the HF repo has no LICENSE file (siblings: README, config, safetensors, bin, tokenizer.json, preprocessor_config, figures). The code repo microsoft/Cream (TinyCLIP/LICENSE and root LICENSE) is "MIT License, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation", and the TinyCLIP README "License" section points to that MIT file. The GitHub release host wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo has NO license file (GitHub API license=null), so the stated weights license comes from the HF card plus the Cream README. Weights and code licenses do not conflict, and the model card adds no use restrictions. row.load_id: HF transformers: wkcn/TinyCLIP-ViT-61M-32-Text-29M-LAION400M (CLIPModel, fp32 safetensors, 461.6 MB). open_clip: hf-hub:timm/vit_betwixt_patch32_clip_224.tinyclip_laion400m (MIT, includes open_clip_config.json and the tokenizer). Original checkpoint: github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo/releases/download/checkpoints/TinyCLIP-ViT-61M-32-Text-29M-LAION400M.pt (230.8 MB, fp16)
row.arch: Plain OpenAI-CLIP-style ViT ("betwixt" width 640), patch 32, 224px gives 49 patches + CLS = 50 tokens, 12 layers, 10 heads. Text transformer: width 512, 9 layers, ctx 77. Shared embedding dim 512. Uses OpenAI CLIP mean/std and bicubic shortest-side resize. "Manual" weight inheritance (uniform shrink), unlike the "auto" models.
row.image_gmacs: About 3.1 GMACs for the image tower (my own computation: 12 layers x ~249M MACs at 50 tokens, plus a 96M patch-embed). The README's "5.3 GMACs" is image plus text combined: the text tower is about 2.2 GMACs at 77 tokens, and 3.1 + 2.2 = 5.3.
row.export_notes: No existing TFLite/LiteRT, ONNX or CoreML export found on the HF repos or the official repo. The only mobile latency report is MobileCLIP paper (arXiv 2311.17049) Table 7: 4.3 ms image + 2.6 ms text on an iPhone 12 Pro Max (Core ML Tools 7.0, iOS 17.0.3, batch 1). For comparison, TinyCLIP-40M/32 is 3.0 + 1.9 ms on the same device. The architecture is a vanilla CLIP ViT/text transformer (LayerNorm, GELU, standard MHA), the same op set as the TinyCLIP-45M the app already converts, so GPU delegate / XNNPACK compatibility should be the same. Expect roughly 1.35x the shipped model's latency (~95-100 ms on an A54, extrapolated by params/MACs, not measured). Expected size: int8 image tower about 62 MB vs 46 MB today; fp16 about 123 MB. VERDICT: dominated by the model already shipped. It is bigger (61.4M vs ~45M image params), slower, and scores lower on IN-1k zero-shot (62.4 vs 62.7). Its text tower is also bigger (54M vs ~40M). row.arch: Vision: ViT-B/16 (width 768, 12 layers, 12 heads, MLP 3072), CLS token plus an 8-head attention-pooling head projecting to a 1024-d CLIP space. row.image_params_M: 93.7M (timm vit_pe_core_base_patch16_224.fb safetensors count; the card rounds it to 0.09B). That is about 2x the current TinyCLIP 45M image tower: within the 100M ceiling but over the ~50M ideal. Expected int8 size is about 94 MB, and the existing fp16 TFLite file is 187 MB.
row.text_params_M: The card says 0.31B. My own estimate from the config is about 354M including the 50.6M token-embedding table: 24 x ~12.6M per block ≈ 302M, plus 50.6M embeddings, plus ~1M projection. A cross-check agrees: the official fp32 checkpoint is 1,790,786,632 bytes, about 447.7M params in total, and 447.7M - 93.7M ≈ 354M. That means roughly 350 MB int8 or 700 MB fp16 for the on-demand text download, which is very heavy compared with TinyCLIP's 18M text tower.

row.export_notes:
**Existing LiteRT export (image tower only):** community repo mlboydaisuke/PE-Core-base-patch16-224-LiteRT (Apache-2.0).
- File: pe_core_base_224_fp16.tflite, 187 MB fp16.
- Converted from timm vit_pe_core_base_patch16_224.fb with litert-torch / ai-edge-torch; the convert_pecore.py script is included.
- Input [1,3,224,224] NCHW float in [-1,1]; output a 1024-d L2-normalized embedding.
- Reported speed: about 66 ms/image steady-state on a Pixel 8a (Mali-G615) GPU through the LiteRT CompiledModel GPU accelerator (best 12.5 ms).
- All 1028 ops run on GPU, with no CPU fallback and no Flex ops. Getting there took four model-side rewrites, including replacing interleaved 2D RoPE with the rotate-half form and an overflow-safe LayerNorm for fp16.
- The author reports output correlation of 1.0 against PyTorch.

**Gaps and caveats:**
- I found no ONNX or CoreML export.
- No text-tower export exists. Text embeddings would have to be precomputed offline, or the 354M text tower converted yourself.
- RoPE and the attention-pool head are the GPU-delegate pitfalls; the rewrites above address them.
- No int8 or XNNPACK latency report exists. At ~17.6 GMACs vs ~4.4 for TinyCLIP-45M/32, CPU latency on a Galaxy A54 would likely be several times today's 73 ms.

**Fit for this app:** strong accuracy jump (+15.7 points IN zero-shot over TinyCLIP's 62.7) and a clean license. However, the image download roughly doubles (~94 MB int8) and the text tower is ~354M params, too heavy for an on-demand mobile download unless free-text search is moved off-device or a smaller text tower is distilled.

row.name: PE-Core-T16-384 (Perception Encoder Core, Tiny/16, 384px)
row.arch: Image tower: ViT-Ti/16 (timm vit_pe_core_tiny_patch16_384, Eva class). Width 192, 12 layers, 3 heads, MLP 768. Pre-transformer LayerNorm, 2D RoPE in attention (attn_type='rope', grid 24x24) plus a learned abs pos_embed [1,577,192]. Has a CLS token plus an 8-head attention-pooling (MAP) head, then a linear head 192->512. 384px gives 24x24 = 576 patch tokens + 1 CLS = 577 tokens. Text tower: CLIP-style transformer, width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, context 32, vocab 49408 (OpenAI CLIP BPE tokenizer). Joint embedding dim 512. Preprocess: mean/std 0.5, bilinear, squash resize. The model card does not state the training data (the paper uses Meta's MetaCLIP-style curated web data). Per the official README, T and S are distilled from larger PE-Core.
row.image_params_M: 6.14M (computed by me from the safetensors header of timm/PE-Core-T-16-384: sum of all visual.* tensors = 6,141,056). The README says "0.01B" (rounded).
row.text_params_M: 63.4M (computed by me from the safetensors header: text.* = 63,405,056, of which the token embedding is 49408x512 = 25.3M). The official README says "0.04B", which matches the ~38M non-embedding params. The ~63M figure (fp32 file ~278 MB = ~69.5M total params) is the real on-disk size. The text tower is the same shape as the OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/32 text encoder, so it is about 3.5x TinyCLIP's 18M text tower: roughly 63 MB int8 and 127 MB fp16.
row.image_gmacs: ~4.7 GMACs (my own estimate, not reported anywhere). Per block: QKV+proj 4*d^2*N = 85M, MLP 8*d^2*N = 170M, attention matmuls 2*N^2*d = 128M (N=577, d=192), so ~383M x 12 blocks = 4.6G, plus ~85M for the patch embed. That is more compute than TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224 (49 tokens) despite ~7x fewer params, and 577-token attention dominates on mobile.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 62.1% (official perception_models apps/pe/README.md table and the timm/PE-Core-T-16-384 model card). This is lower than the 62.7% of the current TinyCLIP-45M/32.
row.other_zeroshot: Official README / timm card: IN-v2 54.7, IN-A 21.1, ObjectNet 43.9, COCO T2I retrieval 33.0 (R@1), Kinetics-400 41.5, MSR-VTT T2V 28.8. For comparison, PE-Core-S16-384 gets IN 72.7 / COCO T2I 42.6 / ObjectNet 60.0, with ~22-24M img params and the same 63M text tower.

row.export_notes:
I found no official or third-party TFLite/LiteRT export or mobile latency report for T16-384, and a web search returned nothing. Derivatives on HF: mlx-community/PE-Core-T16-384 (MLX, Apple only), and namgyu-youn/pe-core-trt (ONNX + TensorRT vision/text models; I did not verify which PE size it is). Export concerns:
(1) 2D RoPE inside attention gives extra slice/concat/mul ops per block. They usually work on the TFLite GPU delegate but add overhead, and the sin/cos tables should be constant-folded at fixed 384px.
(2) The 577-token sequence makes attention N^2 = 333k per head-layer, so expect latency far above what the 6M params suggest. A 224px input (196 tokens) would need RoPE/pos-embed interpolation, with unknown accuracy loss.
(3) The MAP attention-pool head is plain ops.
(4) An int8 image tower would be only ~6-7 MB, a huge download win.
The text tower (~63 MB int8) is bigger than TinyCLIP's.
Bottom line vs the current model: smaller download, but slightly lower IN ZS (62.1 vs 62.7), probably slower on device due to 577 tokens, and a 3.5x larger text tower. PE-Core-S16-384 (72.7%) is the more interesting sibling.

row.name: TIPS v1 B/14-HR (TIPS-B/14 HR, distilled from g/14)
row.arch: Image tower: plain ViT-B/14 (12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, MLP ratio 4, GELU, qkv bias, layerscale). It has 1 CLS token plus 1 extra CLS/register token, and pos_embed is [1,1025,768]. The first CLS (alt-text-trained) is the one aligned with text; the second CLS was trained on synthetic captions. Per Appendix A.1, the released B/14 image encoder is distilled from TIPS-g/14 HR, and its text encoder is trained from scratch. Input is RGB in [0,1] with no mean/std normalization.
row.image_params_M: 86.3 (computed from the safetensors header of google/tipsv1-b14: vision_encoder = 86,316,288; includes the 448-px pos-embed of about 0.79M). The GitHub table says 85.7M and the HF card rounds to 86M.
row.text_params_M: 109.6 (computed from the safetensors header: text_encoder = 109,632,000, of which about 24.6M is the 32k x 768 token embedding). This matches the GitHub table (109.6M).
row.image_gmacs: My own estimate, not reported anywhere. At the native 448 px (1026 tokens), about 107 GMACs per image. At 224 px (258 tokens, pos-embed interpolated), about 23 GMACs. TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224 is only a few GMACs, so this is roughly 30x more compute at the native resolution.

row.export_notes: No official TFLite/LiteRT/ONNX/CoreML export of v1 B/14, and no mobile latency report found. Community ONNX exports exist only for TIPSv2 L/14 and So400m/14 (HF Armaggheddon/tips-v2-l14-onnx, tips-v2-so400m-onnx, made with "tips-onnx", with FP32/FP16/INT8 vision+text). Their input is float [0,1] with H/W as multiples of 14, and they note an FP16 text encoder batch=1 caveat. That suggests the same pipeline would likely work for B/14 (my inference). Architecture is a vanilla ViT plus a vanilla transformer (GELU/ReLU, LayerNorm, softmax attention, no exotic ops), so litert-torch (ai-edge-torch) conversion should be straightforward (inference, not tested). The HF version needs trust_remote_code (TIPSv2Model class). Mobile concerns: (1) int8 image tower is about 86 MB, nearly 2x the current 46 MB, and about 172 MB in fp16. (2) At 448 px it is about 107 GMACs, roughly 25-30x TinyCLIP-45M/32, so on a Galaxy A54 expect seconds per photo rather than ~73 ms (my estimate, not measured). Running at 224 cuts this to about 23 GMACs, but zero-shot accuracy at 224 is unreported and the model may degrade. (3) The int8 text tower is about 110 MB including a 24.6M-param embedding table. Verdict: license is fine and accuracy is strong, but it is over the ~50M ideal and its compute and download cost make it a poor fit for the image tower. The sibling TIPS v1 S/14 (21.6M image tower, 71.5% IN ZS, about 27 GMACs at 448 by the same estimate) is the more relevant TIPS candidate.
row.load_id: HF: google/tipsv1-b14 (AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True); encode_image / encode_text). Not in open_clip or timm.
row.released: Paper arXiv 2410.16512 v1 Oct 2024 (v2 07 Mar 2025, ICLR 2025). GitHub repo created 2025-03-03. HF google/tipsv1-b14 uploaded 2026-08-19. The repo now recommends TIPSv2 (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2604.12012).

row.name: TinyCLIP-ViT-39M/16-Text-19M (YFCC-15M)
row.org: Microsoft (Cream repo, ICCV 2023 TinyCLIP paper; HF upload by wkcn, a TinyCLIP author)
row.arch: Plain ViT, patch 16, 224px gives 196+1 = 197 tokens. Width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, MLP 2048. Text: CLIP transformer, width 512, 6 layers, 8 heads, ctx 77, BPE vocab 49408. Embed dim 512. Built by manual weight inheritance plus affinity-mimicking distillation from OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 (LAION-2B teacher, 70.2% IN ZS).
row.image_params_M: 38.59M, computed from the config. It exactly matches the timm image-only safetensors count of 38,587,904.
row.text_params_M: 44.5M including the token embedding table (49408x512 = 25.3M). The advertised "19M" (19.2M) excludes that table. The two towers total 83.10M, which exactly matches the HF safetensors count of 83,101,184. I computed these from config.json.
row.image_gmacs: 9.5 GMACs, from the paper Table 1 and the README. That is about 2.6x the 3.7 GMACs of the currently shipped ViT-45M/32. The cost comes from patch 16 (197 tokens versus 50).
row.in1k_zeroshot: 63.5% (paper arXiv 2309.12314 Table 1; Cream TinyCLIP README model zoo; HF card). This is only +0.8 over the currently shipped ViT-45M/32 LAION+YFCC-400M (62.7%).
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 1, zero-shot retrieval R@1. Flickr30k: I2T 84.4, T2I 66.7. MSCOCO: I2T 54.9, T2I 38.9. The current ViT-45M/32 LAION+YFCC model scores 80.3 / 63.9 and 54.0 / 36.7 on the same benchmarks, so this one is modestly better at retrieval. Throughput is 1,469 pairs/s on GPU, against 3,685 for the current model.
row.weights_license: MIT
row.license_notes:
- **Code:** microsoft/Cream root LICENSE and TinyCLIP/LICENSE are both MIT ("Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation"). I fetched both.
- **Weights:** the wkcn HF repo is tagged license: mit. The timm mirror timm/vit_medium_patch16_clip_224.tinyclip_yfcc15m is also tagged mit.
- **Restrictions:** the model card adds no use restrictions or acceptable-use policy beyond the MIT link. The weights license does not differ from the code license.
- **Data caveat, not a weights-license term:**
  - Training data is YFCC-15M, a subset of YFCC100M. That is Flickr images under a mix of Creative Commons licenses, some of them NC/ND.
  - The distillation teacher is OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 trained on LAION-2B (MIT weights, web-scraped data).
  - The same kind of data-provenance caveat applies to the TinyCLIP model already shipped.
row.load_id:
- **HF transformers:** CLIPModel.from_pretrained('wkcn/TinyCLIP-ViT-39M-16-Text-19M-YFCC15M'). Both towers are in one model.safetensors / pytorch_model.bin, plus tokenizer.json and preprocessor_config.json.
- **open_clip:** 'hf-hub:timm/vit_medium_patch16_clip_224.tinyclip_yfcc15m'. The repo has open_clip_model.safetensors with both towers.
- **timm, image tower only:** timm.create_model('vit_medium_patch16_clip_224.tinyclip_yfcc15m').
- **Original checkpoint:** a .pt file on the Cream GitHub release (TinyCLIP-model-zoo), used with the config TinyCLIP-ViT-39M-16-Text-19M.json.
row.released: 2023-09 (paper and Cream release, ICCV 2023). HF weights created 2023-12-19.
row.export_notes:
- **ONNX:** community exports exist at onnx-community/TinyCLIP-ViT-39M-16-Text-19M-YFCC15M-ONNX (2025-09) and twn39/... (2025-06). Each is a single combined model.onnx, not split into towers: fp32 333 MB, fp16 167 MB, int8/uint8 85 MB, q4f16 84 MB. Neither repo states a license.
- **TFLite/LiteRT:** I found no export and no Android latency report.
- **Mobile latency:** MobileCLIP v1 (arXiv 2311.17049, Table 4) reports 5.2 ms image + 1.9 ms text on an iPhone 12 Pro Max via Core ML. That is slower than MobileCLIP-S2 (3.6 ms) and, per the paper, less accurate.
- **Ops:** it is a vanilla ViT with standard ops (conv patch embed, LayerNorm, GELU in the HF config: hidden_act check advised, softmax attention), the same op set as the shipped ViT-45M/32. It should convert via ai-edge-torch or litert-torch and run on the GPU delegate and XNNPACK just like the current model.
- **Estimates (not measured):**
  - int8 image tower: about 39-40 MB.
  - int8 text tower: about 45 MB including the embedding table.
  - Galaxy A54: about 2.5x the current 73 ms (roughly 180 ms/photo), because of the 197-token sequence.
- **Verdict:** commercially clean, but it is a poor trade for this app. It gives +0.8 IN ZS and +1-4 retrieval R@1 for about 2.6x the compute, with only a slightly smaller image tower.

row.name: TIPS v1 S/14-HR (TIPS-S/14 HR, distilled; HF google/tipsv1-s14)
row.released: Paper Oct 2024 (arXiv 2410.16512), ICLR 2025. GCS checkpoints (tips_data/v1_0) came with the GitHub release. HF transformers port google/tipsv1-s14 was created 2026-08-19.
row.arch: Image: ViT-S/14 (12 layers, width 384, 6 heads, MLP 1536, GELU, qkv bias, LayerScale, 1 register token; DINOv2-style), trained at 448px, so 32x32 = 1024 patch tokens + CLS + 1 register. It outputs 2 CLS-style tokens. The first (cls_token) is trained on web alt-text and is the one aligned with the text tower. The second, trained on synthetic captions, is the register_tokens output. Text: 12-layer transformer, width 384, 6 heads, MLP 1536, ReLU, SentencePiece vocab 32k, max 64 tokens, lowercased. Shared embedding dim 384. The S model is knowledge-distilled from the TIPS ViT-g teacher (paper App. A.1).
row.image_params_M: 21.6 (paper Table 5 and GitHub README; HF card rounds to 22M). Consistent with the PyTorch vision .npz: 87.7 MB fp32 ≈ 21.9M.
row.text_params_M: 33.6 (paper Table 5 and README; HF card says 34M). I recomputed it from config.json: ~12.3M embeddings + ~21.2M for the 12 layers ≈ 33.5M. The HF safetensors is 222 MB F32, 55.5M total.
row.image_gmacs: Not reported anywhere. My own estimate from the config (ViT-S, d=384, 12 layers): ~31 GMACs at the native 448px (1026 tokens: ~22G linear + ~10G attention). At 224px (258 tokens, pos-emb interpolated) it is ~6 GMACs. So at native resolution it is roughly 8x the compute of TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224.
row.resolution: 448x448 native (HF config image_size 448; the GCS files are named 'highres'). The HF card says other multiples of 14 work through positional-embedding interpolation. Input is RGB in [0,1] with no mean/std normalization. The paper does not clearly state the eval resolution used for its ImageNet zero-shot number. It says protocols are identical for LR and HR models and input resolution is not modified, which implies 448 for HR models. Accuracy at 224 is not reported.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 71.5%. Source: paper arXiv 2410.16512, Appendix Table 7 'Image-text evaluations for all released TIPS model variants', row TIPS-S/14 HR. The claim is verified. The GitHub README and HF card do not report IN zero-shot; the README gives ImageNet-KNN 75.1 instead, which explains the 'not reported' claims. The Table 7 Flickr values (86.3/74.7) exactly match the README row, so the table refers to the released checkpoint. For comparison, B/14-HR scores 76.3.
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 7 (S/14 HR): COCO I->T R@1 64.8, COCO T->I R@1 50.0, Flickr I->T 86.3, Flickr T->I 74.7, DOCCI I->T 42.9 / T->I 44.7. README also lists ImageNet-KNN 75.1, UnED-KNN 57.7, PASCAL seg 80.6, NYU depth RMSE 0.425. Dense/spatial features are strong (zero-shot segmentation), which TinyCLIP does not have.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 on the HF repo google/tipsv1-s14. CC-BY-4.0 applies to the GCS .npz checkpoints, as 'all other materials' under the GitHub README. Code is Apache-2.0.
row.license_notes: GitHub (google-deepmind/tips, LICENSE = Apache-2.0) README section 'License and disclaimer': 'All software is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0'. It also says: 'All other materials are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC-BY)'. That makes the official GCS checkpoints most plausibly CC-BY-4.0: commercial use is allowed, but attribution is required, e.g. an in-app credits/licenses screen. The HF transformers port google/tipsv1-s14 is published by the google org with license: apache-2.0 in its card metadata and adds no use restrictions. It is 'converted from the official checkpoints', so the safest reading is to comply with both, which in practice means attribution. The README also says 'This is not an official Google product'. There is no acceptable-use policy, gating or research-only clause on HF or GitHub. Training data is a curated WebLI subset (~116M pairs, Google-internal) plus synthetic captions; no data license is passed on to downstream users. The license does not differ in a way that blocks commercial use: Apache-2.0 vs CC-BY-4.0 are both permissive.
row.load_id: HF: AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/tipsv1-s14", trust_remote_code=True) (model_type 'tipsv2', remote code image_encoder.py/text_encoder.py, transformers 5.x). Official: storage.googleapis.com/tips_data/v1_0/checkpoints/pytorch/tips_oss_s14_highres_distilled_vision.npz (87.7 MB) + ..._text.npz (134.4 MB); Scenic/JAX versions are in .../scenic/. Not in open_clip or timm.
row.export_notes: No TFLite/LiteRT, CoreML or mobile latency report exists for any TIPS model. Community ONNX exports (Armaggheddon/tips-v2-b14-onnx, -l14-onnx, -so400m-onnx) cover only TIPSv2 B and larger. Their card notes dynamic-shape issues with TensorRT and an FP16 text-encoder issue. There is no S/14 export. The model is a plain ViT plus a text transformer, so conversion via litert-torch/ai-edge-torch should be straightforward; ops are standard (GELU, LayerNorm, softmax attention, ReLU in the text tower). Expected int8 sizes are ~22 MB image (half of TinyCLIP's 46 MB) and ~34 MB text. The main mobile cost is compute: 1024 tokens at 448 means ~31 GMACs, roughly 4-8x TinyCLIP-45M/32, likely several hundred ms/photo on an A54 CPU. A 224px run (~6 GMACs) would require validating the accuracy drop yourself. Retrieval quality is unverified at that resolution. TIPSv2 (CVPR 2026, Apache/CC-BY) has no S size; its smallest is B/14 at 85.7M image / 109.6M text.

row.name: TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M (LAION-400M)
row.org: Microsoft (TinyCLIP, ICCV 2023; Kan Wu, Houwen Peng et al.), distributed via github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP and microsoft/Cream
row.arch: Image tower is CLIP ModifiedResNet (RN50-style bottleneck ResNet): layers [3,4,6,3], width 56 (OpenAI RN50 uses 64), 3-conv stem, anti-aliased avgpool downsampling, and an AttentionPool2d head (embed 1792, 28 heads) that outputs a 1024-d shared embedding. The attention pool alone is 11.6M of the 29.6M image params. Text tower is a CLIP transformer with 9 layers, width 512, 8 heads, context 77, vocab 49408 (CLIP BPE), projected to 1024-d. Weights were inherited (manual mask, about 75% of params) and distilled from OpenAI CLIP RN50 by affinity mimicking.
row.image_params_M: 29.6 (I computed this by instantiating TinyCLIP's own resnet.py ModifiedResNet from the repo config TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M.json. The paper/README's '30M' matches.)
row.text_params_M: 28.9 without the token-embedding table (this is the '29M' in the name), 54.2 including the 25.3M token embedding (49408x512). I computed both from the config. The released .pt is 167,871,927 bytes, which matches about 83.8M total params in fp16.
row.image_gmacs: About 4.7 GMACs for the image tower alone. I measured 9.37 GFLOPs with torch FlopCounterMode at 224px. The paper/README list 6.9 G MACs, which is apparently image+text combined. That is more compute than the shipped TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-45M/32 (README: 1.9 G MACs for the LAION+YFCC version).
row.in1k_zeroshot: 59.1% top-1 (TinyCLIP paper arXiv 2309.12314 Table 1, repeated in the README model zoo). For comparison, the teacher OpenAI CLIP RN50 gets 59.6%. This is 3.6 pts below the currently shipped auto-ViT-45M/32 LAION+YFCC (62.7%).
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 1: Flickr30k I->T@1 81.1, T->I@1 61.2; MSCOCO I->T@1 52.7, T->I@1 33.9. Throughput 1,811 pairs/s (A100, paper). Sibling ResNet-19M-Text-19M: 56.4% IN, Flickr 76.2/58.3, COCO 48.9/30.9.
row.weights_license: MIT (by the code repo; the weights host itself has no license file)
row.license_notes: The code repos wkcn/TinyCLIP and microsoft/Cream have LICENSE = MIT License, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. The README's License section points to that file and links this checkpoint. The weights host is the GitHub release wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo, tag 'checkpoints', asset TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M-LAION400M.pt. That repo has no LICENSE file (GitHub API license=null) and an empty release body, so the weights are MIT only because the repo that distributes the links is MIT. The ResNet variants are not on Hugging Face (wkcn's HF account has only 4 ViT variants, each tagged license: mit), so there is no separate model card adding use restrictions. Caveats: (1) The weights are inherited and distilled from OpenAI CLIP RN50. Those weights are MIT, but OpenAI's CLIP model card says deployed use cases, commercial or not, are 'out of scope'. That is advisory, not a license term. (2) The training data is LAION-400M: the metadata is CC-BY 4.0, the images are third-party copyrighted, and LAION frames the dataset as research-oriented. The currently shipped TinyCLIP model has the same license posture, so this candidate adds no new license risk.
row.load_id: No HF or open_clip-hub id. Use the TinyCLIP repo's fork of open_clip: create_model_and_transforms('TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M', pretrained='<path>/TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M-LAION400M.pt'), with the checkpoint from https://github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo/releases/download/checkpoints/TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M-Text-29M-LAION400M.pt (167.9 MB, fp16, image+text). The architecture is the standard OpenAI ModifiedResNet, so upstream open_clip should also load it with a custom config (width 56, text layers 9). I have not verified that.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite/ONNX/CoreML export or mobile latency report for this model. Only the ViT variants appear in third-party ports (Spark NLP, Ambarella's ViT-8M). The conv tower should be very GPU-delegate friendly: Conv/BN (foldable)/ReLU/AvgPool. The main op to watch is the AttentionPool2d head, which uses F.multi_head_attention_forward on a 50-token sequence at 1792-d. It exports to ONNX fine, but onnx2tf/ai-edge-torch turns it into batch-matmul/softmax/reshape ops, which may fall back to CPU on some GPU delegates. A rough download estimate: int8 image tower about 30 MB (vs 46 MB for the shipped ViT-45M), and int8 text tower about 55 MB including the embedding table. However, compute is about 2.5x the shipped ViT-45M/32 (about 4.7 vs 1.9 GMACs), so latency on the A54 will probably be worse, and zero-shot accuracy is lower (59.1 vs 62.7). In short, the only gain is a smaller image-tower download; it is not an upgrade on accuracy or speed.

The 22M model is therefore about 10-12 points worse on text->image retrieval, which drives the app's free-text search. Throughput is 5,504 pairs/s on an A100 against 3,685 for 45M (about 1.5x). No IN-variants or other zero-shot results were reported for this model.
row.weights_license: MIT, inferred from the repo that distributes the weights. The weights host repo has no LICENSE file of its own.
row.license_notes:
- **Code license:** microsoft/Cream is MIT according to the GitHub API, and TinyCLIP/LICENSE is MIT, "Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation". Its third-party notices cover CLIP, CoFi and OpenCLIP (all MIT) and PyTorch (BSD-style).
- **Weights host:** the checkpoint exists only as a GitHub release asset in wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo. That repo has just a README and a figure folder, no LICENSE, and the GitHub API reports license=None.
- **Why MIT still applies:** the official MIT-licensed README links the weights from its model zoo, and pretrained.py hard-codes the URL. The four sibling TinyCLIP models on Hugging Face (wkcn/*) say license: mit.
- **Model card:** there is none for this checkpoint, and I found no extra use restrictions anywhere.
- **Same footing as today:** this is exactly the licensing basis of the TinyCLIP-auto-45M checkpoint the app already ships (same release page). If that is acceptable, this one is too.
- **Data caveats:** the model was trained on LAION-400M (metadata CC-BY 4.0; images are third-party copyrighted; LAION withdrew it in 2023 over CSAM findings and replaced it with Re-LAION). It was distilled from OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 LAION-2B, which is MIT. This is the usual web-scraped-data caveat and the same exposure the app already has. It does not change the weights license.
row.load_id: Not upstream open_clip, and not on Hugging Face. The HF collection holds only the four manual-inheritance models, not the auto ones. Loading takes TinyCLIP's open_clip fork (microsoft/Cream/TinyCLIP or wkcn/TinyCLIP): open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-22M-32-Text-10M', pretrained='LAION400M'). Weights: https://github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo/releases/download/checkpoints/TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-22M-32-Text-10M-LAION400M.pt (114.2 MB, 1,186 downloads). The eval docs load it as --model ViT-B-32 --prune-image --prune-text --resume.
row.export_notes:
- **No existing export:** I found no ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or Qualcomm AI Hub export and no mobile latency report. A web search turned up nothing either.
- **Export path:** it is the same as for the TinyCLIP-auto-45M the app already exports. Physically prune the model with the fork's model.prune() methods (the L0Module masks get removed), then trace or convert as before.
- **Ops:** plain ViT/transformer ops (conv patch-embed, LayerNorm, MHA, GELU) and nothing GPU-delegate-hostile. Pruned layers can have non-uniform head counts and FFN widths, which the existing pipeline already handles for the 45M model.
- **Size estimate (not measured):** int8 image tower about 22-25 MB, based on the 46 MB int8 for the ~45M tower.
- **Latency estimate (not measured):** roughly 35-45 ms/photo on a Galaxy A54, about half of 73 ms if latency scales with MACs and params. Real ViT latency usually scales somewhat less than linearly.
- **Text tower:** fp16 about 70 MB, int8 about 35 MB, because the ~25M-param token embedding likely dominates. The paper's '10M' figure leaves it out.
- **Verdict:** this is an ultra-light fallback only. It is clearly worse than the 45M model the app ships (-9.0 IN-1k, about -12 Flickr T->I R@1) and was trained only on LAION-400M, with no LAION+YFCC version.
row.released: 2023-09 (arXiv 2309.12314, ICCV 2023). The auto-inheritance checkpoints were added to the GitHub model zoo release in late 2023. The repo was last pushed 2024-07.

row.name: TinyCLIP ResNet-19M Text-19M (LAION-400M)
row.arch: CLIP ModifiedResNet image tower (bottleneck layers [3,4,6,3], width 44, 3-conv stem, avgpool downsampling, attention-pool head with a 7x7+1 token MHA of dim 1408, 22 heads), embed_dim 1024. Text tower is a 6-layer, 512-wide, 8-head causal transformer (ctx 77, vocab 49408). No patches (conv); attention pool runs over 50 tokens. Distilled from an OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 (LAION-2B) teacher. Weights are inherited manually from TinyCLIP-ResNet-30M, which inherited from OpenAI CLIP RN50 (WIT-400M). Trained 12 epochs on LAION-400M.
row.image_params_M: 18.6 (computed by me from the official config TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M.json with a re-implementation of OpenCLIP ModifiedResNet: 18.60M. The attention-pool head alone is 7.46M). Paper Table 1 says 19M. Estimated int8 size is about 19 MB, versus 46 MB for the current tower.
row.text_params_M: 44.8 total, computed from config: 19.5M in the transformer, plus a 25.3M token embedding, plus the projection. The paper's "19M" excludes the token embedding. Cross-check: the release .pt is 126,949,695 bytes, which is about 63.4M params x 2 bytes, so it is an fp16 checkpoint of both towers. That matches 18.6 + 44.8.
row.image_gmacs: 2.74 GMACs for the image tower at 224px (computed with torch FlopCounterMode on the config re-implementation). The paper and README list 4.4 G MACs, which appears to count image + text together.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 56.4% (TinyCLIP paper arXiv:2309.12314 Table 1 and repo README model zoo). This is 6.3 points below the currently shipped TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-45M/32 LAION+YFCC (62.7%). Same family: ResNet-30M Text-29M = 59.1%.
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 1: Flickr30k I->T@1 76.2, T->I@1 58.3; MSCOCO I->T@1 48.9, T->I@1 30.9. For comparison, OpenAI CLIP RN50 scores 81.2/58.2/50.8/28.3, and ResNet-30M scores 81.1/61.2/52.7/33.9.
row.weights_license: MIT (Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation). This is the LICENSE in github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP and in microsoft/Cream/TinyCLIP. The weights host repo wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo has no LICENSE file (GitHub API license: null). The README there points to microsoft/Cream, and the TinyCLIP README's License section links the MIT LICENSE.
row.license_notes: Code is MIT (Microsoft). The weights are distributed as a GitHub release asset in wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo. That repo carries no license file of its own; MIT is inferred from the code repo, which hosts the model zoo table and download links. This is the same situation as the currently shipped TinyCLIP model. Neither README adds use restrictions; I searched for research-only, commercial and responsible-use wording and found none. Caveats: (1) The weights come by inheritance from OpenAI CLIP RN50. The OpenAI CLIP repo is MIT, but its model card says deployed use cases are out of scope. That card is guidance, not a license term, and it applies equally to the current TinyCLIP ViT models (OpenCLIP teacher). (2) Training data is LAION-400M: metadata is CC-BY 4.0, image copyrights belong to third parties, and the dataset was withdrawn in 2023 over CSAM findings (Re-LAION replaced it). The license risk is the same as for the currently shipped model.
row.load_id: No HF Hub repo; the wkcn HF collection holds only 4 ViT models. Load via the TinyCLIP fork of open_clip: model name 'TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M' (config in src/open_clip/model_configs) plus checkpoint https://github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo/releases/download/checkpoints/TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M-LAION400M.pt (126.9 MB, fp16, contains both towers). Upstream open_clip has no pretrained tag for it, and HF transformers CLIPModel does not support ModifiedResNet. Upstream open_clip's ModifiedResNet class accepts this config directly (layers/width json).
row.export_notes: I found no existing ONNX, TFLite or CoreML export and no mobile latency report; only TinyCLIP ViT-39M/16 has community ONNX ports. The image tower should be GPU-delegate friendly: plain Conv2d, BatchNorm (foldable), ReLU, AvgPool2d, residual add, and no GELU or LayerNorm. The only non-conv part is the attention pool, a single-query MHA over 50 tokens: mean, concat, add positional embedding, linear, softmax, matmul. It is small and should convert cleanly through litert-torch/ai-edge-torch or ONNX->TFLite. The text tower is the standard CLIP transformer (GELU/LayerNorm/causal mask), the same as the current text tower. Paper throughput is 3,024 pairs/s on V100, versus 3,682 for ViT-45M/32 (LAION-400M) and 3,685 for the LAION+YFCC variant. The README also lists ViT-45M/32 at 3.7G MACs. So on GPU it is not faster than the shipped model, and its accuracy is lower. Its main gains are an image tower about 2.4x smaller (18.6M vs ~45M params) and a conv architecture that may run faster on mobile GPU/NPU. That would need measuring on the A54.
row.released: 2023-09 (arXiv 2309.12314, ICCV 2023); checkpoint release in wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo, 'checkpoints' tag
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.12314 (Table 1: ResNet-19M 19+19M params, 4.4G MACs, 56.4% IN-1k, Flickr/COCO retrieval; Sec 4: inherits from ResNet-30M, 12 epochs)

verdicts.corrections:
I found nothing that refutes the row. Only small points need care.

(1) License. github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP/LICENSE and microsoft/Cream/TinyCLIP/LICENSE are both MIT, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. The weights repo wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo has no license: the GitHub API returns license: null. Its README only sends readers to microsoft/Cream for the code. So MIT for the weights is inferred from the companion code repo; no explicit weights license exists. Neither README has research-only, non-commercial or gated-access wording. This is the same basis as the currently shipped TinyCLIP model, so the license holds to the same standard.

(2) Image params. I re-derived 18.60M from the official config (layers [3,4,6,3], width 44, embed_dim 1024). The attention pool is 7.46M of that. This confirms the row.

(3) Text params. I get 44.78M in total. The 6x512 transformer blocks alone are 18.91M. Adding the positional embedding, the final LayerNorm and the 512x1024 projection gives about 19.5M, which is the figure the row uses. The token embedding adds 25.30M. All of this agrees with the row.

(4) Checkpoint. The release asset TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M-LAION400M.pt is 126,949,695 bytes. At 63.37M params x 2 bytes that is about 126.7 MB plus overhead, which fits an fp16 file holding both towers.

(5) ImageNet zero-shot. The TinyCLIP README model zoo and the model-zoo README both give 56.4% and 4.4 G MACs. This confirms the row.

I could not refute the license or the numbers. One factual error in the arch field: the row says the ResNet-19M was "Distilled from an OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 (LAION-2B) teacher". That is not supported. Paper Sec 4 (arXiv 2309.12314) says that on LAION-400M they distilled three different teachers: Florence DaViT, CLIP ResNet, and OpenCLIP ViT-B/32. The ResNet students belong to the CLIP ResNet (OpenAI, WIT-400M) branch. The paper says ResNet-30M is trained for 4 epochs in the first stage and inherits 75% of its parameters from the original model, and ResNet-19M inherits from the 30M model and is trained for 12 epochs. The passage does not say whether the teacher is RN50 or RN101; Table 1 lists both as baselines. Correct the arch field to: distilled from OpenAI CLIP ResNet (the teacher is OpenAI CLIP, not OpenCLIP ViT-B/32). License risk is unchanged, because OpenAI CLIP is MIT.

Verified items:
- Config TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M.json: layers [3,4,6,3], width 44, embed_dim 1024, text 6L/512w/8h, ctx 77, vocab 49408.
- My own re-implementation gives an image tower of 18.597M params, with an attention pool of 7.465M. Text total is 44.78M (transformer blocks 18.91M + token embedding 25.30M + positional/LN/projection). The row's "19.5M transformer" figure includes the positional embedding, final LN and projection; that is fine.
- Release asset TinyCLIP-ResNet-19M-Text-19M-LAION400M.pt is 126,949,695 bytes, which is consistent with about 63.4M fp16 params.
- Table 1: 19+19M params, 4.4 GMACs, 3,024 pairs/s, LAION-400M, IN-1k 56.4. Flickr30k I2T/T2I 76.2/58.3 and MSCOCO 48.9/30.9. RN50 is 81.2/58.2/50.8/28.3, ResNet-30M is 59.1 and 81.1/61.2/52.7/33.9, and ViT-45M/32 LAION+YFCC is 62.7. All match the row.
- LICENSE files in wkcn/TinyCLIP and in microsoft/Cream/TinyCLIP are both MIT, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
- The wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo GitHub API shows license null, and its README only points to microsoft/Cream. MIT for the weights is therefore inferred, not explicit. This is the same situation as the shipped ViT-45M model.
- I did not independently verify the 2.74 GMACs image-only figure.

row.name: TIPSv2 B/14
row.arch: The image tower is a ViT-B/14 (DINOv2-with-registers style): 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, MLP 3072, GELU, QKV bias, no SwiGLU. It has 1 register token, which is reused as a second CLS token: CLS 1 is trained on alt-text and CLS 2 on PaliGemma synthetic captions. The config defaults to 448x448 input, which gives 32x32 = 1024 patch tokens plus 2. The text tower is a 12-layer transformer: width 768, 12 heads, MLP 3072, ReLU, 32k SentencePiece vocabulary, lowercased, max 64 tokens. The embedding dimension is 768. B/14 is distilled from the ViT-g/14 teacher with patch-level distillation; it was not pretrained directly.
row.image_params_M: 85.7-86.3. The GitHub README says 85.7M; paper Table 16 and the HF card say 86.3M / 86M. This is close to the ~100M ceiling, about 1.9x TinyCLIP-45M's image tower. An int8 image tower would be roughly 86-90 MB (my estimate).
row.text_params_M: 109.6. Confirmed by paper Table 16 and the GitHub README. Total is 195.9M; the HF safetensors header shows 195,948,288 F32 parameters. An int8 text tower would be about 110 MB (my estimate).
row.image_gmacs: Not reported. My estimate from standard ViT-B FLOP scaling: about 23 GMACs at 224px (258 tokens) and about 105 GMACs at the native 448px (1026 tokens). TinyCLIP-45M/32 is about 3.7 GMACs.
row.resolution: 448x448 per the config, HF processor and card example. The architecture accepts any resolution. Distilled students received a high-resolution adaptation stage (448 global crops), so running at 224 is untested and quality there is unknown.
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported for B/14. Paper Table 6 gives ImageNet zero-shot only for g/14 (80.7). The GitHub README and HF card give no zero-shot number for any size. B/14's ImageNet KNN is 79.8 (paper Table 15 and GitHub README); KNN is not zero-shot.
row.other_zeroshot: B/14 per paper Table 15: Flickr30k I->T 92.6 and T->I 80.0. ADE20K-150 zero-shot segmentation is 17.4 mIoU (GitHub README). COCO retrieval for B/14 is not reported.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 (license tag on the HF repo google/tipsv2-b14). The GitHub repo is unclear for the checkpoints themselves.
row.license_notes:
- **HF repo google/tipsv2-b14:** license tag is apache-2.0. It is public and not gated, and the model card adds no use restrictions.
- **GitHub repo google-deepmind/tips:** code is Apache-2.0. The README also says all other materials are CC-BY-4.0, without saying whether the checkpoints count as "other materials". If that clause applies to the GitHub-hosted .npz checkpoints, it is still commercial-OK, but attribution is required.
- The README adds the standard "not an official Google product" disclaimer.
- The paper is CC-BY-4.0 on arXiv and gives no weights license.
- **Data caveat:** training data is a filtered WebLI subset (~116M images) plus PaliGemma and Gemini 1.5 Flash synthetic captions. None of this is released, and no data-use restriction is placed on the weights.
- **Recommendation:** use the HF Apache-2.0 copy and include the Apache NOTICE/attribution.
row.load_id: HF: google/tipsv2-b14. Load with `AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/tipsv2-b14", trust_remote_code=True)`; transformers main also has native Tipsv2Model / Tipsv2VisionModel / Tipsv2Tokenizer and pipeline("zero-shot-image-classification"). Use `get_image_features` / `get_text_features`. The GitHub google-deepmind/tips repo has PyTorch and JAX checkpoints with separate vision and text .npz files.
row.released: The HF repo was created 2026-04-09 (last modified 2026-08-17). The paper was posted to arXiv 2026-04-13 and appears at CVPR 2026.
row.export_notes:
- **Existing LiteRT export (vision only):** litert-community/TIPSv2-B14-DPT-LiteRT (Apache-2.0). It packs the B/14 backbone plus three DPT dense heads (depth, normals, ADE20K segmentation) into one fp16 graph of 318 MB at 1x3x448x448. It outputs dense maps only: no CLS/embedding output and no text encoder.
- **Conversion notes:** it was converted with litert-torch (build_tipsv2.py). It needed GPU-friendly rewrites of the attention reshape, LayerNorm, GELU (tanh vs erf variants) and transposed conv, which shows the stock graph is not delegate-clean.
- **Reported latency (backbone + 3 heads, 448px):** Pixel 8a GPU about 0.92 s/image (1434/1434 nodes delegated). Galaxy S26 NPU 142 ms (erf build) and GPU 273-283 ms. Raspberry Pi 5 CPU about 10.6 s with about 1.3 GB peak memory. The card says the Mali GPU path is unverified with the erf build.
- **No other exports found:** no ONNX/TFLite/CoreML export of the CLIP-style image-embedding head or the text tower.
- **Rough fit for this app:** the backbone alone at 448 is about 28x TinyCLIP's compute, so expect several hundred ms per photo on a Galaxy A54. Running at 224 cuts this about 4.5x, but accuracy at 224 is unverified.
- **Size:** an int8 image tower would be about 86-90 MB, versus 46 MB now.

verdicts.corrections:
I could not refute the row; the license and core numbers check out.

1. **License:** the HF card for google/tipsv2-b14 tags it apache-2.0 and its License section says "Apache 2.0". It is not gated and adds no extra terms. The GitHub README licenses software under Apache-2.0 and all other materials under CC-BY-4.0, without naming the checkpoints. Either license permits commercial use. The paper states no weights license. It only says that code and models are released via gdm-tipsv2.github.io.

2. **Param counts:** these hold. The GitHub README gives 85.7M vision and 109.6M text. Paper Table 16 gives 86.3M image, 109.6M text and 195.9M total. The HF card gives 86M and 110M.

3. **Zero-shot numbers:** the claim that B/14 has no IN-1k zero-shot number holds, and B/14 KNN is 79.8 (Table 15). One minor gap: the row implies only g/14 has an ImageNet zero-shot figure. Paper Table 8 also reports TIPSv2 L/14 ImageNet zero-shot at 79.7. Table 6 has g/14 at 80.7. No B/14 or SO/14 zero-shot number exists.

4. **Retrieval and segmentation:** Flickr30k for B/14 (I->T 92.6, T->I 80.0) and ADE150 zero-shot segmentation 17.4 are confirmed.

I could not refute the row. Every checkable claim matches the primary sources.

**License**
- **HF repo (API):** license is apache-2.0 and the repo is not gated (gated:false).
- **Model card:** the "## License" section says "Apache 2.0" and adds no use restrictions.
- **GitHub README:** software is Apache-2.0, all other materials are CC-BY-4.0, and it carries the "not an official Google product" disclaimer. Both licenses allow commercial use, and I found no research-only or NC clause.
- **LiteRT export:** litert-community/TIPSv2-B14-DPT-LiteRT is also apache-2.0 and not gated. It contains tipsv2_b14_dpt_fp16.tflite, tipsv2_b14_dpt_erf_fp16.tflite and build_tipsv2.py.

**Numbers**
- **Param counts:** the GitHub README gives B/14 as 85.7M / 109.6M. Paper Table 16 gives 86.3M / 109.6M / 195.9M total. The HF card says 86M / 110M. The HF safetensors total is 195,948,288 F32.
- **ImageNet zero-shot:** none is reported for B/14. Paper Table 6 gives 0-shot ImageNet 80.7 only for g/14.
- **One addition the row lacks:** paper Table 8 gives L/14 ImageNet 0-shot 79.7.
- **B/14 metrics:** Table 15 and the README give KNN 79.8, Flickr I->T 92.6, T->I 80.0 and ADE150-ZS 17.4. These match the row.
- **Resolution:** the HF card example uses Resize((448,448)) and outputs 1024 patch tokens, which matches the row.
- **Paper note:** the paper says TIPSv2 does "not perform as well in ImageNet classification".

**Minor nuance (not an error)**
- The HF card's "Model details" says "resize to any resolution", but the 448 default still holds.

**Lead for the table (not a correction to this row)**
- Google also publishes TIPS v1 checkpoints on HF, including google/tipsv1-s14. It is apache-2.0, not gated, created 2026-08-19, and has 55.5M F32 params total.
- The GitHub README lists S/14-HR at 21.6M vision / 33.6M text, with ImageNet-KNN 75.1 and Flickr I->T 86.3 / T->I 74.7. No zero-shot ImageNet number is shown for it.
- S/14-HR is a much better size fit for this app than B/14 and is worth its own row.

row.name: OpenVision ViT-B/8-224
row.image_params_M: ~86.2M (computed from open_clip_config.json: ViT-B width 768, 12 layers, patch 8, 224px, 785 pos-emb, 512 proj). The README says 86M. Cross-check: the fp32 checkpoint is 562,968,474 bytes, about 140.7M params, which equals 86.2 image + 54.5 text. This is about 1.9x the current TinyCLIP 45M tower, inside the 100M ceiling but well over the ~50M target. Estimated int8 size is about 87 MB, versus 46 MB today.
row.text_params_M: ~54.5M (computed from config: width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, vocab 32000 with BERT-base-uncased tokenizer, context 80, bidirectional with no causal mask, last-token pool, 512 text projection). The token embedding alone is 16.4M of that. About 3x TinyCLIP's 18M text tower.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 75.4% at 224px, from the official OpenVision GitHub README model-zoo table (row: ViT-Base, 86M, patch 8, 224, 75.4%). Siblings: B/8-160 74.8%, B/8-384 75.6%, B/16-224 73.9%, S/16-224 65.9%, S/8-224 68.6%, Ti/8-224 53.5%.
row.other_zeroshot: None checked in the README zoo table. The OpenVision paper (arXiv 2505.04601) mostly reports results as a LLaVA vision encoder, not COCO/Flickr retrieval, and no retrieval numbers for B/8 were confirmed.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The weights host and the code repo both say Apache-2.0 and match. The HF model card metadata has license: apache-2.0, with a 361-byte card that adds no use restrictions. The repo is not gated. The GitHub LICENSE file is the full Apache License 2.0, and the README says "licensed under the Apache License 2.0". Data caveats: training data is DataComp-1B images (web-scraped) plus Recap-DataComp-1B synthetic captions. The HF dataset card for Recap-DataComp-1B says CC-BY-4.0. Those captions came from a LLaVA/LLaMA-3-based captioner, so the Llama 3 license terms on outputs may apply upstream. That restriction targets improving other LLMs, not vision encoders, so the risk for shipping the encoder weights is low, but you may want legal to note it. The weights license itself has no NC/research-only clause.
row.load_id: open_clip: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('hf-hub:UCSC-VLAA/openvision-vit-base-patch8-224'). The HF repo has open_clip_pytorch_model.bin (563 MB fp32, image+text), open_clip_config.json, BERT tokenizer files, and the JAX orbax checkpoint in jax_orbax_weight/.
row.arch: ViT-B/8 image tower: 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads (head_width 64), patch 8, 28x28 = 784 patch tokens (+1 class pos slot). No ln_pre, global avg pool, LN after pool, embed dim 512. Text tower is a 12-layer, 512-wide bidirectional transformer with BERT-uncased vocab (32k), context 80. Preprocessing uses ImageNet mean/std (0.485/0.456/0.406, 0.229/0.224/0.225), bilinear squash resize. This differs from OpenAI CLIP normalization.
row.image_gmacs: ~78 GMACs, computed for 785 tokens: about 6.5 GMAC/layer x 12 plus the patch embed. This matches timm's 78.2 GMACs for vit_base_patch8_224. It is roughly 17-20x TinyCLIP-45M/32 (about 4 GMACs) and about 4.4x ViT-B/16 (17.6 GMACs).
row.export_notes: No existing ONNX, TFLite, LiteRT or CoreML export of any OpenVision model was found, and no mobile latency report either (searched the GitHub README, HF repo files and the web). The ops are plain ViT (conv patch embed, MHA, GELU-tanh, LayerNorm, avg pool), so standard paths should work: torch.onnx, then onnx2tf or ai-edge-torch. The bad fit is compute. With 785 tokens, the attention matrices are 12 x 785x785 per layer, and at about 78 GMACs per image, an A54 should land far above today's 73 ms/photo. Rough extrapolation, not measured: several hundred ms to over 1 s per image on CPU/GPU delegate. Not suitable for bulk indexing of a photo library. Within this family, OpenVision B/16-224 (73.9%, about 17.6 GMACs, same 86M params) gives nearly the same accuracy at about 4.4x less compute. S/16-224 (22M, 65.9%) is the size-matched option.
row.released: HF repo created 2025-05-06, last modified 2025-05-17. Paper arXiv 2505.04601 (May 2025, ICCV 2025).

verdicts.corrections:
I found nothing to refute. Every check matched the row.

License: The HF API shows license:apache-2.0 and gated:false. The 361-byte model card has only license and pipeline_tag metadata plus links, with no use restrictions. The GitHub LICENSE file is the full Apache 2.0 text, and the README says "licensed under the Apache License 2.0". The HF API confirms Recap-DataComp-1B is cc-by-4.0. row.image_params_M: 22.0 (model card: 'trainable params Image+Text 22.0+40.4'). Cross-check: pytorch_model.bin is 250,017,253 bytes in fp32, which is about 62.5M params total and matches 22.0+40.4. Expected int8 image tower is about 22-24 MB, roughly half of TinyCLIP-45M/32's 46 MB.
row.text_params_M: 40.4 (model card). From config.json (text_cfg width 384, 12 layers, 6 heads, vocab 49408, ctx 77): the token embedding is 49408x384 = 19.0M, plus 12 transformer layers at 12*384^2 = 21.2M, plus pos/proj, which comes to about 40.4M. row.resolution: 224px (patch-equivalent: 196 tokens at 14x14 after a conv stem)
row.arch: Hybrid conv + ViT, from timm vitamin.py `vitamin_small_224`. Conv stem is 64 ch, stride 2. Then MBConv stage 1 (64 ch, 2 blocks) and stage 2 (128 ch, 4 blocks), using LayerNorm2d pre-norm, GELU, depthwise 3x3 and avg-pool downsample shortcuts. Then a 1-block embed to 384 ch at 14x14 = 196 tokens. Then 14 ViT blocks (dim 384, 6 heads) with a GeGLU MLP (mlp_ratio 2), no class token, global average pool, and a linear projection to 384. The text tower is a standard OpenCLIP causal transformer, 12 layers / width 384 / 6 heads, context 77.

Sibling ViTamin-S-LTT reports 63.4% with the same 22.0M image tower, but its timm cfg projects to 768-d (num_classes=768), so the text-side setup differs; not verified. Both are roughly equal to TinyCLIP-45M/32's 62.7%, so this model is no accuracy upgrade.

row.export_notes:
I found no TFLite, ONNX, CoreML or LiteRT export of ViTamin-S on the HF hub. The only repos are the official jienengchen/* PyTorch .bin files plus unrelated derivatives of the B-sized model. I also found no mobile latency report, and the paper reports none for phones. Export path: timm/open_clip, then PyTorch, then ai-edge-torch (or ONNX, then TFLite).

Possible GPU-delegate friction:
- LayerNorm2d (channel-last permute + LN) runs at high resolution (112x112 / 56x56) in the MBConv stages. That adds transposes, and LN at large spatial size is slower on the mobile GPU than BatchNorm.
- GELU (erf) appears everywhere, including in the conv stages. Exporters often lower it to tanh-approx or erf; check delegate coverage.
- GeGLU needs split + mul. It is supported, but each one is an extra op.
- The attention itself is simple (196 tokens, 6 heads). There is no class token or interpolated pos-embed at a fixed 224px.

Compute is 5.5 GMACs, higher than a ViT-*/32 at 224 such as TinyCLIP-45M/32. Most of it is at 196 tokens plus the conv stages. Despite having half the params, expect latency similar to or higher than the current 73 ms on an A54 (my estimate, not measured).

The int8 image tower should be about 22 MB versus 46 MB, which is the main win. The text tower is about 40 MB int8, about 19 MB of which is the token embedding table. Zero-shot accuracy (62.2%) roughly equals the current model, so ViTamin-S is a size/download upgrade, not a quality upgrade.

row.arch:
Plain ViT-B/16 image tower:
- Width 768, 12 layers, 12 heads.
- No ln_pre; global average pool, then LayerNorm, then a linear projection to the 512-d shared embedding.
- Token counts: 100 patches at 160, 196 at 224, 576 at 384.
- Preprocessing: ImageNet mean/std, bilinear "squash" resize.

Text tower: a 12-layer, 512-wide bidirectional transformer with a BERT WordPiece tokenizer.

Training: CLIPS-style contrastive + generative training on Recap-DataComp-1B; progressive resolution starting at 160.
row.image_gmacs: Estimated, not reported by the authors: about 8.8 at 160, about 17.6 at 224 (standard ViT-B/16 figure, as in timm), and about 55.5 at 384. That is roughly 2.4x / 4.8x / 15x the compute of TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224 (about 3.7 GMACs, also an estimate).
row.released: 2025-05-06/07 (HF repos created); paper arXiv 2505.04601 (ICCV 2025)
row.export_notes:
I found no official or third-party TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. The GitHub README has no export section, and a web search turned up nothing.

Export should be easy:
- The ops are vanilla ViT: conv patch-embed, LayerNorm, MHA, GELU (exact erf in the image tower, tanh-approx in the text tower), mean-pool and linear layers. Nothing exotic, and it should work with the GPU delegate and XNNPACK, the same as any ViT-B/16.
- Use the separate per-resolution checkpoints rather than resizing positional embeddings at runtime.

Size against the current model:
- Image tower is about 86M params: roughly 86-88 MB as int8 and about 172 MB as fp16. The current TinyCLIP int8 tower is 46 MB, so this is about 1.9x the download.
- Text tower int8 is about 55 MB; 16 MB of that is the embedding table.

Latency on a Galaxy A54, my extrapolation only, not measured: about 2.4x TinyCLIP's 73 ms at 160 and about 4-5x at 224. That puts it near 170-350 ms per photo on CPU int8. The 384 checkpoint is impractical for indexing a whole gallery.

Fit: it exceeds the ~50M image-param target but is under the ~100M ceiling. 160px is the best fit, at 72.4% zero-shot and about 8.8 GMACs.

Note: switching text towers means swapping to the BERT WordPiece tokenizer (context 80) and recomputing the ~3,600 concept vectors.

The architecture is plain ViT plus a BERT-style encoder with standard ops (LayerNorm, tanh-GELU, MHA, mean-pool), so it should convert through ai-edge-torch or ONNX to TFLite like any open_clip ViT. Expected issues are the usual ones for ViTs on the GPU delegate: LayerNorm and GELU decomposition, and int8 attention accuracy. Compute is the main risk: at 224, S/16 runs 196 tokens and about 4.6 GMACs per image, several times what the current ViT-45M/32 uses (49 tokens). row.arch: Hybrid conv and ViT model, timm `vitamin_base_224`. The stem (width 128) feeds 2 MBConv stages with depths (2,4) and widths (128,256). These use LayerNorm2d, GELU and depthwise convs, and reach stride 16. Next is a 14-block ViT stage at width 768 with 12 heads and a GeGLU MLP (ratio 2). It works on 196 tokens (14x14) at 224px, which is 4x the 49 tokens of a B/32. Linear projection to a 512-d shared embedding. Text tower: a standard CLIP causal transformer (12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408 CLIP BPE). Sibling ViTamin-B-LTT ('locked text tower') uses the same image tower. Its open_clip config has a 768-wide text tower, but its model card table says 12/512, so the two disagree.

The HF repo has only pytorch_model.bin (fp32, 604 MB, image + text) plus remote-code .py files, and a search turned up nothing ViTamin-specific. Export risks for the GPU delegate: (1) LayerNorm2d (channels-first LN) in the MBConv stages lowers to transpose+LN or to mean/var ops, which work but are slow and unfused on GPU delegates. (2) GeGLU MLP (split + GELU + mul) is fine but adds ops. (3) 196 tokens x 14 blocks at width 768 makes attention 4x heavier than B/32. (4) Exact (erf) GELU everywhere. Swapping it for the tanh approximation is advisable for XNNPACK/GPU. No exotic ops are expected; it is plain PyTorch with timm layers, so litert-torch / ai-edge-torch or ONNX->TFLite should work, but conversion has not been tested. The text tower is a vanilla CLIP text transformer, so it is easy to export.

row.name: OpenVision ViT-S/8 (160 / 224), CLIPS-style dual encoder (image + text tower)
row.org: UCSC-VLAA (UC Santa Cruz; Xianhang Li, Yanqing Liu, Haoqin Tu, Hongru Zhu, Cihang Xie)
row.arch: Image tower: plain ViT-S, patch 8, width 384, 12 layers, 6 heads (head_width 64), MLP ratio 4. No ln_pre. Avg-pool over patch tokens, then a final LN and a 384x384 projection. Embed dim 384. 224 px gives 28x28 = 784 patch tokens + 1 cls = 785; 160 px gives 400 + 1 = 401. Text tower: 12-layer, width 384, 6-head transformer with no causal mask and 'last' pooling. Context length 80, vocab 32000, bert-base-uncased tokenizer with the SEP token stripped, GELU-tanh. Preprocessing: ImageNet mean/std (0.485, 0.456, 0.406 / 0.229, 0.224, 0.225), bilinear 'squash' resize. Trained with the CLIPS framework (contrastive loss plus a caption decoder) on Recap-DataComp-1B, in three stages at 160, then 224, then 384 px.
row.image_params_M: 21.8M at 224 (21,817,344), 21.7M at 160 (21,669,888). I computed these from open_clip_config.json: 12 blocks x 1,774,464 + patch embed 73,728 (no bias) + pos emb 785x384 + cls + ln_post + 384x384 proj. The README rounds this to "22M". About half of TinyCLIP-45M/32's image tower. Int8 would be about 22 MB and fp16 about 44 MB.
row.text_params_M: 33.8M (33,760,512), computed from the config: token emb 32000x384 = 12.29M, 12 blocks = 21.29M, pos emb, ln_final and a 384x384 projection. Image + text = 55.58M, which fits the size of the released fp32 open_clip_pytorch_model.bin (222,411,674 bytes, or about 55.6M x 4 B). The text tower is released in the same checkpoint and is larger than TinyCLIP's 18M text tower (int8 about 34 MB).
row.image_gmacs: 224 px: about 22.4 GMACs. 160 px: about 10.0 GMACs. I computed these myself: per block 12*N*d^2 + 2*N^2*d, with N = 785 or 401 and d = 384, plus the patch embed. The 224 version is about 4x ViT-S/16 and roughly 5x TinyCLIP-45M/32 (ViT-B/32-class at about 4.4 GMACs), so expect several times the current 73 ms/photo. Attention at 224 also builds 785x785 maps per head, and the paper notes patch 8 causes "much higher memory consumption and latency".
row.resolution: 160 and 224 are the candidates. There are also separate repos for 384 (68.5%) and S/16 at 160/224/384. Each resolution is a separate HF repo with its own pos-emb.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 68.6% at 224 and 67.3% at 160, from the model-zoo table in the official GitHub README (column "IN-1K Top-1"). The paper's Table 1 defines that metric as zero-shot ImageNet classification, but the paper does not table S/8 zero-shot by resolution (Table 5 gives S/8 only in LLaVA downstream tasks). Same-family references from the README: S/16 at 224 is 65.9%, S/16 at 160 is 63.5%, Ti/8 at 224 is 53.5%. That makes S/8 at 224 about +5.9 pts over TinyCLIP 45M/32 (62.7%).
row.other_zeroshot: S/8 retrieval is not reported. For S/16 at 224, the paper's Table 3 gives MSCOCO retrieval 43.6 / 64.5 (as reported). The paper reports no Flickr results. Table 5 (LLaVA-1.5 downstream): S/8 gets TextVQA 59.3 and ChartQA 15.9, versus 54.3 and 12.0 for S/16.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The HF model card metadata for both the 224 and 160 repos says license: apache-2.0. The card body adds no use restrictions; it only links the paper, project page and code. The HF repo has no separate LICENSE file, only the metadata tag. The GitHub code repo's LICENSE file is Apache-2.0, and the paper claims to release all weights, code and data. So the weights and code licenses are the same. Data caveat: the training data is Recap-DataComp-1B, licensed CC-BY-4.0. Its captions come from LLaVA-1.5-LLaMA3-8B, so there is upstream Llama 3 license lineage in the synthetic captions. That license's output clauses mainly target improving other LLMs, which this is not. The images are DataComp web crawl, with 1.9% flagged opt-out by Spawning. These are the usual provenance caveats for web-data CLIP models and do not restrict the weights license. No NC or research-only terms were found anywhere.
row.load_id: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('hf-hub:UCSC-VLAA/openvision-vit-small-patch8-224'), or ...-patch8-160. Tokenizer: open_clip.get_tokenizer(same id). The JAX orbax weights are under /jax_orbax_weight in the same repos.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export and no mobile latency report; search found nothing, and the repo and paper only say "edge-ready" with no measurements. The architecture is a vanilla ViT (LayerNorm, GELU-tanh, MHA, avg pool) with no unusual ops, so open_clip to ONNX or ai-edge-torch to LiteRT should be straightforward and GPU-delegate friendly. One quirk: the text tower uses 'last' pooling with no causal mask and a stripped SEP token, so match open_clip's tokenizer handling when precomputing or running text on device. The main risk is compute, not ops. 785 tokens means about 22 GMACs at 224, roughly 5x TinyCLIP-45M/32, plus large attention activations. The 160 px variant (about 10 GMACs, 67.3%) is the realistic mobile pick, about 2.3x TinyCLIP's compute for +4.6 pts. By comparison, S/16 at 224 is about 4.6 GMACs for 65.9%. These latency ratios are my estimates and have not been measured.

row.name: DatologyAI cls-opt-vit-b-32 (sibling: retr-opt-vit-b-32)
row.arch: Unmodified OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 (see open_clip_config.json): vision has width 768, 12 layers and patch 32 at 224px, giving 7x7=49 patches plus CLS = 50 tokens. Text is a 12-layer, width-512, 8-head transformer with 77-token context and the 49,408-token CLIP BPE vocab. Shared embedding dim is 512. Uses OpenAI CLIP mean/std with bicubic shortest-side resize.
row.image_params_M: ~87.8M. I computed this from the config because the card only says "about 86M". Breakdown: patch conv 2.36M, positional/CLS ~0.04M, 12 blocks x 7.08M = 85.0M, LN and projection 768x512 = 0.39M. That makes it about 2x the TinyCLIP-45M image tower. Estimated int8 image tower is ~88-90 MB, against 46 MB today.
row.text_params_M: ~63.4M. I computed this from the config: token embedding 25.3M, 12 blocks x 3.15M = 37.8M, projection 0.26M. Total 151.3M x 4 B = 605 MB fp32, which matches the safetensors size from the HF x-linked-size header (605,143,284 B). The text tower is released in the same checkpoint.
row.image_gmacs: ~4.4 GMACs per image. This is the standard ViT-B/32 @224 figure and I did not measure it for this checkpoint. It is in the same range as TinyCLIP-45M/32, so latency should be similar to somewhat higher, but nobody has measured it.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 76.91% IN-1k zero-shot and 70.2% IN-V2, both from the HF model card (self-reported by DatologyAI, not independently reproduced). The card compares against SigLIP2 B/32 at 74.0% and MetaCLIP B/32 at 67.7%.
row.other_zeroshot: The cls-opt card reports no retrieval numbers. The sibling DatologyAI/retr-opt-vit-b-32 (same arch, Apache-2.0, trained on ~20B samples) reports MSCOCO R@1 55.53% and Flickr30K R@1 79.7%, against SigLIP2 at 55.45% / 82.4% and MetaCLIP at 46.6% / 72.9%. Its card does not state an ImageNet number, so check it. Free-text photo search is one of the app's main uses, so the retr-opt variant may fit better than cls-opt; both are the same size.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The HF metadata says license: apache-2.0 and the README body says "License: Apache 2.0". The card adds no use-based restrictions, no non-commercial clause and no research-only wording. It is not gated. The repo has no separate LICENSE file; the files are README, open_clip_config.json, safetensors, bin and tokenizer files. The license therefore rests only on the HF metadata and the README line, which is normal for HF and still a clear grant. There is no separate code repo, because training used stock OpenCLIP 2.24.0, which is MIT. row.load_id: open_clip: create_model_and_transforms('hf-hub:DatologyAI/cls-opt-vit-b-32'). The retrieval-tuned sibling is 'hf-hub:DatologyAI/retr-opt-vit-b-32'.

row.name: ViTamin-B-LTT (DataComp-1B, 224px)

row.image_params_M: 87.5 (model-card table; also confirmed by file size: the plain ViTamin-B checkpoint is 603.95 MB fp32, which matches (87.5+63.5)M x 4 bytes). That is above the ~50M ideal and close to the ~100M ceiling, so expect roughly 88 MB at int8 against 46 MB today.

The paper explains why: LTT (Locked-Text Tuning) reuses ViTamin-L's frozen pretrained text encoder (ViTamin-L is listed with a 123.7M text tower). The text tower is released inside the same checkpoint.

The ops look convertible: depthwise and pointwise conv, LayerNorm over channels in MBConv-LN (permute or LayerNorm2d), GELU/GeGLU, standard MHSA over 196 tokens, linear projection. Nothing exotic, so it should go through litert-torch/ai-edge-torch or ONNX into TFLite, but that is untested. Practical concerns: the image tower is about 21.8 GMACs, about 5x a ViT-B/32 and several times the current TinyCLIP 45M/32, so latency on a Galaxy A54 will likely be several hundred ms per photo on CPU. It would be about 88 MB at int8 image and about 124 MB at int8 text, with a 845 MB fp32 download for the full checkpoint. The LTT text tower is 768-wide (about 124M), so the text download roughly 7x what ships today (18M). Overall the accuracy (+8 pts IN ZS over TinyCLIP) is real, but size and compute make it a weak fit. PE-Core S16 or OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 DataComp give similar or better ZS with less compute.
