verdicts.corrections:
I could not refute the row. Everything I re-checked holds.

1. **License:** the HF API reports cardData.license as "mit" and gated as False, so there are no gated-access terms. The model card has no research-only, NC or AUP clause. The repo has no separate LICENSE file. GitHub Beckschen/ViTamin LICENSE.txt is Apache-2.0.

2. **Image params, ImageNet zero-shot and other benchmarks:** the card table gives 87.5M image params and 70.8% IN-1k zero-shot. The code comment says 70.72%. Avg38 is 59.4 and retrieval is 59.4. ViTamin-B is 68.9% and ViTamin-S-LTT is 22.0M / 63.4%. All of these match.

3. **Text params:** the card's 63.4M is wrong for the LTT model. HF config.json and open_clip's ViTamin-B-LTT.json both set text width 768, 12 heads, 12 layers, ctx 77, vocab 49408 and embed_dim 768. That works out to about 123.6M. The checkpoint sizes agree: x-linked-size is 845,629,989 B for ViTamin-B-LTT against 603,953,957 B for ViTamin-B. So the row's ~123.7M is correct.

4. **Minor nit, not checked:** the row's estimate of about 6.6 GMACs for the 768-wide text tower, borrowed from ViTamin-L, is plausible but I did not check it.

5. **Note on ViTamin-S-LTT:** the card lists its text tower as 40.4M, not 63.4M, so the sibling's text size also needs its config checked.

I could not refute the row; every claim checked out against primary sources.

License:
- HF API for jienengchen/ViTamin-B-LTT returns cardData license 'mit' and gated=False.
- The repo has no LICENSE file. Its files are README, config.json, configuration_vitamin.py, model.py, timm_model.py, vitamin.py, preprocessor_config.json and pytorch_model.bin.
- The model card adds no usage restrictions.
- The GitHub repo Beckschen/ViTamin has LICENSE.txt = Apache-2.0.
- Commercial use is OK. The only caveat is the usual one: DataComp-1B images keep their original copyrights.

Numbers on the HF card table:
- ViTamin-B-LTT: image 87.5M, text listed as 63.4M, IN-1k zero-shot 70.8%, GMACs 21.8+2.9, average over 38 datasets 59.4, retrieval 59.4.
- ViTamin-B: 68.9%.
- ViTamin-S-LTT: 22.0M image / 40.4M text, 63.4%, 5.50+1.64 GMACs.
- ViTamin-L: 123.7M text, 6.6 G text GMACs.

The row's correction of the text tower is right. config.json on HF and open_clip's ViTamin-B-LTT.json both set text width 768, 12 heads, 12 layers, vocab 49408, context 77 and embed_dim 768, which works out to about 123.5–123.7M. The checkpoint sizes agree:
- ViTamin-B-LTT pytorch_model.bin is 845,629,989 bytes, close to (87.5+123.7)M x 4.
- ViTamin-B is 603,953,957 bytes, close to (87.5+63.4)M x 4.

The paper (arXiv 2404.02132, Sec. 3) confirms how LTT works: the text encoder of ViTamin-S/B is initialized from pretrained ViTamin-L and then frozen. So the card's '63.4M text' and '2.9 G text GMACs' for the LTT variant are copy-paste errors carried over from the plain ViTamin-B row.

In open_clip's pretrained.py, ViTamin-B-LTT has the tag datacomp1b and points to hf_hub jienengchen/ViTamin-B-LTT/pytorch_model.bin.

By the same logic, ViTamin-S-LTT's real text tower is probably the 768-wide ViTamin-L one (about 124M), not the 40.4M on the card. Check its config before listing it.

row.name: ViTamin-S-LTT (CLIP, DataComp-1B, Locked-Text Tuning)
row.org: Johns Hopkins University + ByteDance (Jieneng Chen et al., CVPR 2024)
row.released: 2024-04-08 (HF upload; paper arXiv 2404.02132, CVPR 2024)
row.arch: The image tower is a hybrid ViTamin-Small. It has a conv stem (3x3 s2, 64ch, LayerNorm2d+GELU) and 2 MBConv-LN stages (64ch x2, 128ch x4; depthwise 3x3, expansion 4, GELU, LayerNorm2d). A strided 3x3 conv patchifies to 14x14=196 tokens at width 384. Then come 14 transformer blocks (width 384, qkv 1152, GeGLU MLP 384->2x768->384 with an inner LayerNorm), then fc_norm, mean pooling (timm_pool '') and a linear proj 384->768. The text tower is the frozen ViTamin-L text encoder: an OpenCLIP-style causal transformer with 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, MLP 3072, ctx 77, vocab 49408, projection 768x768. The shared embedding dim is 768. Preprocessing uses OpenAI CLIP mean/std, bicubic resize, center crop 224.
row.image_params_M: 22.2 (22.17M, counted from the tensor shapes in the published pytorch_model.bin including the 384->768 head; the card and paper state 22.0-22.03M)
row.text_params_M: 123.7. I counted 123.65M from the checkpoint tensors. The card's "40.4M" is WRONG for the LTT variant: that figure is ViTamin-S's own 12/384 text tower. The S-LTT checkpoint and its config (text width 768, 12 layers, embed_dim 768) carry the ViTamin-L text encoder. The paper Appendix C confirms this ("we employ the text encoder pretrained from ViTamin-L"; 6.6 text GMACs). That makes the on-demand text download about 3x larger than TinyCLIP's 18M (about 124 MB int8, about 247 MB fp16).
row.image_gmacs: 5.50 (card/paper). Text: the card says 1.64 but the real figure for this text tower is ~6.6 GMACs (ViTamin-L text encoder, per paper Appendix C)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 63.4%, from the official HF model card table and the paper's Table 15 (LTT, DataComp-1B, 1.28B seen samples). Plain ViTamin-S without LTT: 62.2%.
row.other_zeroshot: From the official card: avg over 38 datasets 54.6, retrieval 52.9 (DataComp-eval retrieval average, i.e. Flickr/COCO combined; no separate COCO R@1 number), IN dist-shift 51.6, VTAB 54.9. Plain ViTamin-S: 53.2 / 50.0 / 51.3 / 51.7.
row.weights_license: MIT (HF repo jienengchen/ViTamin-S-LTT, license tag 'mit'; sibling repos ViTamin-S and ViTamin-L-224px are also MIT)
row.license_notes: Weights: MIT, from the HF card metadata `license: mit`. There is no separate LICENSE file in the HF repo, and the card adds no use restrictions or responsible-use clauses. Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub Beckschen/ViTamin, LICENSE.txt). That repo's README does not mention weights licensing and its checkpoint links are placeholders ("google.com"); the HF repo is the real weights host. So code and weights licenses differ, but both are permissive. The frozen text tower comes from the same authors' ViTamin-L, which is also published MIT. Training data is DataComp-1B: the metadata is CC-BY-4.0 and the images remain under their original copyrights. This is the usual web-scrape caveat, the same one TinyCLIP's LAION/YFCC data carries, and it is not a weights-license restriction. Ships with ByteDance co-authorship but no ByteDance-specific terms.
row.load_id: open_clip: create_model_and_transforms('ViTamin-S-LTT', pretrained='datacomp1b') (hf_hub 'jienengchen/ViTamin-S-LTT/pytorch_model.bin'; config ViTamin-S-LTT.json with custom_text=true). The tokenizer is the standard OpenCLIP/OpenAI BPE (the card uses the 'hf-hub:laion/CLIP-ViT-L-14-DataComp.XL-s13B-b90K' tokenizer). HF: AutoModel.from_pretrained('jienengchen/ViTamin-S-LTT', trust_remote_code=True). Vision trunk in timm: 'vitamin_small_224'.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. The HF search shows only the official repos, and a web search turned up nothing. The weights are a single fp32 pytorch_model.bin of 583.4 MB (image and text together), with no safetensors. Ops: Conv2d, depthwise 3x3, LayerNorm2d over channels (permute+LN or a manual mean/var, which can split into many small ops under the GPU delegate), exact GELU (erf; better to swap in the tanh approximation for the GPU delegate), GeGLU, and standard MHSA over 196 tokens. There are no exotic ops, so export via ai-edge-torch or ONNX should be straightforward. Compared with TinyCLIP-45M/32 (49 tokens), ViTamin-S runs 196 tokens and 5.5 GMACs, roughly 2-4x the image compute, so expect noticeably more than 73 ms on an A54 (my estimate, not measured). Image int8 size should be about 22 MB, half of today's 46 MB. Text tower int8 is about 124 MB, compared with ~18 MB today.

row.name: SigLIP ViT-B/16-i18n-256 (WebLI, multilingual)
row.org: Google Research (big_vision); PyTorch/OpenCLIP port by timm/OpenCLIP (Ross Wightman)
row.arch: Vision: ViT-B/16 (12 layers, width 768) with MAP (attention-pooling) head, 256x256 input, 256 patch tokens, no CLS. Text: 12-layer, width 768 bidirectional transformer (no causal mask, last-token pool), context 64, 250k multilingual SentencePiece vocab (Gemma/mT5-style). Shared embed dim 768. Sigmoid loss (logit_bias init -10).
row.image_params_M: 92.93 (OpenCLIP docs/model_profile.csv); consistent with ViT-B/16 ~86M + MAP head ~7M
row.text_params_M: 277.7 (OpenCLIP model_profile.csv). About 192M of this is the 250,000 x 768 token-embedding table (computed from the config); the transformer itself is about 85M. Pruning the vocabulary to English/needed languages could cut it a lot.
row.image_gmacs: 46.82 GFLOPs image tower per OpenCLIP model_profile.csv (about 23.4 GMACs). Text tower 11.02 GFLOPs. Total 57.84 GFLOPs. This is about 4-5x TinyCLIP-45M/32 compute (patch 16 at 256px means 256 tokens vs 49).
row.in1k_zeroshot: 75.13% (OpenCLIP docs/openclip_results.csv, English prompts, CLIP_benchmark). Average over 38 datasets: 60.68%. ImageNet-v2 68.1%, ImageNet-R 89.2%, ObjectNet 59.8%.

The closest is litert-community/SigLIP2-base-patch16-224: a 185 MB fp16 LiteRT graph whose card says it runs fully on the GPU delegate with no CPU fallback. The architecture is similar (ViT-B + MAP head), so the GPU delegate should be workable here too. row.image_params_M: 94.55M total. I summed the vision_model.* tensors in the model.safetensors header myself. That includes a 7.09M MAP head, so the backbone without the head is about 87.5M. row.text_params_M: 282.30M. I summed the text_model.* tensors in the safetensors header myself. Of that, 196.6M is the 256000x768 token-embedding table, the transformer is about 85.7M, and the head is 0.59M. The HF API gives 376,856,066 params for the full model, which matches 94.55 + 282.30.
row.image_gmacs: About 5.75 GMACs. I computed this from the architecture myself; no source states it. Per token per layer, the QKV/out projections plus MLP are about 7.08M MACs, times 64 tokens times 12 layers = 5.44G. Attention matmuls add about 0.08G, the patch embed about 0.15G and the MAP head about 0.08G. For reference, timm lists ViT-B/32@224 (49 tokens) at 4.41 GMACs.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 74.0%. Source: paper arXiv 2502.14786 Table 1 (B/32, 256px, seq len 64). The same number appears in the big_vision README_siglip2 checkpoint table. Same row: IN-v2 66.9, ReaL 81.4, ObjectNet 66.1. In that table, OpenCLIP B/32@256 (DataComp) gets 72.8 for comparison.
row.other_zeroshot: From paper Table 1 and the big_vision README: COCO T->I R@1 47.2 and I->T R@1 63.7; Flickr T->I 75.5 and I->T 89.3; XM3600 (multilingual, 36 langs) T->I 38.3 and I->T 49.0; 10-shot IN 66.6. row.license_notes:
Every source I checked says Apache-2.0, and none adds a use restriction:
- The HF model card for google/siglip2-base-patch32-256 has `license: apache-2.0` in its metadata. The card has no acceptable-use policy, no gating and no NC clause.
- The timm/ViT-B-32-SigLIP2-256 (open_clip) and timm/vit_base_patch32_siglip_256.v2_webli repos are both `license: apache-2.0`.
- The keras/siglip2_base_patch32_256 card says weights and code are both Apache 2.
- The big_vision repo LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0. Its README footer says "All software is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0" and "All other materials are licensed under ... CC-BY". The original .npz checkpoints are hosted on GCS from that repo.
- I found no place where the weights license differs from the code license.

Caveats:
- WebLI is a proprietary Google dataset. That limits reproducibility, but nothing I found imposes a downstream restriction on the weights.
- The tokenizer is Gemma's 256k SentencePiece. It ships inside the Apache-2.0 SigLIP2 repo, and the repo does not reference the Gemma Terms of Use.
- The README says "not an official Google product" and the weights come AS IS (standard Apache disclaimer).
- The paper's CC BY 4.0 covers only the paper text.

row.export_notes:
ONNX already exists. onnx-community/siglip2-base-patch32-256-ONNX ships separate vision_model and text_model graphs:
- Vision: fp32 378.5 MB, fp16 189.4 MB, int8/uint8 95.9 MB, q4 69.9 MB, q4f16 58.0 MB.
- Text: fp32 1129.5 MB, fp16 564.9 MB, int8 283.4 MB, q4f16 442.8 MB.

So int8 roughly doubles the image-tower download (about 96 MB vs the current 46 MB). The text tower is about 283 MB at int8, about 6x heavier than TinyCLIP's 18M text tower, mostly because of the 256k-vocab embedding table. Trimming the vocab or keeping only the embedding rows needed on device would be a custom step.

Other exports:
- Immich's immich-app/ViT-B-32-SigLIP2-256__webli has an open_clip ONNX (visual 378 MB fp32) plus RKNN builds for RK3566/68/76/88 NPUs.
- Synaptics/siglip2-base-patch32-256-torq is a compiled build for Synaptics Torq NPUs (apache-2.0).

I found no TFLite/LiteRT export of the B/32-256 variant and no Android latency report for it. The closest is litert-community/SigLIP2-base-patch16-224 (apache-2.0, B/16-224 image tower, fp16 .tflite 185 MB):
- It runs fully on the LiteRT GPU delegate (ML Drift, 809/809 nodes, no Flex ops).
- That needed rewrites: decomposed q/k/v head-split and an overflow-safe fp16 LayerNorm. A naive conversion of the MAP-head and attention ops may fall back to CPU or overflow in fp16.
- Its card reports about 60 ms/img steady-state on a Pixel 8a GPU and 13.7 ms p50 on a Galaxy S26 GPU.

B/32-256 has 64 tokens vs 196 for B/16-224, so it should be noticeably cheaper than those figures, but still about 1.5x TinyCLIP-45M/32's MACs. Expect it slower than the current 73 ms on the A54 unless measured otherwise; this estimate is unmeasured.

Qualcomm AI Hub (qualcomm/SigLIP2, apache-2.0) profiles the B/16-224 variant only.

row.arch:
- Image tower: EVA-02 ViT-B/16 at 224px. 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads (head_width 64), giving 196 patch tokens + CLS = 197 tokens.
  - 2D RoPE on q/k (pt_hw_seq_len 16, intp_freq). The patch embedding was interpolated from 14 to 16.
  - SwiGLU MLP with mlp_ratio 2.6667 (hidden 2048) and sub-LayerNorm inside the MLP (subln).
  - Token pooling, then a projection to a 512-d shared embedding.
- Text tower: standard CLIP transformer. 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, context 77, vocab 49408 (OpenAI BPE). Initialized from OpenAI CLIP B/16.
- Training: 8B samples seen, batch 131K.
row.image_gmacs: ~17.6 GMACs. OpenCLIP model_profile.csv lists image_gflops 35.13; I halved it to get MACs. My own estimate (about 1.45 GMAC/block x 12 + patch embed) agrees. That is about 4.4x TinyCLIP-45M/32's image compute. Text tower: 5.96 GFLOPs (~3.0 GMACs) per 77-token query.

row.export_notes:
- No existing ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or LiteRT export found. On HF there are only timm/open_clip PyTorch/safetensors re-hosts; a web search also found no mobile latency report.
- Size: fp16 checkpoint for both towers is 299 MB. Estimated int8 sizes: image tower about 86-90 MB (vs 46 MB today), text tower about 63 MB. That is about 1.9x the current image download, so it is near the ~100M ceiling.
- Compute: about 17.6 GMACs per image at 197 tokens vs about 4.4 GMACs for TinyCLIP-45M/32. Expect several times the current ~73 ms/photo on an A54. That latency is my estimate, not a measurement.
- TFLite risks:
  - The timm Eva block's 2D RoPE (apply_rot_embed_cat) uses interleaved rotate-half: x[...,::2] / x[...,1::2] strided slices, a stack/reshape, and sin/cos multiplies. This lowers to STRIDED_SLICE, PACK and RESHAPE. Converters handle it, but it adds ops and it is a likely GPU-delegate partition point; check the delegate coverage.
  - Precompute RoPE as constants at a fixed 224 input, so no dynamic shape work runs on the graph.
  - SwiGLU (SiLU + MUL) and the extra sub-LN are fine.
  - The xattn/fusedLN flags in the EVA config only matter for training (xformers/apex). Export through the timm/open_clip implementation, not the EVA repo's.
- Suggested path: ai-edge-torch (litert-torch) or ONNX, then TFLite on the timm 'eva02_base_patch16_clip_224' module.
- The text tower is a plain CLIP text transformer, so it exports like the current one.

row.name: SigLIP 2 ViT-B/16 (224 / 256 / NaFlex)
row.arch: Same ViT-B/16 SigLIP dual encoder in all three variants. Image tower: ViT-B/16 (width 768, 12 layers, 12 heads, MLP 3072). It has no CLS token and uses a MAP attention-pool head (7.09M params), with a 768-d output. The token count is 196 at 224px, 256 at 256px, and variable for NaFlex (64 to 1024, native aspect ratio). Text tower: a 12-layer, 768-wide transformer using the multilingual Gemma tokenizer (256k vocab), lowercased text and 64 tokens max. Trained with the sigmoid loss plus decoder/self-distillation/masked-prediction objectives (SigLIP 2 recipe) on WebLI.
row.image_params_M: 92.88M at 224 and 92.93M at 256. I counted these from the tensor shapes in the HF model.safetensors headers: vision embeddings 0.74M (0.79M at 256), encoder 85.05M, MAP head 7.09M, post-LN 0.002M. timm lists 92.9M.
row.text_params_M: 282.30M, counted from the safetensors header. The token embedding table alone is 196.66M (256,000 x 768) and the transformer is 85.05M, plus the head (0.59M) and final LN. The checkpoint holds 375.19M params in total (375.23M at 256/NaFlex), which matches the HF "0.4B" figure. So about 70% of the text tower is the vocab embedding table. Most of it could be cut by trimming the vocab to English/used tokens, but that would be custom engineering, not anything released.
row.image_gmacs: About 17.5 GMACs at 224 and about 23.1 GMACs at 256. I computed these by hand: 12 x (N*12*768^2 + 2*N^2*768) plus the patch embedding, with N=196 or 256. They are not from a primary source. That is roughly 4.5-5x the compute of TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224. For reference, the OpenCLIP csv gives 46.44 GFLOPs for image+text combined for SigLIP v1 ViT-B-16 at 224.
row.resolution: 224 (196 tokens), 256 (256 tokens), and NaFlex (variable sequence length 64 to 1024, native aspect ratio; a fixed-shape export needs one chosen sequence length). 384 and 512 B/16 variants also exist.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 78.2% at 224 and 79.1% at 256 (SigLIP 2 paper, arXiv 2502.14786, Table 1). NaFlex B/16: 71.2% at seq 64, 76.2% at seq 144, 78.5% at seq 256 (paper, Appendix Table 7). For comparison, SigLIP v1 B/16 scores 76.2% at 224. The OpenCLIP results csv has no SigLIP2 rows (checked).
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 1, B/16 at 224: IN-v2 71.4, ReaL 84.8, ObjectNet 73.6, COCO T->I 52.1 / I->T 68.9 R@1, Flickr T->I 80.7 / I->T 93.0. At 256: IN-v2 72.5, ReaL 85.4, ObjectNet 74.5, COCO 53.2 / 69.7, Flickr 81.7 / 94.4. NaFlex at seq 256: COCO 51.1 / 67.3. The model is multilingual (Gemma tokenizer).

row.export_notes:
**Official LiteRT image tower (litert-community, updated 2026-09-08)**
- One file, siglip2_base_224_fp16.tflite (185 MB, FP16 only, no int8). There is no text tower; the card says to precompute label embeddings with the open_clip text tower.
- I/O: input [1,3,224,224] NCHW in [-1,1]; output [1,768] L2-normalized.
- Graph rewrites, reported as weights-exact (corr about 1.0): the fused qkv is split into separate q/k/v with 4-D attention; MAP-pool single-query attention becomes broadcast-mul plus reduce-sum; LayerNorm is made overflow-safe for fp16 by scaling the input by 1/32 before squaring. convert_siglip2.py is included.
- **Latency (as reported on the card)**
  - Galaxy S26, LiteRT 2.2 CompiledModel: 13.7 ms p50 on GPU (ML Drift, all 809 nodes on GPU) and 6.94 ms on NPU (Hexagon v81). The first NPU compile takes about 6.5 s.
  - Pixel 8a (Mali-G615): about 60 ms steady-state.
- **Important for this app:** the card's Pixel 8a classic TFLite benchmark_model rows show only 44 of 809 nodes delegated by the GPU Delegate V2 (OpenCL), giving 963.6 ms. XNNPACK CPU with 4 threads takes 312.9 ms. The card warns that the CompiledModel and classic-delegate numbers are not comparable. So the app's current classic GPU delegate plus XNNPACK path would probably be slow unless it moves to the LiteRT CompiledModel API.

**Qualcomm AI Hub (qualcomm/SigLIP2, v0.65.0)**
- Exports for both towers: ONNX float/w8a16, QNN_DLC float/w8a16, TFLite float.
- Sizes: image encoder 352 MB float / 92.8 MB w8a16; text encoder 1.05 GB float / 461 MB w8a16.
- NPU latency for the image encoder is 2.1-3.3 ms on 8 Elite Gen 5 and 3.7 ms w8a16 on 8 Gen 3. The text encoder takes 1.2-2.4 ms.
- The AI Hub web pages reportedly say the model is "not supported" on some chipsets.

**No numbers for the Galaxy A54 (Exynos 1380 / Mali-G68).** Expected sizes: image tower int8 about 93 MB, about 2x the current 46 MB. Text tower fp16 about 565 MB, int8 about 282 MB, mostly the 256k-vocab embedding table, which is a large on-demand download unless the vocab is pruned.

row.name: SigLIP (v1) ViT-B/16 WebLI-en (224 / 256 / 384 / 512)
row.arch: Image tower: ViT-B/16 (12 layers, width 768, MLP 3072, 12 heads) with a MAP (attention-pooling) head and no CLS token; 196 tokens at 224, 256 at 256, 576 at 384, 1024 at 512; embedding dim 768. Text tower is released: it is in the HF safetensors (203.16M params total, 812.7 MB fp32) and in the open_clip weights.

Existing exports:
- Xenova/siglip-base-patch16-224 (transformers.js ONNX, split towers): vision_model.onnx 372 MB fp32, vision_model_fp16 186 MB, vision_model_int8 94.1 MB, vision q4 63 MB / bnb4 57.5 MB; text_model_int8 111 MB, text_model_fp16 221 MB, text q4f16 98.7 MB.
- h9899/siglip-base-patch16-224-coreml (Apache-2.0): CoreML vision int8 weights ~92.6 MB, text int8 ~110.7 MB.
- No official LiteRT/TFLite export of SigLIP v1 B/16 was found.

Same-architecture SigLIP 2 B/16-224 exports do exist: litert-community/SigLIP2-base-patch16-224 and mlboydaisuke/SigLIP2-base-patch16-224-LiteRT (FP16 image encoder ~185 MB, card says it runs fully on the LiteRT GPU accelerator with no CPU fallback), plus qualcomm/SigLIP2 (~5.9 ms on the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 NPU). This suggests v1 B/16 will also convert cleanly (same ViT + MAP head, LayerNorm, GELU-tanh; the MAP head is a standard MHA with a learned query).

I found no mobile CPU/GPU latency report for v1 B/16. My rough expectation for the Galaxy A54 at 224 is ~4-5x TinyCLIP-45M/32 compute (~17.6 vs ~3.5-4 GMACs), so a few hundred ms per photo on XNNPACK CPU. That is unmeasured. The 384 variant is ~3x worse again.

Download cost: int8 image tower ~93 MB (vs 46 MB today), int8 text ~110 MB, mostly the 24.6M-param 32k-vocab embedding table. The text embeddings are 768-d, so the ~3,600 concept vectors must be recomputed.

Bottom line: v1 is strictly dominated by SigLIP 2 B/16 (same size, Apache-2.0, +2 IN ZS, +5 COCO T->I). Only pick v1 if SigLIP 2's Gemma tokenizer (256k vocab) makes its text tower too big.

row.arch: ViT-B/32 image tower: 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, patch 32, which gives 49 patch tokens plus CLS = 50 tokens at 224px. The text tower is a 12-layer transformer (width 512, 8 heads, causal mask, 77 tokens, BPE vocab 49,408). Shared embedding is 512-d.

row.export_notes: (1) mlboydaisuke/clip-vit-b32-litert (MIT tag). Image encoder only (clip_image_encoder.tflite, NCHW 1x3x224x224 in, L2-normalized 512-d out), made with litert-torch. It runs about 40 ms on a Pixel 8a with all 691/691 ops on the OpenCL/ML Drift GPU delegate. The stock conversion fails on GPU: torch MultiheadAttention lowers to 5D RESHAPE, and the GPU supports at most 4D. The fix is a manual 4D attention rewrite (explicit matmul and softmax) with GELU replaced by x*sigmoid(1.702x). Precision and size are not stated. No text tower; it ships only 96 precomputed label embeddings. (2) Arm/clip-vit-base-patch32-int8-xnnpack-executorch (MIT tag). One .pte file with encode_image and encode_text. The vision tower uses dynamic int8 (per-channel weights). The text tower stays FP32 because PT2E could not capture the causal mask. The file is 327 MB. p50 is 95.5 ms on a single-threaded Raspberry Pi 5 A76 (vs 298 ms FP32). CIFAR-100 top-1 is 61.6% vs 60.7% FP32. (3) Software Mansion's react-native-executorch also ships CLIP ViT-B/32 image embeddings (hint, not re-verified). Compared with the current TinyCLIP-45M: about 2x the image params (int8 image tower roughly 88 MB vs 46 MB) and a larger text tower (63M vs 18M), for only about +0.6 points of IN-1k zero-shot (63.3 vs 62.7). OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 DataComp-XL has the same architecture and size at 72.7%, and the same mobile exports apply to it. That makes OpenAI B/32 dominated on accuracy at equal cost.

The image tower is standard OpenAI B/32, about 88 MB int8, about 2x the current 46 MB, and widely exported to TFLite/ONNX/CoreML. I found no mobile latency report for this pair. row.license_notes:
The only license is the MIT LICENSE in github.com/openai/CLIP. It covers "software and associated documentation files" and does not explicitly name the weights. The weights host (openaipublic Azure blob) and the HF repo openai/clip-vit-base-patch16 have no license file or tag. The model card (model-card.md, also on the HF page) adds non-binding but explicit restrictions on scope:
- "Any deployed use case of the model - whether commercial or not - is currently out of scope."
- Surveillance and facial recognition are "always out-of-scope".
- Use should be limited to English.
- The data statement says "We do not intend for this dataset to be used as the basis for any commercial or deployed model".
The training data (WIT-400M) was never released or itemized.

In practice, commercial use is widespread. Qualcomm AI Hub tags it license_type: mit, and Stable Diffusion etc. ship OpenAI CLIP weights. But there is no explicit weights grant, and the model card discourages deployment, so I marked this "unclear" (not a clean yes). row.export_notes:
Both towers are released. Qualcomm AI Hub (quic/ai-hub-models, src/qai_hub_models/models/openai_clip) exports one combined graph: forward(image, text) returns L2-normalized image and text features. It is not split into separate towers; to compute image embeddings alone you would need your own split export. Runtimes are TFLite, QNN-DLC and ONNX, in float and w8a16. There is no int8 TFLite asset.

perf.yaml latencies, all on NPU (combined image + text graph, float TFLite):

| Device | Latency |
|---|---|
| Galaxy S22 (8 Gen 1) | 36.4 ms |
| Galaxy S24 | 21.1 ms |
| Galaxy S25 | 17.1 ms |
| Galaxy S26 | 12.8 ms |
| Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 QRD (w8a16, QNN) | 37.0 ms |

These are Hexagon NPU numbers and say nothing about the Exynos A54 GPU delegate or XNNPACK. The aihub.qualcomm.com page shows a contradictory notice, "This model is currently not supported on any All Models chipset", next to a supported-chipset list.

Expected on the A54: about 2x the FLOPs of B/32 and about 4x TinyCLIP-45M/32 (196 vs 49 tokens). A plain ViT has no exotic ops; standard LayerNorm, GELU and MHA lower fine to the TFLite GPU delegate. Qualcomm patches the packed in-projection (patched_in_projection_packed) for export.

Verdict: OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 DataComp-XL (MIT) beats it on accuracy, size and compute. It would not be an upgrade.

row.name: nomic-embed-vision-v1.5 + nomic-embed-text-v1.5
row.arch: Image tower: an EVA02-style ViT-B/16 (initialized from EVA02 ViT-B/16 per the tech report). 12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, SwiGLU MLP (2048), rotary position embeddings, multi-head attention pooling, CLS output. At 224px with patch 16 it sees 196 patches plus CLS, so 197 tokens. The embedding is 768-d. Text tower: nomic_bert, a BERT-base-sized model (12 layers, 768 wide, SwiGLU 3072, rotary embeddings, 8192 context, Matryoshka 768/512/256/128/64). It is LiT-style: the text tower stayed frozen and the vision tower was aligned to it. Both towers need trust_remote_code (custom nomic_bert code from nomic-ai/nomic-bert-2048). Text queries must start with the "search_query: " prefix.

Earlier revisions were CC-BY-NC-4.0, so pin a revision on or after 351ebb2. The weight files were not changed in that commit; ONNX files have been there since 2024-06-05. row.export_notes: Official ONNX exports are on HF in onnx/, with Transformers.js support. Vision: model.onnx fp32 374 MB, fp16 187 MB, int8/quantized/uint8 96.7 MB, q4 62.0 MB, bnb4 56.2 MB. Text: fp32 547 MB, fp16 274 MB, int8 137 MB, q4 165 MB, q4f16 111 MB, bnb4 158 MB. I found no TFLite/LiteRT or CoreML export and no published mobile latency for this model; a web search turned up nothing. For LiteRT, convert ONNX with onnx2tf, or PyTorch with ai-edge-torch. Expected GPU-delegate issues: the rotary embeddings (slice, concat, sin/cos ops), the attention-pooling head, and custom nomic_bert code paths such as fused/flash-attention flags in the config, which must be off for export. Rough size and speed against what ships now (TinyCLIP-45M/32): about 2x the params and about 97 MB int8 versus 46 MB. ViT-B/16 at 224 is about 4x the MACs, so expect roughly 250-300 ms per photo on an A54 on CPU, extrapolated and not measured. The text tower (137M, ~137 MB int8) is much bigger than TinyCLIP's 18M text tower. The vision card does not say whether Matryoshka truncation of the shared space keeps image-text alignment; unclear.

row.name: FG-CLIP base (v1), qihoo360/fg-clip-base
row.arch: The vision tower is a standard CLIP ViT-B/16 (12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, MLP 3072, patch 16, 224px, 196 patch tokens plus CLS), projecting to 512-d. The text tower is a CLIP text transformer (12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, vocab 49,408). The config lists 77 positions, but the custom modeling_clip.py extends text positions to 248 for long captions (positions up to 20 keep their original values, and later ones are interpolated by a factor of 4). The model adds an extra text_filip_projection Linear(512,512) and two scalar logit scales that are only used for training. Loading requires trust_remote_code. It is registered unusually, under AutoModelForCausalLM.
row.image_params_M: About 86M (vision tower plus projection). This is computed from config.json: it is the standard ViT-B/16 CLIP visual geometry, which is about 86.2M in OpenCLIP's ViT-B-16 accounting. The card does not state it separately.
row.text_params_M: About 64M (CLIP text transformer about 63.4M, plus text_projection and the extra 512x512 FILIP projection, about 0.26M). This is computed from config.json. The total is consistent: the HF safetensors metadata gives 150,136,832 params.
row.image_gmacs: About 17.5 GMACs at 224px. This is the standard ViT-B/16 figure (OpenCLIP profile about 17.6), and I did not measure it myself. That is roughly 4-5x TinyCLIP-45M/32.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 69.0% top-1 (ImageNet-v2 61.8%), from the FG-CLIP paper (arXiv 2505.05071, Table 4, ViT-B/16 row). For comparison, the same table gives OpenAI CLIP B/16 68.4% and EVA-CLIP B/16 74.7%. The HF card itself reports no IN-1k number.
row.other_zeroshot: From paper Table 4 (ViT-B/16, likely R@1): MSCOCO I2T 64.1, T2I 45.4; Flickr30k I2T 90.7, T2I 76.4. The model's strengths are long-caption retrieval (up to 248 tokens) and fine-grained/region tasks.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 (HF license tag on qihoo360/fg-clip-base, and the GitHub repo 360CVGroup/FG-CLIP LICENSE is also Apache-2.0)
row.license_notes: The weights (HF tag) and the code (GitHub repo) are both Apache-2.0, with no separate weights license and no added use restrictions in the card. The one caveat is a card disclaimer that the project "utilizes certain datasets and checkpoints that are subject to their respective original licenses." The base checkpoint is OpenAI CLIP (MIT license), but the OpenAI CLIP model card says deployed use cases, commercial or not, are "out of scope". That is guidance, not a license term. The paper does not name the exact CLIP checkpoint, but the architecture matches OpenAI ViT-B/16. Training data: stage 1 used about 1.6B LAION-2B images recaptioned with CogVLM2-19B; stage 2 used FineHARD (12M GRIT-based images, 40M boxes, 10M hard negatives). It is unclear whether CogVLM2's license or the LAION/GRIT image licenses carry over to the weights. That risk is the same as for any LAION-trained CLIP. Overall, commercial use is permitted on paper, with the usual data-provenance caveats.
row.load_id: HF: qihoo360/fg-clip-base (transformers, trust_remote_code=True, loaded via AutoModelForCausalLM; it exposes get_image_features / get_text_features(walk_short_pos=True for 77-token short text)). It is not in open_clip or timm.
row.released: Uploaded to HF 2025-05-08/09 (last modified 2025-10-09). Paper arXiv 2505.05071, ICML 2025. Successor FG-CLIP 2 (base/large/so400m) released 2025-10-14.
row.export_notes: I found no existing ONNX, TFLite or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report, in the repo, the HF card or a web search. The fp32 safetensors file is 600.6 MB for both towers. Expect about 87 MB for an int8 image tower, roughly 2x TinyCLIP's 46 MB, and about 4-5x the compute (ViT-B/16 vs ViT-B/32), so expect several hundred ms per photo on an A54-class GPU or CPU. This is an estimate, not measured. The ops are plain ViT and CLIP-text ops (LayerNorm, QuickGELU, softmax attention), so they are GPU-delegate friendly. The custom remote code (modeling_clip.py with the walk_short_pos position handling) would need to be traced and frozen to short-text mode, or the standard HF CLIPModel used after remapping weights. Verdict: weak fit. The image tower is about 86M, near the ceiling, and its IN-1k zero-shot score (69.0) is below OpenCLIP B/32 DataComp-XL (72.7) and PE-Core S16-384 (72.7), which are cheaper or comparable. Its advantage is only long, fine-grained text queries.

row.name: UForm3 image-text-multilingual-base
row.released: HF repo created around 2024-04 (repo id 662347e0, which dates to April 2024). Last commit 2024-12-19. It is the v3 repackaging of uform-vl-multilingual-v2.
row.arch: Image tower: ViT-B/16, 224px, 12 layers, dim 768, CLS pooling, 196 patch tokens + CLS. Text tower: 12-layer BERT-style, dim 384, XLM-R-size vocab of 250,037, max 50 tokens, mean pooling. Shared embedding is 256-d. Blocks 8 to 11 of the text tower are cross-attention 'multimodal' layers. The v3 code (torch_encoders.py forward_features) SKIPS them for embeddings, so text embeddings come from 8 unimodal layers. Calling it a dual encoder is correct.
row.image_params_M: 86.0, computed from the image_encoder.safetensors header (BF16 tensors, 86,012,928 params). That is about 2x TinyCLIP-45M.
row.text_params_M: 120.1 stored, from the text_encoder.safetensors header (120,090,242). About 110.3 are used for retrieval embeddings, after removing blocks 8 to 11 (9.47M), the context projection (0.3M) and the matching head. 96.0M of that is the 250k x 384 word-embedding table. The transformer itself is only about 14M, so vocab pruning could shrink it a lot. Total 206M, matching the README.
row.image_gmacs: About 17.6 GMACs. This is standard ViT-B/16 @224 (timm vit_base_patch16_224). It is inferred from the architecture, not reported by Unum.
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported. There is no ImageNet zero-shot number on the HF card, in the GitHub README or in BENCHMARKS.md. The older PyPI description says the models were trained on about 4M samples and 'may not be suited for zero-shot classification'. Expect it to be well below TinyCLIP's 62.7%.
row.other_zeroshot: HF card: Zero-shot Flickr R@1/5/10 = 0.558/0.813/0.874. MS-COCO R@1/5/10 = 0.401/0.680/0.781, but the COCO train split was in the training data. The card says 'the multimodal part was used' for these evals, which suggests cross-attention reranking, not pure dual-encoder scores, and the v3 code no longer exposes that path. XTD-10 R@10: EN 96.1, DE 93.5, ES 95.7, etc. COCO-SM mean text-to-image R@1 is 31.8 vs 26.5 for OpenCLIP xlm-roberta-base-ViT-B-32, and English is on par (37.7 vs 37.8). These multilingual tables are the same ones BENCHMARKS.md gives for uform-vl-multilingual-v2. Its strength is retrieval in 21 languages, not zero-shot tagging.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The license is Apache-2.0 in three places: the HF model card YAML (license: apache-2.0, plus the HF API tag license:apache-2.0), the GitHub repo LICENSE file (unum-cloud/uform, Apache License 2.0, per the GitHub API), and the weights host. YFCC/Flickr images carry mixed CC licenses, including some NC. This is a common provenance caveat that does not change the weights license. The HF repo ships exports already:

row.org: LAMDA Lab, Nanjing University (Shu-Hao Zhang, Shao-Qun Zhang et al.)
row.arch: Standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 dual encoder (patch 16, 224px gives 196+1 tokens; 12-layer text transformer, width 512). row.image_params_M: ~86M (computed: the HF safetensors total is 149.62M, and the standard ViT-B/16 CLIP split gives ~86M image and ~63M text). That is over the 50M target but within the 100M ceiling. These are full-size ternary-valued weights, not a small architecture.

row.image_gmacs: ~17.5 GMACs (standard ViT-B/16 at 224px; ternary weights do not reduce MACs on standard kernels)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 53.28% for TernaryCLIP Q-ALL (the released ternary model, per the HF card) and 56.76% for the Q-FFN variant, from paper Table 7 (arXiv 2510.21879 HTML). TFLite/LiteRT has no ternary or 2-bit kernels, so a TFLite export would hold ternary values as int8 (~86 MB image tower at int8, larger than the current 46 MB) and keep full ViT-B/16 compute. That compute is likely several times slower than TinyCLIP-45M/32 on an A54, because the patch-16 token count is ~4x that of patch-32. The only latency report is 106.75 ms total on an Apple M4 Pro CPU (GGML TQ1_0, mean of 1000 runs); there is no phone measurement. row.name: FG-CLIP 2 base (fg-clip2-base, ViT-B/16 NaFlex)
row.arch: A SigLIP2-style dual encoder whose weights start from SigLIP 2 B/16 (paper). The vision side is a ViT-B/16 NaFlex: 12 layers, width 768, MLP 3072, 12 heads, patch 16 (embedded as a 768x768 linear layer over flattened patches), a 256-entry (16x16) learned position embedding that is resized to match the patch grid, and a MAP attention-pool head. The token count is variable through max_num_patches, which defaults to 256 in preprocessor_config, so about a 256x256 image. The README demos use 128 to 1024 patches, and dense features use 16384. The text side is 12 layers, width 768, with the Gemma 256k vocabulary. It uses max_length 64 for short captions and has separate 196-token long-caption position embeddings. The output embedding is 768-d. The checkpoint also contains extra heads for long text, box text and dense features, about 8.5M params that plain retrieval does not need.
row.image_params_M: 92.93M, which I computed from the model.safetensors header: vision embeddings 0.79M + encoder 85.05M + MAP head 7.09M + post-LN. The model card states no per-tower count. Int8 would be about 93 MB and fp16 about 186 MB, so roughly twice the current 46 MB TinyCLIP image tower.
row.text_params_M: 282.6M, computed from the safetensors header. 197.0M of it is the embedding table (the 256000x768 token table plus position embeddings), the encoder is 85.05M and the head is 0.59M. The longtext_head (0.59M) is used only for long captions. The total checkpoint is 383.8M (F32), which matches the HF '0.4B' figure and the 384M in the hint.
row.image_gmacs: About 23 GMACs at 256 patches. I estimated this from the config and it is not reported anywhere: about 21.7 GMACs for the linear layers plus about 1.2 GMACs for attention. That is about 5-6x a ViT-B/32 at 224px.
row.resolution: NaFlex with a variable patch budget. The default is max_num_patches=256 (about 256x256 equivalent, aspect ratio preserved). The paper trains with {128,256,576,784,1024} patches and does not state the evaluation resolution.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 79.5% top-1 (IN-v2 72.2%), from the FG-CLIP 2 paper (arXiv 2510.10921 v3, Table 4, ViT-B/16). SigLIP 2 B/16 scores 81.2% in the same table, so this model is about 1.7 points below its own SigLIP 2 base. The model card has no ImageNet number, and the evaluation patch budget is not stated.
row.other_zeroshot: From paper Table 4 (ViT-B/16, English): COCO I->T 72.1 / T->I 54.5 and Flickr30k I->T 94.1 / T->I 81.9. SigLIP 2 B/16 scores 71.2/55.2 and 92.6/78.0. Box classification (Table 2): COCO80 74.9 / LVIS 47.3 / BoxClass-CN 60.7, versus SigLIP 2 at 53.4/20.6/57.9. The model is strong on Chinese and fine-grained / long-caption benchmarks.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 (HF license tag and README). The GitHub repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0.
row.license_notes: The HF card (license: apache-2.0) and the GitHub repo 360CVGroup/FG-CLIP (LICENSE = Apache License 2.0) both say Apache-2.0. However, the README License section says, in substance, that the project uses datasets and checkpoints that keep their own original licenses and that users must comply with those terms. It then says the project's own content is Apache-2.0. The README links ./LICENSE, but the HF repo has no LICENSE file: fetching it returns 'Entry not found'. The card adds no explicit commercial or field-of-use restriction. The initialization checkpoint is SigLIP 2, which is Apache-2.0, so that part is fine. The ambiguity comes from the training data: Stage I uses LAION-2B (recaptioned), Wukong 100M, Zero 250M and a 500M in-house Chinese set, and Stage II uses FineHARD and FineRegion-CN. I did not verify the Wukong and Zero dataset terms; they are commonly research-oriented. Whether those data terms carry over to the weights is not stated anywhere. In short, the weights are labeled Apache-2.0 with no stated use restriction, but the authors' blanket clause about dataset and checkpoint licenses makes this weaker than a clean Apache release. Treat it as 'probably OK, get a legal read' rather than 'clean'. A separate practical note: loading needs trust_remote_code (modeling_fgclip2.py, Apache per the repo).
row.load_id: HF: qihoo360/fg-clip2-base (AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True); get_image_features / get_text_features). The processor is Siglip2Processor with image mean/std 0.5. This is not in open_clip or timm.
row.export_notes:
No TFLite/LiteRT export and no mobile latency report were found. Third-party exports exist on HF:
(a) zihuv/fg-clip2-base-onnx (2026-04): visual.onnx 371 MB and text.onnx 343 MB fp32. The 393 MB token-embedding table is split out as a .bin.
(b) pigzhou/fg-clip2-base-immich (2026-09): an Immich ONNX export with visual 374 MB and textual 1.13 GB.
(c) Kn90688/kb-fgclip2-base-coreml (2026-10): CoreML image 185 MB (fp16) and text short 369 MB with int8 embedding.
These show the towers export cleanly to ONNX/CoreML. For the GPU delegate, the risks are the NaFlex path's variable patch count, its bilinear position-embedding resize and its attention masks; fix the patch budget (e.g. 16x16=256) and bake the position embeddings to get a static graph. The MAP head uses nn.MultiheadAttention, which normally exports fine. The text tower is heavy for on-demand download: about 283 MB int8, mostly the 256k-vocab embedding table. The int8 image tower is about 93 MB, about 2x TinyCLIP's size. Compute is about 23 GMACs/image, so expect several times TinyCLIP's 73 ms on an A54 (not measured).

row.name: SLIP ViT-S/16 (YFCC15M, 100 ep)
row.arch: Image tower: ViT-S/16 in the MoCo v3 variant (timm vit_small_mocov3_patch16_224, width 384, 12 layers, 12 heads instead of 6), 196 patch tokens + CLS at 224px, linear projection 384->512. Text tower: OpenAI CLIP-style causal transformer (width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, context 77, vocab 49408, BPE). Shared embedding dim 512. SLIP also adds a SimCLR SSL MLP head on the image side, which is used only during training.
row.image_params_M: ~22M, computed from models.py (ViT-S/16 ~21.7M + 384x512 projection 0.2M). Params are not stated in the README.
row.text_params_M: ~63M, computed from models.py (12 x 512-wide blocks ~37.8M + token embedding 49408x512 ~25.3M + 512x512 projection). This is the same size as the OpenAI CLIP B text tower, so it is roughly 3.5x larger than TinyCLIP's 18M text tower.
row.image_gmacs: ~4.6 GMACs at 224px (standard ViT-S/16 figure; not reported by SLIP)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 39.5% for SLIP ViT-S/16 trained 100 epochs on YFCC15M (GitHub README table). Other checkpoints: 50 ep 39.3%, 25 ep 38.3%, and the CLIP-only ViT-S baseline 32.7%. For comparison, the current TinyCLIP-45M/32 scores 62.7%, so this is about 23 points worse.
row.other_zeroshot: The paper (arXiv 2112.12750) reports zero-shot results on its downstream benchmark suite and linear-probe accuracy (68.3% IN-1k for this checkpoint), plus 80.7% after fine-tuning. Neither the README nor the paper gives a headline COCO/Flickr retrieval number for ViT-S.
row.weights_license: MIT, by inheritance: the repo LICENSE is MIT ("Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates") and the README says "This project is under the MIT license." The weights have no separate license file.
row.license_notes: The code is MIT (LICENSE file plus README statement). The weights are hosted on dl.fbaipublicfiles.com (slip_small_100ep.pt) with no separate license or model card, so the only license that covers them is the repo's MIT; there is no Hugging Face card and no added use restrictions. Data caveat: the training set, YFCC15M, is a subset of YFCC100M, whose Flickr images carry mixed Creative Commons licenses, some NC/ND. MIT on the weights is still the operative license, but anyone strict about provenance may treat this as a risk.
row.load_id: No open_clip, Hugging Face or timm id. Download https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/slip/slip_small_100ep.pt and build the model with SLIP_VITS16 from facebookresearch/SLIP models.py (needs timm's vit_small_mocov3_patch16_224). Released ckpts are full CLIP/SLIP state dicts; models.py defines the text tower and its keys follow the CLIP layout, but I did not inspect a ckpt directly.
row.export_notes: I found no ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or Hugging Face conversion and no mobile latency report; the search turned up only TinyCLIP YFCC15M ONNX exports. The architecture is plain ViT-S/16 plus a CLIP text transformer (standard ops, GPU-delegate friendly), so a manual PyTorch->ONNX->TFLite conversion is easy. Note that ViT-S/16 has 196 tokens and about 4.6 GMACs, versus about 49 tokens for TinyCLIP's /32 tower, so expect it to be slower per photo than the current model even though it has fewer params.
row.released: December 2021 (arXiv 2112.12750; ECCV 2022)

row.name: BLIP ITM base COCO, ITC path only (Salesforce/blip-itm-base-coco = model_base_retrieval_coco.pth)
row.image_params_M: ~86.3M, my estimate from config.json (no params count in the card or safetensors metadata). ViT-B/16 at 384px, hidden 768, 12 layers, 577 tokens: about 86.1M for the encoder plus 0.2M for vision_proj (768->256). Cross-check: pytorch_model.bin is 895,139,697 B fp32, so the whole checkpoint is about 224M params. That matches the paper's Table 3 figure of "224M".
row.text_params_M: ~109M for ITC text-only use, my estimate from config.json. BERT-base, vocab 30524, 12 layers, 768 hidden: about 23.8M for embeddings, 85.1M for the layers, 0.2M for text_proj. The checkpoint's text encoder also has 12 cross-attention blocks (about 28M) and an ITM head. ITC does not use these, but you have to strip them before export. The text tower is released (same checkpoint and tokenizer).
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported for this checkpoint. The BLIP paper and model card have no ImageNet zero-shot number. The only third-party figure I found (47.48%, arXiv 2209.13816) is for a ViT-L BLIP, not this base COCO-finetuned model. Expect it to be weak: this checkpoint is retrieval-finetuned on COCO, not a general classifier.
row.other_zeroshot: COCO 5k retrieval after finetuning on COCO, from the BLIP paper, Table 5. Both rows use ITC top-k=256 followed by ITM rerank, so ITC-only results will be lower. BLIP 129M ViT-B: TR@1 81.9, IR@1 64.3. BLIP 14M ViT-B: TR@1 80.6, IR@1 63.1. README says the 'BLIP w/ ViT-B' retrieval checkpoint is the 129M-pretrain model; the CapFilt-L column has no retrieval checkpoint. Flickr30K zero-shot from the COCO-finetuned model, paper Table 6, 129M: TR@1 96.0, IR@1 85.0, also reranked with ITM. The paper gives no ITC-only numbers.
row.weights_license: bsd-3-clause (HF metadata tag). The GitHub repo LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2022 Salesforce.com, Inc.
row.license_notes: The license tag is permissive: BSD-3-Clause on both HF and the GitHub LICENSE.txt, with the usual no-endorsement and keep-the-notice clauses. But the HF model card adds a use statement that conflicts with commercial shipping: "This release is for research purposes only in support of an academic paper." The card also points users to Salesforce's AUP and AI AUP. The GitHub repo salesforce/BLIP was archived on 2026-03-03, and its README says "This repo is DEPRECATED and no longer supported" and "We recommend that you do not use the content in this repo for any production or sensitive purpose". The code and weights licenses do not differ (both BSD-3); the restriction comes from the card text and README, not from the LICENSE file. Pretraining data had about 129M images (COCO, VG, CC3M, CC12M, SBU, LAION-115M subset) plus COCO finetuning, so dataset-license caveats apply too. Calling it commercially clean would need legal review, so I set it to unclear (it leans negative).
row.arch: ViT-B/16 image encoder at 384x384 (24x24=576 patches + CLS = 577 tokens). Text encoder is BERT-base (bert-base-uncased tokenizer, vocab 30524) with interleaved cross-attention, which ITC skips. The ITC shared embedding is 256-d (vision_proj and text_proj 768->256, image_text_hidden_size=256). The config's projection_dim=512 is an unused HF default. HF class is BlipForImageTextRetrieval; call it with use_itm_head=False for cosine/ITC scores.
row.image_gmacs: ~55.5 GMACs (my estimate: same compute as a standard ViT-B/16 at 384, e.g. timm vit_base_patch16_384; not stated by Salesforce). That is roughly 12-15x more than TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224.
row.load_id: HF transformers: BlipForImageTextRetrieval.from_pretrained('Salesforce/blip-itm-base-coco') with BlipProcessor. Use get_image_features/vision_proj and text_proj with use_itm_head=False for embeddings. LAVIS name: blip_retrieval / blip_image_text_matching 'base'. Original checkpoint: model_base_retrieval_coco.pth.
row.released: 2022-01 (paper, arXiv 2201.12086); HF repo created 2022-12-12
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, LiteRT, CoreML or ONNX export of this checkpoint, and no mobile latency reports. The only related report is a Unity forum thread where torch.onnx.export of BLIP captioning failed on an aten::full op; that is the decoder, not the retrieval model. HF hosts only pytorch_model.bin and tf_model.h5 (895 MB each, fp32); safetensors exist only as unmerged PR discussions. The vision tower is a plain ViT-B/16 and should convert fine. The text tower needs a text-only wrapper that bypasses the cross-attention blocks. Estimated sizes: int8 image tower about 87 MB, nearly 2x the current 46 MB; int8 text tower about 110 MB. At 384px and about 55 GMACs, expect latency on an A54 to be many times the current 73 ms. Too big and too slow for this app.

verdicts.corrections:
I could not refute anything in the row. The primary sources confirm the following:
- The HF card is tagged bsd-3-clause, and its Ethical Considerations section says "This release is for research purposes only in support of an academic paper". It also points to Salesforce's AUP and AI AUP.
- GitHub LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2022 Salesforce.com, Inc.
- The README opens with "This repo is DEPRECATED and no longer supported" and advises against "any production or sensitive purpose".
- commercial_ok = "unclear" (leaning negative) is the right call. Treat the row as NOT commercially clean for this app.
- config.json matches: vision hidden 768, 12 layers, 384px, patch 16, MLP 3072. Text: BERT-base, vocab 30524, 12 layers. image_text_hidden_size is 256. The 512 projection_dim is an unused default.
- The estimates hold: image tower ~86M (ViT-B/16@384), ITC text path ~109M.
- No ImageNet-1k zero-shot number is reported anywhere for this checkpoint.

Two notes, not corrections:
- I did not re-check the third-party 47.48% figure (arXiv 2209.13816) or the paper's Table 5/6 retrieval numbers line by line. They are not load-bearing.
- At ~86M image params, 384px and ~55 GMACs, this model is not viable for this app anyway.

I could not refute any factual claim in this row. Every claim I checked against primary sources holds.

License (confirmed):
- The HF API cardData and tags show license:bsd-3-clause. The model is not gated.
- The GitHub LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-Clause, "Copyright (c) 2022, Salesforce.com, Inc."
- The HF card says verbatim: "This release is for research purposes only in support of an academic paper." It also points to the AUP and the AI AUP.
- The GitHub README says verbatim: "This repo is DEPRECATED and no longer supported - We recommend that you do not use the content in this repo for any production or sensitive purpose."

Recommendation: change commercial_ok from "unclear" to false (exclude). The row's own evidence supports this. The publisher states the release is research-only and advises against production use, so a skeptic should not treat it as cleared for a shipped commercial app, whatever the BSD-3 tag says.

Numbers (confirmed):
- config.json: vision image_size 384, patch_size 16, hidden 768, 12 layers. Text vocab 30524, 12 layers, hidden 768. image_text_hidden_size 256 and projection_dim 512, as the row says.
- pytorch_model.bin x-linked-size is 895,139,697 B, about 223.8M fp32 params.
- The paper's layer-sharing table lists "All 224M".
- The paper's Table 5 and Table 6 values are in the text: 80.6/63.1 (14M), 81.9/64.3 (129M), and Flickr ZS 96.0/85.0.
- The paper confirms the retrieval protocol: ITC selects top-k candidates (k=256 COCO, k=128 Flickr), then ITM reranks.
- Neither the card nor the paper reports an ImageNet zero-shot result.
- The ~86M image and ~109M text estimates are arithmetically consistent: ViT-B/16 with a 577-token pos-embed, and BERT-base without its roughly 28M of cross-attention weights.

This model remains unsuitable for the app: the image tower is about 2x the 50M target, it runs at 384px, and the license is not clean.

row.name: DeCLIP (ResNet50 and ViT-B/32, DeCLIP-88M checkpoints)
row.arch: Two image backbones. RN50 is CLIP's ModifiedResNet-50 with a 1024-d embedding. ViT-B/32 has width 768, 12 layers, 12 heads, patch 32 and 49+1 tokens, with an unusual 3072-d embedding (config embed_dim: 3072). The text tower is a CLIP-style transformer: width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, 77-token context, CLIP BPE vocab of 49,408. Extra training-only heads (MLM, SimSiam predictor, nearest-neighbour bank) are not needed at inference.
row.image_params_M: Calculated from the repo code, not stated anywhere: about 38M for RN50 (CLIP ModifiedResNet-50 with a 1024-d attention-pool output) and about 90M for ViT-B/32 (standard ViT-B/32 is about 87.5M, plus a 768x3072 projection of about 2.4M). ViT-B/32 is near the 100M ceiling. RN50 is under 50M, but its zero-shot accuracy is weak.
row.text_params_M: Calculated from text_transformer.py defaults: about 38M (512-wide, 12-layer CLIP text transformer of about 37.8M, plus a 512x1024 projection for RN50). For ViT-B/32 it is about 39M because of the 512x3072 projection.
row.in1k_zeroshot: The paper (arXiv 2110.05208) reports RN50 at 60.4% and ViT-B/32 at 66.2%, both trained on DeCLIP-88M. The repo README model zoo lists the same checkpoints as RN50 62.5% and ViT-B/32 66.2%. The YFCC-15M benchmark checkpoints from the CLIP-Benchmark paper (arXiv 2203.05796) score much lower, in the 40% range.
row.other_zeroshot: The paper reports linear-probe and zero-shot results on 11 downstream datasets. It reports no COCO or Flickr retrieval for the DeCLIP-88M models. The CLIP-Benchmark paper covers the YFCC15M variants (CLIP, DeCLIP, SLIP, FILIP, DeFILIP).
row.weights_license: No standard license. The README says the project is BSD-2-Clause for academic use and that commercial users must contact the authors. The repo has no LICENSE file (GitHub reports license null), and setup.py says license='Internal'. The weights are on Google Drive with no license file attached.
row.license_notes:
The README "License" section says that for academic use the project is licensed under the 2-clause BSD License, and that for commercial use you should contact the authors. Commercial use is therefore not granted without a separate agreement with SenseTime. This rules DeCLIP out under the user's criteria. setup.py declares license='Internal' with the classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: Internal'. The Google Drive weights add no license of their own, so the academic-only README terms are the only grant.

The training data adds a second problem. DeCLIP-88M is about 29M open pairs (CC3M, CC12M, YFCC15M) plus about 59M web-crawled pairs that were never released. The terms of the crawled data are unknown.

The repo has been inactive since 2022-09-19.
sources: https://github.com/Sense-GVT/DeCLIP (README: model zoo plus the License section)
Google Drive full-model links: R50 1YS6xRdF5bY4rvgyCFQVIyPMr7evfZi3D, ViT-B/32 135v0R8zTiAppr-BejtoXRHeGeMTlDf2x (HTTP 200 on 2026-10-21)
row.load_id: No open_clip, Hugging Face or timm id. Load the Google Drive .pth.tar into the repo's prototype/model/declip.py (declip_res50 / declip_vitb32), which uses SenseTime linklink distributed utilities. The README also lists visual-only backbone checkpoints with no text encoder; use the "w text encoder" ones.
row.image_gmacs: Not reported. Estimate from the standard architectures: about 4.4 GMACs for ViT-B/32 and about 5.4 GMACs for CLIP RN50 at 224px.
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export and no mobile latency report. RN50's attention pool and the ViT are plain CLIP-style ops, so export should be possible after porting the model out of the linklink/prototype codebase. The text tower has both the released full-model checkpoints and visual-only checkpoints, so pick the full ones. These models are not worth pursuing: they are not licensed for commercial use, and the accuracy is matched or beaten by TinyCLIP (MIT) and OpenCLIP B/32 DataComp (MIT).

row.name: ALIP ViT-B/32 (YFCC15M)
row.arch: This is a standard OpenAI-CLIP ViT-B/32. The image tower has 12 layers, width 768, patch size 32 at 224px, which gives 49 patch tokens plus 1 CLS token. The text tower is a 12-layer, width-512, 8-head transformer with a 77-token context and the CLIP BPE vocabulary of 49,408. The shared embedding has 512 dimensions. Source: src/open_alip/model_configs/ViT-B-32.json. ALIP's 'bi-path' (raw text plus synthetic caption) only changes the training loss and gating. Inference is a plain dual encoder.
row.image_params_M: 87.8 (my calculation from the config: 87,849,216; matches standard CLIP ViT-B/32). This is about 2x TinyCLIP-45M and close to the 100M ceiling.
row.text_params_M: 63.4 (my calculation from the config: 63,428,096, of which 25.3M is the token embedding)
row.image_gmacs: ~4.4 (not in the repo or paper; this is the standard ViT-B/32 at 224 figure, e.g. from open_clip's model profile)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 40.3%. Source: ALIP README zero-shot table, consistent with the paper (arXiv 2308.08428). Trained on YFCC15M only. This is far below the current TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 62.7%.
row.other_zeroshot: These figures are from the README and paper. MSCOCO zero-shot retrieval R@1 is 46.8 image-to-text and 29.3 text-to-image. Flickr30k R@1 is 70.5 / 48.9. The 11-dataset zero-shot average is 41.7: CIFAR10 83.8, CIFAR100 51.9, Food101 45.4, Pets 30.7, Flowers 54.8, SUN397 47.8, Cars 3.4, DTD 23.2, Caltech101 74.1, Aircraft 2.7.
row.weights_license: unclear. The README says the project is released under the MIT license, but the LICENSE file it links does not exist (GitHub API returns 404 and repo license=null). The weights have no license statement on Google Drive or BaiduYun.
row.license_notes: The README's License section says "This project is released under the MIT license" and links to a LICENSE file. That file was never committed: the repo has a single code commit, from 2023-08-22, and GitHub detects no license. The weights are distributed only as ALIP_YFCC15M_B32.pt on Google Drive (link still live as of 2026-10-21) and on BaiduYun, and no license text sits next to them. There is no Hugging Face model card. The DeepGlint-AI HF org has no ALIP repo. So nothing explicitly says the MIT grant covers the weights. There is no model card, so no extra use restrictions are stated either. Data caveat: YFCC15M is a subset of YFCC100M, whose Flickr images carry mixed Creative Commons licenses, including NC variants. The synthetic captions were generated with OFA (Apache-2.0). To be safe for commercial use, get written confirmation or an added LICENSE from DeepGlint. The code is based on open_clip, which is MIT.
row.load_id: No hub ID. Download ALIP_YFCC15M_B32.pt from https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AqSHisCKZOZ16Q3sYguK6zIZIuwwEriE and load it with the repo's src/open_alip factory, model name 'ViT-B/32'. The state dict should be close to an open_clip / OpenAI ViT-B-32 layout and may remap into open_clip, but I have not verified this.
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export and no mobile latency report. It is a vanilla ViT-B/32 with QuickGELU, LayerNorm and standard MHA, so it should export like any CLIP B/32 through ONNX to LiteRT. int8 image-tower size would be about 88 MB, versus 46 MB for the current TinyCLIP. Expect roughly 2x TinyCLIP-45M/32's per-photo latency (my extrapolation). Verdict: dominated. It is larger and much less accurate (40.3% vs 62.7% ImageNet zero-shot) than the model already shipped, and the weights license is unconfirmed. Not recommended.
row.released: 2023-08 (code and weights; arXiv 2308.08428, ICCV 2023)
sources: https://github.com/deepglint/ALIP (README: results tables, MIT license sentence, weights links)

License:

row.name: COYO-ALIGN-B7-Base (kakaobrain/align-base; original TF checkpoint kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base)
row.arch: Dual encoder. Image tower: EfficientNet-B7 (width 2.0, depth 3.1), 289x289 input, SiLU, depthwise conv and squeeze-excite, global pool to a 640-d embedding with no separate image projection. Text tower: BERT-base uncased (12 layers, 768 hidden, 30522 vocab, max 512 positions) plus a linear projection from 768 to 640. Shared space is 640-d. A CNN, so it has no patch tokens.
row.image_params_M: 62.1M (vision_model). I computed this by building AlignModel from the HF config.json on the meta device (transformers 4.57.6). The card does not state it. The 66M in the hint is slightly high. The total of 172.1M x 4 bytes matches pytorch_model.bin at 690,175,332 bytes. Estimated int8 size is about 62 MB, about 35% larger than the current 46 MB TinyCLIP image tower.
row.image_gmacs: About 8.4 GMACs at 289px. I measured this with torch.utils.flop_counter on a random-init AlignVisionModel; it is not reported anywhere. That is roughly 2x+ the compute of a ViT-B/32 at 224px, so expect it to be well above the current 73 ms/photo on an A54.
row.text_params_M: 109.5M (BERT-base text_model) plus 0.49M text_projection. I computed both from the config. The text tower is released in both repos, about 440 MB fp32 or about 110 MB int8.
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported. The Kakao Brain sources (HF card for coyo-align-b7-base, the coyo-align and coyo-dataset GitHub READMEs, and the HF align-performance chart) give only ImageNet KNN: 68.6 (68.618), against 69.3 for Google ALIGN-B7-Base trained on 1.8B pairs. The ALIGN paper (arXiv 2102.05918) reports zero-shot only for the EfficientNet-L2 model (76.4%), not B7. I found no third-party zero-shot IN1k evaluation of this checkpoint.
row.other_zeroshot: The coyo-align-b7-base HF card gives Flickr30k I2T R@1 88.1 and T2I R@1 73.2, and MS-COCO I2T R@1 61.2 and T2I R@1 43.1. The coyo-dataset GitHub README gives different COCO numbers: I2T 59.0 and T2I 42.419. These sources do not say whether the retrieval numbers are zero-shot or fine-tuned. For comparison, Google ALIGN-B7-Base reports COCO 55.4 / 41.7.
row.weights_license: Unclear for kakaobrain/align-base: the HF repo has no license tag, no LICENSE file and no license text. Apache-2.0 for kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base, which is Kakao Brain's original TF checkpoint: the HF metadata says license: apache-2.0.
row.license_notes: 1) The coyo-align GitHub code is under the Apache 2.0 License, and the README says the source code is licensed under Apache 2.0. 2) The original weights at kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base (TF checkpoint model-weights.data-00000-of-00001, 2.06 GB including optimizer/EMA state, card dated April 2022) are tagged license: apache-2.0 on HF, with no added use restrictions in that card. 3) The ready-to-load Transformers conversion kakaobrain/align-base (created 2023-02-24 and converted by the HF team per the card) has no license field, no LICENSE file and no license section. Its card also says the model is intended as a research output for research communities, with AI researchers as the primary users. That is copied CLIP-card boilerplate, not a license term, but it is a use statement. 4) The COYO-700M dataset is CC-BY-4.0, with each image and text subject to its original owner's license. The dataset README recommends research use and advises against commercial use as-is without filtering out inappropriate data. That is advisory, not a weights license term. Net: there is a clear Apache-2.0 grant on the original TF checkpoint, but the convenient HF transformers repo is unlicensed. The clean commercial path is to convert from coyo-align-b7-base yourself, or get confirmation that align-base carries the same grant. I did not verify that the two repos hold byte-identical weights.
row.load_id: HF transformers: AlignModel.from_pretrained("kakaobrain/align-base") with AlignProcessor. The Apache-2.0 TF checkpoint is kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base and needs the coyo-align repo code to load. Not available in open_clip or timm.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. An HF Hub search for align-base derivatives found only kakaobrain repos and two empty or fine-tune forks, and Optimum's TFLite exporter does not list ALIGN or EfficientNet. EfficientNet-B7 ops (depthwise conv, SiLU, SE global-pool and mul, 1x1 conv) all work on the LiteRT GPU delegate and XNNPACK. Export via ai-edge-torch or ONNX should be straightforward, but EfficientNet with int8 quantization is known to lose accuracy, so per-channel or fp16 is advisable. The cost is high: about 8.4 GMACs at 289px, 62M params and a 55-stage-deep CNN, so latency will likely be several times TinyCLIP-45M/32. The BERT-base text tower (110M) is large for an on-demand download. Overall the 2022-era model is a poor fit: bigger and slower than TinyCLIP, with no proven zero-shot gain, and KNN of 68.6 is below the ~72-73% zero-shot of PE-Core S16 or OpenCLIP B/32 DataComp.
row.released: Model card date April 2022. kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base repo last modified 2022-11-11. kakaobrain/align-base (transformers conversion) created 2023-02-24, last modified 2023-03-08.

verdicts.corrections: No refutation found. I checked the HF API on 2026-10-22. kakaobrain/align-base has no license tag in its cardData or tags, and no LICENSE file; its only files are README, config, preprocessor config, pytorch_model.bin and the tokenizer files. Its README calls it "a research output for research communities" and names AI researchers as the primary users. That is a use statement, not a license grant, so commercial_ok stays unclear and must not be read as yes. kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base has cardData license apache-2.0 (tag license:apache-2.0), was created 2022-11-09 and last modified 2022-11-11. The github coyo-align README says only "The source codes are licensed under Apache 2.0 License". I rebuilt AlignModel from the align-base config.json on the meta device and got vision_model 62.14M, text_model 109.48M, text_projection 0.49M, total 172.12M, image_size 289, all matching the row. The coyo-align README itself gives 66M+110M params, so the official figure is 66M and 62.1M is the computed one; note both. Its ImageNet column is KNN only (COYO-ALIGN-B7-Base 68.6 vs Google ALIGN-B7-Base 69.3), and it reports no ImageNet zero-shot score, so 'not reported' is correct. The retrieval numbers 88.1/73.2/61.2/43.1 match. One caveat: the 76.4 for ALIGN-L2 appears in the coyo README's KNN column, but the ALIGN paper reports 76.4% zero-shot for L2, so the row's paper citation is still right. The commercial path remains: convert the Apache-2.0 TF checkpoint yourself. Weight identity between the two repos is still unverified.

I could not refute the row. Every claim I checked holds as stated.

License, from HF API metadata:
- kakaobrain/coyo-align-b7-base has cardData license: apache-2.0 and the tag license:apache-2.0.
- kakaobrain/align-base has no license field in cardData, no license tag, and only these files: README.md, config.json, preprocessor_config.json, pytorch_model.bin, tokenizer and vocab files. There is no LICENSE file.
- The align-base README contains the CLIP-style boilerplate ("intended as a research output for research communities" and "primary intended users ... are AI researchers"). It has no actual license clause.
- The coyo-align GitHub README says "The source codes are licensed under Apache 2.0 License."
- The row's commercial_ok of "unclear" is therefore correct. The Apache-2.0 grant is clear only on the original TF checkpoint. The convenient Transformers repo is unlicensed, so shipping it commercially is not cleanly permitted unless you convert from coyo-align-b7-base yourself.

Param counts: I rebuilt AlignModel from align-base config.json on the meta device with transformers 4.57.6.
- vision_model 62.14M, text_model 109.48M, text_projection 0.49M, total 172.12M.
- The config has vision hidden_dim 640, projection_dim 640, image_size 289, width 2.0 and depth 3.1.
- pytorch_model.bin is 690,175,332 bytes (x-linked-size). Divided by 4 that is about 172.5M floats, which fits the total plus BatchNorm buffers.

ImageNet: the coyo-align-b7-base card table reports only ImageNet KNN.
- COYO-ALIGN-B7-Base: 68.6, with Flickr I2T/T2I 88.1/73.2 and COCO 61.2/43.1.
- Google ALIGN-B7-Base: 69.3.
- No IN1k zero-shot number appears there. "Not reported" is correct.

I did not re-measure the 8.4 GMACs figure. Nothing contradicts it.

row.name: MetaCLIP 2 worldwide distilled S/16, M/16, B/32 (plus -384 and mT5 variants)
row.arch: These are ViT image towers with a CLIP text transformer, from MetaClip2Model in HF transformers. All are 12 layers. S/16 is width 384, 6 heads, MLP 1536, projection dim 384. M/16 is width 512, 8 heads, MLP 2048, projection 512. B/32 is width 768, 12 heads, MLP 3072, projection 512. At 224px, S/16 and M/16 give 196+1 tokens and B/32 gives 49+1. The -384 variants use 384px. In the default variants the text tower is a 12-layer CLIP-style transformer with the XLM-V tokenizer (901,629-token vocab, 77-token context), at width 384 for S/16 and 512 for M/16 and B/32. The mT5 variants use the SigLIP-i18n/mT5 tokenizer instead (250,000 vocab). There is also a distilled B/16 and L/14.
row.image_params_M: I computed these from the HF config.json files; they are not stated anywhere. S/16 is about 22M, M/16 about 38-39M and B/32 about 88M (each includes patch embed, positional embedding and projection).
row.text_params_M: I computed these from the configs; they are dominated by the token-embedding table. XLM-V variants: S/16 text is about 368M (346M embeddings plus about 21M transformer; repo total 389.5M), M/16 about 499M (462M embeddings; repo total 538M) and B/32 about 499M (repo total 587.6M). mT5-tokenizer variants: mt5-s16 text is about 117M (96M embeddings; repo total 139.3M), mt5-m16 about 166M (repo total 204.7M) and mt5-b32 about 166M (repo total 254.0M). Every text tower is far larger than the current 18M text tower.
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported for the distilled models. The official README table gives only CVQA-LOCAL zero-shot accuracy: S16 46.9, S16-384 47.4, S16-mT5 42.8, M16 49.3, M16-384 50.7, M16-mT5 48.7, B32 49.1, B32-384 50.0, B32-mT5 48.4. The HF model cards report no benchmarks, and I did not find an IN-1k number in the search I ran.
row.other_zeroshot: CVQA-LOCAL zero-shot only, from the GitHub README (numbers above). All distilled models are listed as trained on 29B seen pairs with online curation. They are multilingual (worldwide data).
row.weights_license: CC-BY-NC-4.0
row.license_notes: The HF model card front matter says `license: cc-by-nc-4.0` on every distilled repo I checked: worldwide-s16, -m16, -b32, -s16-384, mt5-worldwide-s16, -m16, -b32. The GitHub repo LICENSE file is the full "Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International" text. The README says "The majority of Meta CLIP is licensed under CC-BY-NC", and only some parts (code derived from open_clip) carry other terms. Code and weights are therefore both non-commercial, and no separate permissive weights license exists. The model card adds no restrictions beyond the license tag. This EXCLUDES it for a shipped commercial app.
row.load_id: HF transformers (MetaClip2Model, AutoModel): facebook/metaclip-2-worldwide-s16, facebook/metaclip-2-worldwide-m16, facebook/metaclip-2-worldwide-b32 (and -s16-384, -m16-384, -b32-384, -b16, -b16-384, -l14), plus facebook/metaclip-2-mt5-worldwide-s16, -m16, -b32. The original .pt checkpoints (e.g. metaclip2_b32_224px_worldwide.pt) load in the facebookresearch/MetaCLIP repo, as open_clip-style ViT-S-16-worldwide and similar.
row.export_notes: I found no official or community TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. The image towers are plain ViTs, so they should export like other CLIP ViTs. The text towers are impractical on a phone because of the 900k-entry XLM-V embedding table: about 346-462M params, roughly 0.35-0.46 GB even at int8. The mT5 variants cut the vocab to 250k but still have about 96-128M of embedding params. The HF weights are F32 safetensors.
row.released: 2025-11-21 (README news entry: distilled models and training/eval code released). HF repos were created 2025-11-12, and the -384 variants on 2025-11-24. The paper (arXiv 2507.22062) is from 2025-07-29.

row.name: Apple TiC-CLIP ViT-B/16 (basic/bestpool x oracle/cumulative/sequential, yearly checkpoints 2016-2022)
row.arch: OpenCLIP 'ViT-B-16': ViT-B/16 image tower (12L, width 768, patch 16, 196+1 tokens at 224px). Standard 12L/512-wide CLIP text transformer, 77 tokens. Trained by continual learning on TiC-DataComp-Yearly.
row.image_params_M: ~86 (not stated on the model card. This is the standard OpenCLIP ViT-B-16 config value, which the card's create_model_and_transforms('ViT-B-16') uses)
row.text_params_M: ~63 (standard OpenCLIP ViT-B-16 text tower, not stated on the card)
row.image_gmacs: ~17.6 at 224px (OpenCLIP's ViT-B-16 benchmark figure, not from the TiC paper)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 73.3% for Oracle at XL scale with Bestpool filtering. Cumulative-All gets 71.6% and Sequential 66.5% (TiC-CLIP paper, arXiv 2310.16226v3, Table 2). The HF model cards report no ImageNet numbers. I did not find a figure for the 'basic' (non-bestpool) variants. The basic-oracle card also contradicts itself: it says 'xlarge' in the text but its training command uses --scale tic_medium.
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 2 (XL, Bestpool, Oracle): Flickr30k retrieval 68.0, average over 28 datasets 65.8, ImageNet distribution shifts 61.3.
row.weights_license: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License Agreement (HF tag 'custom-apple-license')
row.license_notes: Excluded. The LICENSE file in the HF weights repos (checked apple/TiC-CLIP-basic-oracle and apple/TiC-CLIP-bestpool-oracle, (C) 2025) is the Apple ML Research Model License. It grants rights 'exclusively for Research Purposes', defined as non-commercial research, and it explicitly bars use in any commercial product or service. The code license differs: the LICENSE in the GitHub repo apple/ml-tic-clip is the permissive Apple sample-code-style license ('use, reproduce, modify and redistribute'), but it covers only the code, not the weights. The model card describes the intended use as research (continual-training starting points). The six models in the HF collection presumably share the research license; I checked two of them directly. On top of the license problem, the image tower (~86M) is near the ~100M ceiling and accuracy matches what permissively licensed alternatives already offer (OpenCLIP B/32 DataComp-XL at 72.7%, MIT).
row.load_id: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('ViT-B-16', pretrained=hf_hub_download('apple/TiC-CLIP-basic-oracle', 'checkpoints/2016.pt')). Yearly checkpoints are named checkpoints/<YEAR>.pt. Other repos: apple/TiC-CLIP-{basic,bestpool}-{oracle,cumulative,sequential}.
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, ONNX or CoreML exports and no mobile latency reports. It is a plain OpenCLIP ViT-B/16, so it exports like any ViT-B/16 (standard ops, GPU-delegate friendly), but expect about 4x the per-photo latency of the current 45M/32 model. The checkpoint is a full CLIP state dict, and the card's example calls encode_text, so the text tower is released. The HF repo is about 1.8 GB across many yearly checkpoints.
row.released: Paper arXiv Oct 2023 (ICLR 2024); HF models June 2024

row.name: Apple MobileCLIP2 (S0 / S2 / B / S3 / S4 / L-14). Verdict: EXCLUDED, because the weights license is research-only.

The S0 figure checks out against the config: 12 layers x 512 wide is about 37.8M, plus the 49408x512 token embedding of about 25.3M, gives about 63.4M.
