row.in1k_zeroshot: S0 71.5, S2 77.2, B 79.4, S3 80.7, L-14 81.9, S4 81.9 (Apple ml-mobileclip README and the HF model cards, all trained on 13B seen samples of DFNDR-2B)
row.other_zeroshot: Average over 38 datasets: S0 59.7, S2 64.1, B 65.8, S3 66.8, L-14 67.8, S4 67.5 (Apple README). COCO retrieval numbers are in the paper (arXiv 2508.20691); I did not pull them because the model is excluded.
row.weights_license: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License Agreement (HF tag: apple-amlr). The code is MIT and the data is CC-BY-NC-ND.
row.license_notes:
Apple's repo has three license files: LICENSE (code, MIT), LICENSE_MODELS (weights) and LICENSE_DATA (data, CC-BY-NC-ND). LICENSE_MODELS grants use "exclusively for Research Purposes", defined as non-commercial scientific research. It says Research Purposes do not include "use in any commercial product or service". It also limits Model Derivatives (fine-tunes, retrains and modifications) to Research Purposes, so a converted or quantized TFLite file stays under these terms. The license can be revoked.

Every apple/MobileCLIP2-* HF repo has license: apple-amlr in its cardData and includes a LICENSE file. That covers S0/S2/B/S3/S4/L-14 and the CoCa variants. The timm/MobileCLIP2-*-OpenCLIP repos, which OpenCLIP's 'dfndr2b' tag downloads from, show the apple-amlr tag on their cards (checked for S0); those weights are Apple's.

Several third-party repos carry the wrong license tag, and the upstream AMLR terms still apply to them: szw0407/mobileclip2_s2_litert_export (tagged MIT), ketsugePLATINUM/mobileclip2-b-fp16 (tagged apache-2.0) and anton96vice/mobileclip2_tflite (tagged apache-2.0). The anton96vice repo's files are actually MobileCLIP v1 S1/S2/B (datacompdr), not v2. A newer MobileCLIP3 is not mentioned in Apple's README, and no MobileCLIP3 repo turned up in an HF search.
row.load_id: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('MobileCLIP2-S0', pretrained='dfndr2b'), which downloads from the timm/MobileCLIP2-S0-OpenCLIP HF repo. The same pattern works for S2, B, S3, S4 and L-14. Apple's own checkpoint is apple/MobileCLIP2-S0 (mobileclip2_s0.pt), loaded through the ml-mobileclip package. Call reparameterize_model() before inference or export.
row.released: 2025-08 (apple/MobileCLIP2-S0 created 2025-08-25; code and models released 2025-08-28; arXiv 2508.20691; TMLR 2025 Featured Certification)
row.export_notes:
The text tower is released for every variant (full dual encoder). Third-party exports:
- ONNX: RuteNL/MobileCLIP2-{S0,S2,S3,S4,B}-OpenCLIP-ONNX, plhery/mobileclip2-onnx (transformers.js), felixhrdyn/mobileclip2-s0-onnx (fp32/int8; the author reports about 112 ms for the vision tower on a desktop CPU), BambooHero/mobileclip2-s0-text-onnx (quantized text tower).
- LiteRT/TFLite: szw0407/mobileclip2_s2_litert_export.
- CoreML: nufrnd/LosslessVideoCutter-mobileclip2-b.

The S0 ONNX vision tower is about 43 MB in fp32 at 256px. Apple's latency numbers are iPhone-only, and I found no Android GPU-delegate latency report. FastViT uses reparameterizable MobileOne-style blocks, which need reparameterize_model() before export, plus large-kernel depthwise convs and attention. The PicQuery-ships-mobileclip2_s0 claim was not verified (search found nothing). None of this matters for a commercial app because of the license.

row.name: CLIP-KD ViT-T/16 student (teacher OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 LAION-400M, distilled on CC3M+CC12M)
row.org: winycg (Chuanguang Yang et al., CAS ICT); CVPR 2024 paper "CLIP-KD: An Empirical Study of CLIP Model Distillation"
row.released: Paper on arXiv 2307.12732 (Jul 2023), CVPR 2024. Checkpoint released as a GitHub release asset under CLIP-KDv0.1: release published 2024-03-31, this asset uploaded 2024-04-02. The third-party HF re-upload (fassabilf) was created 2026-03-31.
row.arch: Plain ViT-T/16 (DeiT-Tiny shape): width 192, 12 layers, patch 16. At 224 px that is 196 patches plus CLS, so 197 tokens. Embedding dim 512. Text tower is an OpenCLIP causal transformer: width 384, 6 heads, 12 layers, context 77, vocab 49408. Config is src/open_clip/model_configs/ViT-T-16.json in the repo.
row.image_params_M: About 5.6M. Paper Table 2 says 5.6M visual. My count from the config is about 5.62M: 12 blocks x 0.445M, plus 0.147M patch embedding, plus 0.098M projection.
row.text_params_M: About 40.5M in total (my count from the config). That is 21.3M of transformer layers, which matches paper Table 2's "21.3M", plus 19.0M for the token embedding (49408 x 384) and 0.2M for the projection. Cross-check: the HF fp32 safetensors file is 184.5 MB, which is about 46.1M params for both towers together. The text tower is about 7x larger than the image tower.
row.image_gmacs: About 1.1 GMACs. This is not measured for this checkpoint: I took the published timm figure for the identical-shape vit_tiny_patch16_224 / DeiT-Ti (~1.1-1.3 G). The paper reports no FLOPs.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 42.6%. Source: paper Table 5 and the repo README, for the LAION-400M ViT-B/16 teacher. Other numbers for the same student: 40.9% with the ViT-L/14 LAION teacher, 34.9% with the CC3M+12M ViT-B/16 teacher, 30.6% without KD. That is about 20 points below the TinyCLIP-45M/32 now shipped (62.7%).
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 5, this checkpoint: MSCOCO 5k I2T R@1 28.1 and T2I R@1 26.0; Flickr30k I2T R@1 60.4 and T2I R@1 59.9. Sibling students: RN50 (ViT-B/16 LAION teacher) scores 55.4% IN, COCO 36.3/33.4, Flickr 73.0/72.2, with a 38.3M image tower. MobileViT-S (CC teacher) scores 36.0% IN, COCO 26.1/24.9.
row.weights_license: None from the authors. The GitHub repo has no LICENSE file, the GitHub API reports license: null, and neither the README nor the paper names a code or weights license. The third-party HF re-uploads (fassabilf/*, romrawinjp/*) are tagged "mit", but only by the uploader. There is no basis for it in the original repo.
row.license_notes:
1. Original source: github.com/winycg/CLIP-KD (an open_clip fork) has no LICENSE at the root or under src/. The GitHub license field is null. The README has no license text. The checkpoints are GitHub release assets that carry no terms. With no grant, the default is all rights reserved, so I put "unclear", leaning to not usable as-is. The repo also strips open_clip's MIT notice from derived code.
2. Third-party "MIT" tags: fassabilf/clipkd-released-ViT-T-16-clipkd-vitb16laion-cc12m and romrawinjp/clip-kd_ViT-T-16-Laion400M_KD-CC3M12M both say license: mit. These are re-uploads by people who are not the authors. A re-uploader cannot relicense weights, so do not rely on these tags.
3. Upstream ingredients look permissive: the teacher (OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 laion400m_e32) is MIT; CC3M and CC12M terms allow any use with attribution to Google; LAION-400M metadata is CC-BY-4.0 (images remain third-party copyright).
4. airesearch/ViT-T-16-CC9M-distill-* (Dec 2025) checkpoints have no license tag. Their variants distilled from DFN2B-CLIP inherit Apple's DFN terms (apple-amlr / sample-code license), and the variants distilled from SigLIP SO400M involve Gemma-adjacent terms. Treat all of them as unclear.
5. Commercial use needs an explicit license from winycg, for example by opening an issue. The repo has no existing license issue.
row.load_id: Official: https://github.com/winycg/CLIP-KD/releases/download/CLIP-KDv0.1/ViT_B_16_laion400m_kd_ViT_T_16_cc3m_12m_ep32.pt (553.8 MB; at about 12 bytes/param this is consistent with a training checkpoint that includes optimizer state). Load it with model 'ViT-T-16' through the repo's open_clip fork. Third-party, ready to use: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('hf-hub:fassabilf/clipkd-released-ViT-T-16-clipkd-vitb16laion-cc12m'), which ships open_clip_config.json, a 184.5 MB fp32 open_clip_model.safetensors and a tokenizer. The text tower is included in both.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export and no mobile latency report, in the repo issues, on HF or on the web. The architecture is a vanilla ViT-T and a vanilla OpenCLIP text transformer. Ops are LayerNorm, GELU, MHA, matmul and argmax-EOT pooling. That should convert cleanly through PyTorch -> ONNX/ai-edge-torch -> TFLite, and the image tower is GPU-delegate-friendly. The image tower is about 1.1 GMACs, against about 4.4 GMACs for ViT-B/32-class TinyCLIP-45M, so expect roughly 3-4x faster than the current 73 ms on an A54; this is an estimate, not measured. Int8 image tower would be about 6 MB. The text tower would be about 41 MB int8 (fp16 about 81 MB), and the token embedding dominates its size.
sources: https://github.com/winycg/CLIP-KD (README; GitHub API license=null; no LICENSE in tree)

row.name: Apple MobileCLIP v1 (S0 / S1 / S2 / B / B-LT)
row.arch: The image towers are hybrid conv/attention MobileOne/FastViT-style "MCi" encoders (mci0 for S0, mci2 for S2, per config.json). They use reparameterizable blocks that must be fused before export. S0 pairs with a 4-layer MobileOne-style "repmixer" text encoder. S1, S2 and B use a 12-layer, 512-wide, 8-head base text transformer with context 77 and vocab 49408. The embedding dim is 512. B uses a ViT-B/16 image encoder.
row.resolution: 256x256 (image_size 256 in the HF config.json for S0 and S2)
row.image_params_M: S0 11.4, S1 21.5, S2 35.7, B and B-LT 86.3 (official model-card table)
row.text_params_M: S0 42.4; S1, S2, B and B-LT 63.4 (official table)
row.image_gmacs: Not checked. The card only gives latency: S0 1.5 ms, S1 2.5 ms, S2 3.6 ms, B 10.4 ms (image tower, iPhone 12 Pro Max in the paper). Text tower latency is 1.6 ms for S0 and 3.3 ms for the others.
row.in1k_zeroshot: S0 67.8, S1 72.6, S2 74.4, B 76.8, B-LT 77.2. Averages over 38 datasets: 58.1, 61.3, 63.7, 65.2, 65.8. Source: the official HF card and GitHub README table.
row.other_zeroshot: Not pulled. The paper (arXiv 2311.17049) reports Flickr/COCO retrieval.
row.weights_license: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License Agreement (apple-amlr). This has applied since 2025-02-28 on HF and 2025-08-29 in the GitHub LICENSE_MODELS file. Before that the weights were under the permissive Apple sample-code-style "ML-MobileCLIP Model Weights and Data" license (license_name: apple-ascl).
row.license_notes:
EXCLUDED under the current license. The GitHub README lists three licenses: code is MIT (LICENSE), models are the Apple ML Research Model TOU (LICENSE_MODELS), and data is CC-BY-NC-ND (LICENSE_DATA). LICENSE_MODELS grants use only for research purposes and says these exclude "any commercial exploitation". It also excludes "product development or use in any commercial product or service". Model derivatives are limited to research purposes as well. The HF cards for apple/MobileCLIP-S0/S2 now carry `license: apple-amlr` in the front matter. The HF LICENSE file is the AMLR text, which begins "Disclaimer: ... for the sole purpose of scientific research". The front matter still has the stale fields `license_name: apple-ascl` and `license_link: .../LICENSE_weights_data`. That link now returns 404 because the file was deleted on 2025-08-29. All four apple/MobileCLIP-*-OpenCLIP mirrors are also `license: apple-amlr`.

LICENSE TRAP / HISTORY (checked in git history). From 2024-03 until 2024-07-22, the HF and GitHub LICENSE was Apple's sample-code-style license. On 2024-07-22, commit 341ef05 added LICENSE_weights_data, titled "ML-MobileCLIP Model Weights and Data". It is a permissive ASCL-style grant: "use, reproduce, modify and redistribute ... with or without modifications", with no commercial restriction. Apple then relicensed in two steps. On HF, "Update LICENSE" landed 2025-02-24 and "AMLR license (#2)" landed 2025-02-28. On GitHub, the "MobileCLIP2 release" commit on 2025-08-29 deleted LICENSE_weights_data and added LICENSE_MODELS. The old HF revisions are still reachable, for example apple/MobileCLIP-S2 at revision 22fec9d or d91e0cb, together with their old LICENSE files. That is presumably how Ente justifies shipping MobileCLIP commercially: a community Ente page says Magic Search is based on Apple's MobileCLIP, and that adoption predates the relicense. I could not verify whether a grant taken under the old license survives the relicense. It is legally unclear and needs a lawyer. Relying on it for a new commercial app now is risky, so treat this as excluded. The DataCompDR training data is CC-BY-NC-ND, which is a further caveat.
row.load_id: HF apple/MobileCLIP-S0, -S1, -S2, -B, -B-LT give mobileclip.create_model_and_transforms('mobileclip_s0', pretrained=...). The OpenCLIP variants are apple/MobileCLIP-S1-OpenCLIP, -S2-OpenCLIP, -B-OpenCLIP and -B-LT-OpenCLIP, for open_clip. The S2 checkpoint .pt is 398 MB (fp32, both towers).
row.export_notes: The official repo ships an iOS demo app (ios_app/) with CoreML exports. Reparameterize the MobileOne/FastViT blocks before export. The architecture is mostly conv plus standard attention and should be TFLite/GPU-delegate friendly after fusion, but I did not test this. Third-party ONNX exports exist, for example plhery/mobileclip2-onnx for v2. Ente ships MobileCLIP on Android and iOS through ONNX. The paper's latencies are iPhone 12 Pro Max (CoreML). I did not find a published LiteRT Android latency report.
row.released: 2023-11 (paper arXiv 2311.17049, CVPR 2024). Weights on HF 2024-03-06. B-LT added 2024-07. Relicensed to AMLR in 2025-02 (HF) and 2025-08 (GitHub).

row.name: RWKV-CLIP B/32 and B/16 (YFCC15M / LAION10M / LAION30M checkpoints)
row.org: DeepGlint and collaborators (Gu, Yang, An, Feng, Liu, Cai, Deng). Published at EMNLP 2024, arXiv 2406.06973.
row.released: Paper June 2024 (EMNLP 2024). HF weights last modified 2024-11-19. No updates since.
row.arch: Vision-RWKV (RWKV-6 WKV) image encoder: 12 layers, 640-dim, hidden rate 5, 8 heads, patch 32 or 16, no CLS token, quad-directional token shift (Q-Lerp). 224px input gives 49 tokens (B/32) or 196 tokens (B/16). Text encoder: 6-layer bidirectional RWKV-6, n_embd 640, dim_ffn 2240, ctx 77, CLIP BPE vocab of 49408. Both towers use Bi-WKV linear attention with learned per-channel decay and boost, a SiLU gate in spatial mix, and squared-ReLU channel mix. Config is model_config/RWKV_CLIP_B32.json and RWKV_CLIP_B16.json in the repo.
row.image_params_M: 84.21 (B/32), 82.83 (B/16). Source is paper Table 8. Consistent with the checkpoint size: the 598.4 MB fp32 .pt is about 150M params total.
row.text_params_M: 65.35. Source is paper Table 8. That is bigger than the OpenAI CLIP B text tower (63.4M) and about 3.6x TinyCLIP's 18M.
row.image_gmacs: Paper Table 8 labels these "FLOPs": 7.91 G image (B/32) and 31.05 G image (B/16). Text is 4.93 G. The paper does not say whether these are MACs or FLOPs.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 44.3% for B/32 on YFCC15M (paper Table 3 and repo README; 11-dataset ZS average 44.4). The paper and README report no zero-shot ImageNet for the LAION10M, LAION30M or B/16 checkpoints, only linear probe. Linear-probe ImageNet: B/32 LAION10M 63.7, B/32 LAION30M 67.2, B/16 LAION10M 68.4 (Table 11). Zero-shot for the LAION checkpoints is "not reported". It is very likely far below TinyCLIP's 62.7%, given 10-30M training pairs.
row.other_zeroshot: B/32 on YFCC15M, zero-shot retrieval R@1 (paper Table 2): Flickr30k image-to-text 76.0, text-to-image 57.6; MSCOCO image-to-text 50.3, text-to-image 34.0. Not reported for the other checkpoints.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 on the HF weights (license: apache-2.0 metadata on all 4 repos). Code is MIT (LICENSE file in the GitHub repo, Copyright 2024 DeepGlint).
row.license_notes: The licenses differ: code is MIT (github LICENSE) and weights are Apache-2.0 (HF model card YAML and tags on Kaichengalex/RWKV-CLIP-*). Both permit commercial use. The HF model cards hold only the license tag, a short description and a citation, with no added use restrictions. Data caveats: training used YFCC15M (YFCC100M CC-licensed images), and LAION10M and LAION30M were random subsets of LAION-400M (web images of mixed copyright). The paper's diverse-description pipeline also rewrote captions with an LLM fine-tuned from LLaMA3, plus OFA captions and RAM++ tags. Llama 3 license terms on outputs are a possible but remote caveat. They do not bind the released weights' license. No gating on HF.
row.load_id: HF: Kaichengalex/RWKV-CLIP-B32-YFCC15M, Kaichengalex/RWKV-CLIP-B32-LAION10M, Kaichengalex/RWKV-CLIP-B16-LAION10M, Kaichengalex/RWKV-CLIP-B32-LAION30M. Each holds a single model_31.pt (598.4 MB for B/32, 592.9 MB for B/16, fp32, both towers combined). Load with the deepglint/RWKV-CLIP repo code (model/Image_rwkv.py, model/Text_rwkv.py) plus model_config/*.json. It is not in open_clip, timm or transformers.
row.export_notes: No ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or quantized export exists anywhere I could find. There are also no mobile or CPU latency reports: the paper gives only FLOPs and an FPS/memory figure for GPUs. The repo code is hard to export. Image_rwkv.py and Text_rwkv.py JIT-compile custom CUDA WKV6 kernels with torch.utils.cpp_extension.load at import time. There is no pure-PyTorch fallback, so the code will not even import without nvcc and a GPU, despite the README's "CPU otherwise". To export you would rewrite the bidirectional WKV6 as plain tensor ops. Because the sequences are short (49 or 196 tokens), it can be written as a decay-weighted T x T matrix product, which is attention-like and exportable. Q-shift token mixing is slicing and padding, which is fine. The exp decay and data-dependent LoRA decay are fine but untested on the LiteRT GPU delegate. Size is the real blocker: an 84M image tower is about 84 MB int8, roughly 1.8x the current 46 MB, and the 65M text tower is about 65 MB int8. Accuracy is much lower than TinyCLIP-45M/32 (62.7%). Verdict: license-OK but strictly worse than the incumbent on size, accuracy and exportability. Exclude.

(b) Numbers, from paper Table 8 (arXiv HTML):

- Text params: 65.35M (4.93 GFLOPs).

I did not re-verify the linear-probe values from Table 11, the file sizes or the CUDA-kernel export claims. They are not part of the license and zero-shot check.

row.name: OpenCLIP roberta-ViT-B-32 (pretrained tag laion2b_s12b_b32k)
row.org: LAION / OpenCLIP (mlfoundations). Trained on stability.ai compute.
row.image_params_M: ~87.8M. This is the standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 visual tower: width 768, 12 layers, patch 32, 224px, 512-d projection. Computed as OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 total 151.28M minus its 63.43M text tower; the model config confirms the vision settings match. The model card gives no image-tower count. This is about 2x TinyCLIP-45M's image tower and over the ~50M target, though under the 100M ceiling.
row.text_params_M: ~124.9M. Derived as 212.72M total (openclip_results.csv) minus ~87.8M image. The text tower is HF roberta-base (50,265-token BPE vocab, about 38.6M of that is embeddings) with mean pooling and a projection to 512. It is roughly 7x TinyCLIP's 18M text tower, so the on-demand download would be large (about 125 MB at int8).
row.in1k_zeroshot: 61.71%, from open_clip docs/openclip_results.csv (ImageNet-1k column 0.6171). The HF model card says 61.7%, against 62.9% for the same B/32 baseline with the standard text tower. That is lower than TinyCLIP-45M/32's 62.7%, with a tower twice the size.
row.other_zeroshot: From openclip_results.csv: 38-dataset average 0.5411, ImageNet-v2 0.5331, ImageNet-Sketch 0.4912, ImageNet-R 0.7224, ObjectNet 0.4499, Flickr retrieval 0.7302, MSCOCO retrieval 0.4590 (CLIP_benchmark recall metric), SUN397 0.6627. The model card reports COCO 63% and Flickr30k 86.7% (baselines 60.8% / 85.4%) without saying which metric.

verdicts.corrections:
I tried to refute this row and could not. Every core claim matches the primary sources.

- **Params and compute:** docs/model_profile.csv lists both RN101 and RN101-quickgelu as 119.69M total. That splits into 56.26M image and 63.43M text. Compute is 25.5 GFLOPs total, 19.54 image and 5.96 text.
- **Zero-shot and retrieval:** docs/openclip_results.csv for the yfcc15m checkpoint gives these values.
  - RN101: ImageNet-1k 0.3407, MSCOCO 0.2404, Flickr 0.4426, 38-dataset average 0.2988.
  - RN101-quickgelu: ImageNet-1k 0.3487, MSCOCO 0.2326, Flickr 0.4422, 38-dataset average 0.2993.
- **One checkpoint:** pretrained.py has a single _RN101 dict. Its yfcc15m entry points to v0.2-weights/rn101-quickgelu-yfcc15m-3e04b30e.pt and hf_hub timm/resnet101_clip.yfcc15m, with quick_gelu=True forced.
- **License:** the open_clip LICENSE is MIT (copyright Ilharco, Wortsman, Carlini et al.).
- **HF hosting:** the timm/resnet101_clip.yfcc15m card metadata says license: mit and the repo is not gated (gated=False). The card itself is minimal. It names the dataset as YFCC-15M and says the model is called RN101-quickgelu in OpenCLIP. It adds no further restrictions, so "states no extra restrictions" really means "lists none". The repo holds both open_clip_model.safetensors (both towers) and model.safetensors (timm).
- **Not re-checked:** I did not open the immich ONNX/RKNN file sizes. They are not part of the core claims.

The YFCC Creative Commons (some NC/ND) data-provenance caveat stated in the row is correct and does not affect the weights license. Verdict stands: worse than the shipped TinyCLIP (62.7%) on accuracy, size and compute.

I could not refute the license or the numbers. Two corrections to the loading details:

(1) load_id is wrong for current open_clip main. pretrained.py registers the yfcc15m tag only under "RN101" (_PRETRAINED["RN101"] = _RN101). "RN101-quickgelu" still exists as a model config, but it has no pretrained tags. So create_model_and_transforms('RN101-quickgelu', pretrained='yfcc15m') raises RuntimeError("Pretrained value 'yfcc15m' is not a known tag..."). Use one of these instead:
- create_model_and_transforms('RN101', pretrained='yfcc15m', force_quick_gelu=True)
- 'hf-hub:timm/resnet101_clip.yfcc15m'

(2) The row says quick_gelu=True is "forced" for this tag. It is not. The tag's pretrained cfg says quick_gelu=True, but factory.py only issues a "QuickGELU mismatch" UserWarning. It does not override the model config. So plain 'RN101' + 'yfcc15m' loads with standard GELU, which explains the lower 34.07% score. Pass force_quick_gelu=True to get 34.87%.

row.name: OpenAI CLIP RN50x4 (open_clip 'RN50x4' / pretrained='openai')
row.arch: Image tower: ModifiedResNet-50x4 (CLIP ResNet with 3-conv stem, anti-aliased avgpool downsampling, AttentionPool2d head). Layers [4,6,10,6], width 80, 288x288 input, final 9x9 grid into attention pooling, 640-d embedding. Text tower: 12-layer, 640-wide, 10-head causal transformer, ctx 77, BPE vocab 49408. Config from open_clip model_configs/RN50x4.json, which matches immich-app config.json.
row.released: 2021 (CLIP paper Feb 2021; RN50x4 weights added to openai/CLIP in early 2021). Exact date not re-verified.
row.image_params_M: 87.14 (I counted this by building openai/CLIP model.py CLIP(640,288,(4,6,10,6),80,None,77,49408,640,10,12) in torch. The fp32 ONNX visual file on immich-app is 348 MB, which agrees.)
row.text_params_M: 91.16 (counted the same way; total is 178.30M, which matches open_clip results.csv 178.3. About 31.6M of the text tower is the token embedding table.)
row.image_gmacs: ~20.6 GMACs at 288px, measured with torch FlopCounterMode on the visual tower. The open_clip csv lists 51.82 GFLOPs for image+text combined. By my estimate this is roughly 5x or more the per-image compute of TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224px.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 66.27% (open_clip docs/openclip_results.csv, row RN50x4/openai, ImageNet 1k = 0.6627). Average over 38 datasets is 51.88%, IN-v2 59.4%, IN-R 72.7%, IN-Sketch 44.7%.
row.other_zeroshot: open_clip results.csv retrieval: Flickr 0.7234, MSCOCO 0.4318. The csv does not say whether these are image-to-text or text-to-image recall@5; the retrieval column definition is in that benchmark repo.
row.weights_license: MIT (openai/CLIP repo LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2021 OpenAI). The weights have no separate license file. They download from openaipublic.azureedge.net URLs hard-coded in the MIT-licensed clip.py. The immich-app/RN50x4__openai HF repo has no license tag.
row.license_notes: The code license is MIT and lets you ship commercially. The weights have no explicit license of their own; the usual reading is that MIT covers them, since the MIT repo distributes them. The official model card (openai/CLIP model-card.md) is much stricter. It calls the model a research output and says any deployed use case, commercial or not, is "currently out of scope". It also says surveillance and facial-recognition uses are always out of scope. The model card is an intended-use statement, not a license term, and is probably not legally binding. Many products already ship OpenAI CLIP weights, for example Immich (AGPL, self-hosted) through its ONNX exports. A commercial app should still have legal review this, or at least acknowledge it. Training data is OpenAI's unreleased WIT-400M. The model card says that dataset is not meant to be the basis for a commercial or deployed model, which adds a provenance caveat. Downgrade to 'yes' only if your risk tolerance accepts the MIT-only reading.
row.load_id: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('RN50x4', pretrained='openai') ; clip.load('RN50x4') in openai/CLIP ; ONNX: huggingface.co/immich-app/RN50x4__openai (visual/model.onnx, textual/model.onnx)
row.export_notes: Existing exports: immich-app/RN50x4__openai on HF has fp32 ONNX for both towers (visual 348 MB, textual 365 MB) plus RKNN builds for Rockchip NPUs (rk3566/3568/3576/3588). I found no TFLite/LiteRT export and no published Android or phone latency. A targeted search turned up nothing. Size: about 87 MB int8 or 174 MB fp16 for the image tower, against your current 46 MB. That is roughly 2x the download, near your ~100M param ceiling. Compute: about 20.6 GMACs per image vs roughly 4 for TinyCLIP 45M/32 (my estimate), so expect several times the current ~73 ms/photo on an A54. The towers are almost all plain Conv/BN/ReLU/AvgPool, which suits the GPU delegate well. The AttentionPool2d head (MHA over 82 tokens, softmax, matmul) is small and should convert, but check that it stays on the GPU delegate. Accuracy gain is only +3.6 pts IN-1k ZS (66.3 vs 62.7). Better-licensed options do better on accuracy per MB: PE-Core-S16 (72.7%) and OpenCLIP B/32 DataComp-XL (72.7%). Text tower is 91M (about 2x TinyCLIP's 18M), adding to the on-demand download. Embedding dim is 640.

It calls surveillance and facial recognition "always out-of-scope". About the WIT training data it says: "We do not intend for this dataset to be used as the basis for any commercial or deployed model". These are intended-use statements, not license terms, but together they mean commercial_ok should not be upgraded to "yes" without legal review. I did not re-fetch the IN-v2, IN-R, IN-Sketch or retrieval columns, the immich ONNX file sizes, or the 20.6 GMAC figure. All of those are plausible.

row.name: COSMOS ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 (cc3m / cc12m / yfcc15m / merged30m / pixelprose), CVPR 2025
row.org: ExplainableML (Univ. of Tuebingen / TUM / Helmholtz Munich, Akata lab)
row.arch: A standard OpenCLIP ViT-B dual encoder, from the repo's src/open_clip/model_configs. Image tower: ViT-B, 12 layers, width 768, patch 16 (196 tokens) or patch 32 (49 tokens), 224px. Text tower: 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408, embed_dim 512. Training adds cross-attention pooling modules and an EMA teacher, but inference does not use them: zero_shot.py scores plain image_features @ text_features, so a normal CLIP-style shared embedding exists. The HF repo also has ViT-B/32 checkpoints, which the hint omitted.
row.image_params_M: About 86 (ViT-B/16) and about 88 (ViT-B/32). These are not stated by the authors. They are standard OpenCLIP ViT-B-16/B-32 counts (open_clip model profile), inferred from the identical config. Either way the image tower is close to the 100M ceiling and about 2x TinyCLIP-45M.
row.text_params_M: About 63 (standard OpenCLIP 12L/512w text tower, inferred from the config, not stated by the authors)
row.image_gmacs: About 17.5 (B/16) and about 4.4 (B/32) at 224px. These are the standard OpenCLIP ViT-B profile figures, not reported for COSMOS.
row.in1k_zeroshot: From the GitHub README table, which matches the paper. B/16: cc3m 37.1, cc12m 51.4, yfcc15m 52.4, merged30m 57.6, pixelprose 59.6. B/32: cc3m 33.0, cc12m 46.7, yfcc15m 48.1, merged30m 53.4, pixelprose 54.3. Every variant is below TinyCLIP-45M/32 (62.7).
row.other_zeroshot: README table, R@1, I2T/T2I. B/16 merged30m: COCO 68.0/52.5, Flickr 92.9/80.3. B/16 pixelprose: COCO 62.4/43.4, Flickr 89.9/73.6. B/32 merged30m: COCO 64.3/48.4, Flickr 89.9/76.1. B/32 pixelprose: COCO 57.2/38.9, Flickr 85.6/66.3. Retrieval is strong, well above OpenCLIP models trained on similar data, thanks to training on long synthetic recaptions. The paper also reports zero-shot semantic segmentation.
row.weights_license: MIT (HF model card metadata and tag on sankim2/cosmos only; there is no LICENSE file in the HF repo)
row.license_notes: 1) The weights carry MIT only through the HF YAML front-matter tag (license: mit). The HF repo has no LICENSE file, and the card text adds no use restrictions. 2) The GitHub code repo has no license: the GitHub API returns license null, and the tree has no LICENSE file. Strictly, the training/inference code is all-rights-reserved. Most of it is a fork of OpenCLIP (MIT), which you could use directly instead, since the architecture is plain OpenCLIP ViT-B. 3) Training-data caveats. Merged30M = CC3M + CC12M + YFCC15M with DreamLIP long recaptions; the HF dataset card says cc-by-4.0, but the captions were generated by MLLMs (InstructBLIP, LLaVA-1.5, ShareGPT4V), and the images are web-scraped with unknown or mixed licenses. PixelProse is cc-by-4.0 on HF, but its captions come from Google Gemini, whose output terms may restrict using outputs to build competing models. That one is a legal judgment call, not a clear blocker. 4) The paper is CC BY 4.0 on arXiv. Net: the weights tag says MIT, but the authors never gave an explicit LICENSE grant, and the code is unlicensed. Asking the authors (sankim2) for a LICENSE file would make this a clean yes. The license question is moot anyway, because the model is weaker on IN-1k and about 2x bigger than the current TinyCLIP.
row.load_id: HF sankim2/cosmos, files cosmos_vitb16_{cc3m,cc12m,yfcc15m,merged30m,pixelprose}.pt and cosmos_vitb32_{...}.pt. Load with the repo's modified open_clip (--model ViT-B-16|ViT-B-32 --output-all --attentional-pool --cosmos). These are not open_clip hub-registered pretrained tags. To get vanilla open_clip ViT-B-16/32 weights, strip the student visual/text keys.
row.export_notes: No ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or mobile latency reports found (web search plus repo issues #1-3, which cover only finetuning, training speed and webdataset). The HF config.json is an empty {}. Each .pt is about 2.44 GB (B/16) or about 2.47 GB (B/32), far more than a 150M-param fp32 model (about 0.6 GB), so the files probably hold teacher + student + cross-attn modules and/or optimizer state. You would have to extract the student's visual and text towers yourself. The inference graph is a vanilla ViT-B plus a CLIP text transformer (LayerNorm, GELU, MHA), with no exotic ops, so the standard OpenCLIP-to-ONNX/LiteRT (ai-edge-torch) path should work and the graph should be GPU-delegate friendly. int8 B/32 would be about 88 MB and B/16 about 86 MB, roughly 2x the current 46 MB. Expected latency is above TinyCLIP-45M/32: B/32 at about 4.4 GMACs is comparable in FLOPs, but B/16 at about 17.5 GMACs is about 4x. Verdict: not an upgrade. Its IN-1k ZS (best 59.6) is below the current model and the tower is bigger. Its only advantage is retrieval for long, descriptive queries.
row.released: arXiv v1 2024-12-02 (v2 2025-03-26); GitHub repo created 2024-12-02; HF weights uploaded 2025-03-20 (last modified 2025-03-27); CVPR 2025

row.name: OpenCLIP CoCa ViT-B/32 (coca_ViT-B-32, pretrained laion2b_s13b_b90k), using only the contrastive towers and dropping the caption decoder
row.org: LAION / mlfoundations OpenCLIP (trained by iejMac; CoCa code by lucidrains and gpucce)
row.arch: The image tower is ViT-B/32 (12 layers, width 768, patch 32) at 224px, which gives 49 patch tokens plus CLS. Instead of CLS or mean pooling it uses an attentional pooler: cross-attention with 8 heads and learned queries (256 by default in open_clip), and the first pooled query is projected to a 512-d embedding. The text tower is a 12-layer, width-512, 8-head causal transformer. It has embed_cls=true, so a learned CLS token is appended to the 76-token context, and it uses the CLIP BPE vocabulary of 49408. The multimodal caption decoder (12 layers, width 512) is roughly 101M params and is not needed for embeddings. The source is the coca_ViT-B-32.json config in the open_clip repo.
row.image_params_M: 89.16 (open_clip docs/model_profile.csv image_mparams). For comparison, plain ViT-B-32 is 87.85; the difference is the attentional pooler.
row.text_params_M: 63.43 (open_clip docs/model_profile.csv text_mparams). The total of 253.56M also includes about 101M of caption decoder, which is not needed here.
row.image_gmacs: 9.19 'GFLOPs' image tower according to open_clip model_profile.csv. open_clip's profiler counts one multiply-add as one op, so this is effectively about 9.2 GMACs. The text tower is 5.96. For comparison, plain ViT-B-32 is 8.82.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 63.31% (0.6331), from the open_clip docs/openclip_results.csv row coca_ViT-B-32 / laion2b_s13b_b90k. The HF model card reports no numbers because its README is empty. For context, this is only +0.6 pt over the current TinyCLIP-45M/32 (62.7%) at about 2x the image-tower size. It is below plain OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 laion2b_s34b_b79k (66.6%) and ViT-B-32 DataComp-XL (72.7%), which have the same ~88M image tower without the pooler.
row.other_zeroshot: These figures come from openclip_results.csv for laion2b_s13b_b90k. Flickr retrieval score 0.7248; MSCOCO retrieval score 0.4537; average over the 38-dataset suite 0.5533; WinoGAViL 0.4698. The mscoco_finetuned variant is caption-only and its contrastive embedding is broken: IN1k ZS 0.79% and average 0.1108. Do not use it for embeddings.
row.weights_license: MIT. The HF repo laion/CoCa-ViT-B-32-laion2B-s13B-b90k has cardData license: mit and the tag license:mit. The open_clip code LICENSE file is also MIT (Copyright Ilharco, Wortsman, Carlini, et al.).
row.license_notes: The weights host and the code repo give the same license, MIT, with no difference between them. The HF model card README is empty (21 bytes), so it adds no use restrictions. This differs from the LAION CLIP ViT model cards, which carry the 'deployed use cases out of scope' research disclaimer. The open_clip README states no license or intended-use terms for pretrained weights. Its only caveats are that parts of the modelling and tokenizer code are adapted from OpenAI CLIP (MIT) and that it asks for a citation. The training data was LAION-2B-en (13B samples seen, batch 90k), which carries a data provenance caveat. LAION withdrew LAION-5B in Dec 2023 after the Stanford CSAM-link report and re-released it as Re-LAION-5B in 2024. This checkpoint (uploaded Dec 2022) was trained on the original version. MIT does not restrict this, but some legal and compliance teams flag LAION-trained weights. The data is web-scraped and has no data license of its own.
row.load_id: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('coca_ViT-B-32', pretrained='laion2b_s13b_b90k'), which maps to hf-hub:laion/CoCa-ViT-B-32-laion2B-s13B-b90k per the open_clip pretrained.py _coca_VITB32 entry. Use model.encode_image / model.encode_text and ignore model.text_decoder.
row.released: 2022-12-20 (HF repo created). Last modified 2023-01-29.
row.export_notes: The only file is the PyTorch pickle open_clip_pytorch_model.bin, 1,014,488,932 bytes (~1.01 GB fp32). That one file holds the image tower, the text tower and the caption decoder, so the text tower is released, just not as a separate file. I found no ONNX, TFLite, LiteRT or CoreML export of this CoCa checkpoint and no mobile latency report. Immich and community LiteRT exports exist for plain ViT-B-32 checkpoints, not for CoCa. One community LiteRT ViT-B/32 image encoder (mlboydaisuke/clip-vit-b32-litert) reports about 40 ms per image on a Pixel 8a GPU, which is a rough proxy since FLOPs are about 4% higher here. Every op is standard (LayerNorm, MHA self-attention, plus a single cross-attention pooler with learned queries and GELU), so export through litert-torch/ai-edge-torch or ONNX should be straightforward. Two export cautions: the pooler's MultiheadAttention must be exported with fixed shapes, and the text tower appends a CLS token (embed_cls) and pools from it, not from the EOT argmax like plain CLIP, so the on-device tokenizer and pooling must match. Estimated download sizes: about 89 MB int8 / 178 MB fp16 for the image tower, versus 46 MB int8 for the current tower, and about 63 MB int8 for the text tower. Verdict: it is dominated. It is about 2x the current image tower for +0.6 pt IN1k ZS, while plain OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 (same size, MIT) scores 66.6–72.7%.

row.license_notes:
- **Code vs weights:** The GitHub repo's MIT license covers the code. It does not clearly cover the HF-hosted text weights. The weights repo has no license metadata and the card has no license section, and no use restrictions are stated either way.
- **Base model:** XLM-RoBERTa-Large is MIT on HF (FacebookAI/xlm-roberta-large).
- **Training data:** About 7M CC3M+CC12M+SBU captions (the BLIP ViT-L-filtered set), machine-translated into 48 languages with Opus-MT models. These were published as the HF dataset M-CLIP/ImageCaptions-7M-Translations, which also carries no license tag. The source caption datasets have their own terms (CC12M, for example, has its own license terms that may restrict use).
- **Image tower:** Trained on LAION-400M (the usual web-scrape data caveat). The weights themselves are MIT.
- **Bottom line:** Commercial use is plausible but not documented for the text tower. Treat it as unclear until the author confirms. The image tower alone is MIT.
row.arch:
- **Image tower:** OpenCLIP ViT-B-16-plus-240, a ViT with width 896, 12 layers, patch 16, input 240px. That gives 15x15 = 225 patch tokens + CLS. The embedding dim is 640.
- **Text tower:** XLM-RoBERTa-Large (24 layers, hidden 1024, 250k SentencePiece vocab), mean-pooled, then a linear 1024->640 layer ("SentenceModelWithLinearTransformation", numDims 640). It was trained by distilling the original OpenCLIP B-16+ text embeddings on machine-translated captions only. It covers 48 languages plus English.
row.image_gmacs: About 54.8. open_clip model_profile.csv lists 54.76 image GFLOPs. Its profiler (fvcore-style) counts one multiply-add as one FLOP, so this figure is effectively GMACs, but that is not confirmed. For the whole model it lists 64.03 GFLOPs, of which the original text tower is 9.27.

- **Image:** open_clip `create_model_and_transforms('ViT-B-16-plus-240', pretrained='laion400m_e32')`. The weights come from the GitHub release vit_b_16_plus_240-laion400m_e32-699c4b84.pt. On HF there is timm/vit_base_patch16_plus_clip_240.laion400m_e31. Note that open_clip's pretrained.py points e32's hf_hub at the e31 repo.
row.export_notes:
- **Existing exports:**
  - The immich-app/XLM-Roberta-Large-Vit-B-16Plus repo on HF has ONNX for both towers: visual/model.onnx at 469 MB fp32, and textual as ONNX with external weight files, about 2.2 GB. It also has Rockchip RKNN builds: about 245 MB visual and about 1.13 GB textual.
  - No TFLite/LiteRT or CoreML export was found, and no mobile phone latency report.
  - clip-as-service benchmark (server GPU): 4293 MB on disk, text 662 QPS, image 236 QPS.
- **Image tower on mobile:** It is a plain ViT and should convert cleanly (standard ops: GELU, LayerNorm, MHA). But it has about 2.6x the params of TinyCLIP-45M, so int8 is about 118 MB, and about 55 GFLOPs at 240px against TinyCLIP's few GFLOPs. Expect several times the current 73 ms on an A54.

Existing exports from immich-app/ViT-B-16__laion400m_e32: separate visual and textual fp32 ONNX (345 MB / 254 MB), fp16 ArmNN (173 MB / 127 MB), and RKNN for Rockchip NPUs. There is no TFLite export and no Android TFLite latency report for this checkpoint. The architecture is plain ViT-B/16 (LayerNorm, GELU, MHA), which converts to LiteRT cleanly and runs on the GPU delegate. The nearest reference is Qualcomm AI Hub's OpenAI-CLIP ViT-B/16 TFLite (same architecture, different weights): 12.8-17 ms on the Snapdragon 8 Elite (Galaxy) NPU, but that figure is for the full model on an NPU, not a mid-range CPU or GPU. Arm's int8 LiteRT ViT-B/16 (an ImageNet classifier, not CLIP) reports about 54 ms p50 at 1 thread on a recent flagship. Estimated cost on a Galaxy A54: about 4x the MACs of the current 45M/32 tower, so expect roughly 250-350 ms per photo on CPU (unverified estimate). An int8 image tower would be about 87 MB versus 46 MB today. Verdict: commercially clean, +4.4 IN-1k points over TinyCLIP 45M/32, but it is about 2x the download and about 4x the compute. That is worse on both counts than OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 DataComp-XL (72.7%, MIT, about 88M image params but only about 4.4 GMACs).

row.arch: OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 image tower (12 layers, width 768, patch 16, 224px gives 196 patch tokens + CLS) and OpenCLIP text transformer (12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408), embed_dim 512, with sigmoid-style logit_bias. On top sits a text-conditioned attention pooling block (PureAttentionPoolingBlock, the 'visual_proj') over local image tokens. A global CLS-based embedding (image_post/text_post, the get_logits_as_clip path) also works without text conditioning, so precomputed image vectors are possible. The fine-grained FLAIR scoring needs the local tokens plus the text at query time.
row.image_params_M: ~86 (computed by me from config ViT-B-16-FLAIR.json, since the paper and card give no count: standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 visual is about 86.2M including the 768x512 proj, plus a small image_post head). Above the ~50M target and near the 100M ceiling. Int8 would be about 86-90 MB, roughly 2x the current 46 MB.
row.text_params_M: ~63 (computed from config: OpenCLIP B/16 text tower, width 512 x 12 layers, ctx 77, vocab 49408, about 63.4M), plus about 1M for the attention-pooling block. Total model about 150M.
row.image_gmacs: ~17.6 GMACs at 224px (standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 image figure, not reported by FLAIR). About 4x ViT-B/32 / TinyCLIP-45M/32 compute.
row.in1k_zeroshot: Merged-30M: 56.6%. CC3M-recap: 33.8%. Source: paper arXiv 2412.03561, Table 4, ViT-B/16, 7 CLIP prompt templates. The paper gives no IN number for the CC12M-recap and YFCC15M-recap checkpoints. Best variant is about 6 points below TinyCLIP-45M/32's 62.7%. The paper itself says it lags billion-scale CLIPs by about 20% on classification.
row.other_zeroshot: Merged-30M (paper Table 1): COCO T2I R@1 53.3, I2T 68.0; Flickr30k T2I 81.1, I2T 94.7. These beat OpenCLIP-2B B/16 (41.7/59.3/71.9/87.5) and SigLIP B/16 (47.2/65.5/75.6/89.1). The retrieval numbers likely use FLAIR's text-conditioned pooling, so the global-only path will be somewhat lower; the paper reports no separate global-only number here. Table 4 average over 11 classification sets: 56.8 (Merged-30M), with weak fine-grained classes (Cars 31.1, Aircraft 7.2, Flowers 48.4, Pets 55.6). Strong on long-caption retrieval (DOCCI, Urban-1K) and zero-shot segmentation. GitHub README table for cc3m-recap: COCO T2I 37.7 / I2T 51.6.
row.weights_license: MIT (Hugging Face model card YAML 'license: mit' on xiaorui638/flair). No LICENSE file exists in the HF repo or in the GitHub repo.
row.license_notes: Weights host xiaorui638/flair (HF) declares MIT only through card metadata. Repo files are .gitattributes, README.md, an empty config.json ({}), and 4 .pt files; there is no LICENSE text. GitHub ExplainableML/flair has no LICENSE file: the GitHub API license field is null and the root holds only .gitignore, README.md, assets, datasets, preprocess, src. The README states no license, so the code is all-rights-reserved by default even though it derives from OpenCLIP (MIT). The model card adds no use restrictions. Training data is DreamLIP recaptions (HF qidouxiong619/dreamlip_long_captions, CC-BY-4.0 for URLs + captions; 'individual images are under their own copyrights') of CC3M/CC12M/YFCC15M. The captions were generated by ShareGPT4V / InstructBLIP / LLaVA-1.5, whose own output terms may carry non-commercial or OpenAI-derived caveats. The MIT tag is a reasonable basis for weights use, but with no LICENSE file and no code license I rate commercial use unclear-to-probably-OK. Ask the authors to add a LICENSE before relying on it.
row.load_id: HF xiaorui638/flair, files flair-merged30m.pt | flair-cc3m-recap.pt | flair-cc12m-recap.pt | flair-yfcc15m-recap.pt (about 1.81 GB each; probably full training checkpoints, so fp32 weights alone are about 600 MB). Load with the repo's own package: `flair.create_model_and_transforms('ViT-B-16-FLAIR', pretrained=flair.download_weights_from_hf('xiaorui638/flair','flair-merged30m.pt'))`. Not in upstream open_clip, timm or transformers. The image tower is a vanilla OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 visual, so its state_dict should load into open_clip 'ViT-B-16' visual with key remapping.
row.export_notes: No existing ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or mobile export found, and no mobile latency report. Both towers are plain OpenCLIP ViT/transformer blocks: global path is CLS -> image_post, EOT -> text_post. They should convert like any ViT-B/16 (litert-torch / ai-edge-torch or ONNX) with no exotic ops. The text-conditioned attention pooling is a small MHA. Exporting it separately would let you rerank top-k with local tokens, but that needs 196x512 stored per photo, which is impractical; for this app use the global embedding only. Expected cost: ViT-B/16 at 224 is about 17.6 GMACs vs about 4.4 for B/32. On an A54-class device that is likely several hundred ms per photo on CPU, roughly 4x the current 73 ms (estimate, not measured). Int8 image tower about 87 MB vs 46 MB today. Text tower is OpenCLIP 77-token, same tokenizer as today's pipeline.
row.released: arXiv Dec 2024 (2412.03561); HF weights created 2024-12-16, last modified 2025-03-06; CVPR 2025
sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.03561 (Table 1 retrieval, Table 4 zero-shot classification incl. ImageNet)

row.name: COSMOS ViT-B/32 (cc3m / cc12m / yfcc15m / merged30m / pixelprose)
row.org: ExplainableML / EML Munich, TUM / Helmholtz (Kim, Xiao, Georgescu, Alaniz, Akata). CVPR 2025
row.image_params_M: ~87.8M (computed from the repo's config, not stated by the authors). src/open_clip/model_configs/ViT-B-32.json is the standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/32: width 768, 12 layers, patch 32, 224px. That is the same tower as OpenAI CLIP B/32, and the cross-attention module is training-only.
row.text_params_M: ~63.4M (computed from the config: width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408, embed_dim 512). This is the standard CLIP text transformer, and about 25M of it is the token embedding table.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 53.4% (merged30m) and 54.3% (pixelprose), both from paper Tables 11 and 13 (arXiv 2412.01814) and the GitHub README. The other ViT-B/32 results are 33.0 (cc3m), 46.7 (cc12m) and 48.1 (yfcc15m). For comparison, ViT-B/16 reaches 57.6 (merged30m) and 59.6 (pixelprose). Every variant is below TinyCLIP-45M/32's 62.7%, and so is the OpenCLIP LAION-400M B/32 (60.2) listed in the same table.
row.other_zeroshot: ViT-B/32 retrieval R@1 (paper Tables 10 and 12), as Flickr30K I2T/T2I then MSCOCO I2T/T2I: merged30m 89.9/76.1 and 64.3/48.4; yfcc15m 90.2/73.3 and 64.5/46.0; cc12m 86.5/69.8 and 59.6/43.0; cc3m 74.3/59.2 and 47.6/33.5; pixelprose 85.6/66.3 and 57.2/38.9. Retrieval is strong for the data scale because the models are trained on long recaptions, and it beats CLIP/SigLIP trained on the same data. The paper also reports zero-shot semantic segmentation.
row.weights_license: MIT, declared only as a Hugging Face metadata tag (license: mit) on sankim2/cosmos. Neither the HF repo nor GitHub has a LICENSE file.
row.license_notes: 1) The weights host sankim2/cosmos has the YAML tag license: mit. It is the only license statement anywhere, and there is no LICENSE text. The model card adds no use restrictions. 2) The GitHub repo ExplainableML/cosmos has no license: the GitHub API returns license null and the tree has no LICENSE file. The code is therefore all-rights-reserved by default, although it is a fork of OpenCLIP (MIT). This matters little, because the app would load the weights with stock open_clip ViT-B-32 code. 3) The arXiv paper is CC BY 4.0, which covers the paper only. 4) Data caveats: the cc3m/cc12m/yfcc15m "recap" sets are DreamLIP's MLLM-generated recaptions, and PixelProse captions were generated with Gemini. The underlying images (CC3M, CC12M, YFCC15M) carry mixed web and CC licenses. These are the same kind of caveats as most CLIP data and are not restrictions on the weights. Verdict: the uploader declares MIT, so commercial use is probably fine. But it rests on a metadata tag alone, with unlicensed code and no license text, so I marked it unclear rather than yes. Practically this does not matter: the model is bigger than TinyCLIP (88M image tower vs 45M) and worse on ImageNet zero-shot (53-54% vs 62.7%), so it should not be adopted.
sources: https://github.com/ExplainableML/cosmos (README table; GitHub API reports license=null; no LICENSE file in the tree)
https://huggingface.co/sankim2/cosmos (cardData license: mit; files listed via the HF API)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01814 (Tables 10-13; App. C.2: the cross-attention module is not used at inference)
row.arch: Standard OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 image encoder: 224px, patch 32, 49 tokens plus CLS, width 768, 12 layers. It is paired with a 12-layer, width-512 CLIP text transformer (77 tokens) and a 512-d shared embedding. Training adds a cross-attention module plus a momentum teacher for self-distillation, with multi-crop images and sampled caption crops. Inference uses only the image CLS and the text EOT token, so the deployed graph is plain CLIP ViT-B/32. The inference script passes --cosmos --attentional-pool, which needs checking before export.
row.image_gmacs: ~4.4 GMACs, estimated from the standard OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 profile (4.41 G). The authors do not report it.
row.load_id: open_clip model 'ViT-B-32' using checkpoint file cosmos_vitb32_{cc3m|cc12m|yfcc15m|merged30m|pixelprose}.pt from HF repo sankim2/cosmos. Loading goes through the repo's fork with --huggingface-repo-name sankim2/cosmos --huggingface-model-name <file> --cosmos, or by pulling the student weights out of the checkpoint into stock open_clip. There is no open_clip pretrained tag and no HF transformers integration, even though the card is tagged transformers.
row.released: December 2024 (arXiv 2412.01814; repo created 2024-12-02, last push 2025-03-27). Published at CVPR 2025.
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export and no mobile latency report. Each released .pt is about 2.47 GB, while fp32 ViT-B/32 image plus text is about 0.6 GB. The size suggests the files are full training checkpoints (student, teacher, cross-attention and possibly optimizer state), so the student state_dict has to be extracted. Once extracted, the graph is vanilla CLIP ViT-B/32, which converts cleanly to TFLite with ai-edge-torch, the same path as any OpenCLIP B/32. An int8 image tower would be about 88 MB, roughly 2x the current 46 MB. Latency should be about 2x TinyCLIP-45M/32 on device, since GMACs are about 2x at the same 49-token count. That is my estimate, not a measurement.

verdicts.corrections:
I could not refute the row. Everything I checked matches it.
- License: The HF API for sankim2/cosmos returns cardData license "mit", gated=false and the tag license:mit. The HF README contains only that YAML tag, a description and a citation, with no use restrictions and no LICENSE file; the repo's only files are .gitattributes, README.md, config.json and 10 .pt files. On GitHub, LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, LICENSE.md and COPYING on the main branch all return 404, and the repo page shows no license badge. So the claim of MIT by metadata tag only, with unlicensed code, holds, and commercial_ok "unclear" is the right call.
- One extra caveat to add: the DreamLIP recaptions behind the cc3m/cc12m/yfcc15m sets were produced with MLLMs such as LLaVA/InstructBLIP/ShareGPT4V, and PixelProse captions were produced with Gemini. Those models' output terms are a provenance caveat, not a restriction on the weights.
- Params: The repo's ViT-B-32.json is embed 512; vision width 768, 12 layers, patch 32, 224px; text width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408. That is the standard OpenCLIP B/32: about 87.8M image and 63.4M text, with a token embedding of 49408x512, about 25.3M. Correct.
- ImageNet zero-shot: The GitHub README table matches the row for ViT-B/32: cc3m 33.0, cc12m 46.7, yfcc15m 48.1, merged30m 53.4, pixelprose 54.3. The COCO/Flickr R@1 figures also match. All are below TinyCLIP's 62.7.
- Size: HF usedStorage is about 24.5 GB across 10 checkpoints, about 2.45 GB each, which supports the "full training checkpoint" note.
- Inference script: inference_classification.sh does pass --attentional-pool --cosmos, as the row notes.
- Minor date fix: the HF repo was created 2025-03-20 and last modified 2025-03-27. I could not check the GitHub creation date because the GitHub API was rate-limited.

I could not refute the row. Everything checked matches it.

License:
- The HF API for sankim2/cosmos returns cardData.license = "mit" and the tag "license:mit". The model is not gated (gated: false), and the card text adds no use restrictions.
- There is no LICENSE file on HF (resolve/main/LICENSE returns 404). There is none on GitHub either: raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and license on ExplainableML/cosmos main.
- The README has no license section.
- I could not re-check the claim that the GitHub API returns license=null, because the API rate-limited me. The missing LICENSE files are consistent with it.
- So the bare MIT metadata tag is the only grant. That supports commercial_ok = "unclear", which here means NOT confirmed commercially safe. Treat it as false for adoption unless the authors confirm MIT in writing or a LICENSE file is added.

Numbers:
- The README table gives these ViT-B/32 IN-1k zero-shot results: cc3m 33.0, cc12m 46.7, yfcc15m 48.1, merged30m 53.4, pixelprose 54.3. The retrieval R@1 values match the row exactly.
- The repo's ViT-B-32.json is width 768, 12 layers, patch 32, 224px, with text width 512, 12 layers, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408 and embed 512. My own parameter count gives 87.85M image and 63.43M text, which matches the row's ~87.8M and ~63.4M.

Two small notes:
- inference_classification.sh does pass --cosmos and --attentional-pool, so check the deployed pooling path before export, as the row already says.
- The HF repo holds 10 .pt files totalling about 24.5 GB (usedStorage 24,518,995,506 bytes), about 2.45 GB per file. That is consistent with full training checkpoints.

row.name: Marqo-FashionSigLIP
row.arch: SigLIP ViT-B/16 image tower (timm vit_base_patch16_siglip_224, MAP-pooled, no CLS), patch 16, 196 tokens at 224px; text tower is a 12-layer, 768-wide transformer with 12 heads, a 32k SentencePiece vocab, 64-token context and a 768-d shared embedding. Fine-tuned from ViT-B-16-SigLIP (WebLI) with Marqo's Generalised Contrastive Learning on fashion product data.
row.image_params_M: ~93M, computed by me: fp32 onnx/vision_model.onnx is 371.7 MB / 4 bytes = ~92.9M. That matches standard SigLIP-B/16 (~86M plus the MAP head). It is under the 100M ceiling but nearly 2x the current TinyCLIP 45M image tower.
row.text_params_M: ~110M, computed by me: fp32 onnx/text_model.onnx is 441.4 MB / 4 = ~110M, about 24.6M of which is token embeddings. The full open_clip safetensors is 812.66 MB, so ~203M in total, which agrees.
row.image_gmacs: ~17.6 GMACs at 224px (my estimate for a standard ViT-B/16 at 224px with 196 tokens; not stated by Marqo)
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported. The model card and GitHub report only fashion retrieval metrics. The base ViT-B-16-SigLIP (WebLI) gets about 76.2% in the OpenCLIP results, but that is the base model, not this fine-tune. A fashion-domain fine-tune is likely to lose some general-domain zero-shot accuracy; that is unmeasured.
row.other_zeroshot: Only fashion benchmarks, from the model card averaged over 6 datasets (Atlas, DeepFashion In-shop/Multimodal, Fashion200k, KAGL, Polyvore). Text-to-image: AvgRecall 0.231, R@1 0.121, R@10 0.340, MRR 0.239 (base ViT-B-16-SigLIP-webli: 0.212 / 0.111 / 0.314 / 0.214). Category-to-product: AvgP 0.737 (base 0.688). Sub-category-to-product: AvgP 0.725 (base 0.643). No COCO or Flickr retrieval is reported. The card also mentions a newer "Marqo Fashion SigLIP 2", but only as "contact Marqo"; no open weights were found.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0
row.license_notes: The HF model card YAML says license: apache-2.0, and the card adds no extra use restrictions. The weights repo has no separate LICENSE file (/raw/main/LICENSE returns "Entry not found"), so the license rests on the card metadata. The GitHub repo marqo-ai/marqo-FashionCLIP has an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file (GitHub API confirms the SPDX ID). The code and weights licenses therefore match. The base model, Google's ViT-B-16-SigLIP (WebLI), is Apache-2.0. Caveat: the fine-tuning data is not listed on the card (only the eval datasets are). The datasets Marqo re-hosts on HF, such as DeepFashion, carry their own original terms, but those are eval data, not the weights license.
row.load_id: open_clip: 'hf-hub:Marqo/marqo-fashionSigLIP'; HF transformers: AutoModel.from_pretrained('Marqo/marqo-fashionSigLIP', trust_remote_code=True); transformers.js: SiglipVisionModel / SiglipTextModel from 'Marqo/marqo-fashionSigLIP'
row.export_notes: Official split ONNX exports for transformers.js are in the HF repo under onnx/. Vision: fp32 371.7 MB, fp16 185.9 MB, int8/uint8/quantized 94.0 MB, q4 61.2 MB, q4f16 53.7 MB, bnb4 55.4 MB. Text: fp32 441.4 MB, fp16 220.8 MB, int8 111.1 MB, q4f16 108.9 MB. No TFLite/LiteRT export and no mobile latency report were found. It is a plain ViT-B/16 plus MAP attention-pool head (GELU, LayerNorm, MHA), which is GPU-delegate friendly and converts like other SigLIP-B models (e.g. via ai-edge-torch). The int8 image tower would be ~94 MB vs 46 MB today, and at ~4x TinyCLIP-45M/32's compute (16-px patches, 196 vs 49 tokens) expect several times the 73 ms/photo latency on an A54 (my estimate, not measured). The text tower and download are also large: ~111 MB int8, 64-token context. It is a fashion-domain fine-tune, so it is a poor fit for general photo tagging and search. Listed for completeness, not recommended.
row.released: 2024-08-09 (HF repo created; last modified 2026-02-18)

row.name: Long-CLIP-B (LongCLIP-B)
row.org: Beichen Zhang et al. (Shanghai AI Lab / SJTU), ECCV 2024
row.arch: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 image tower (patch 16, 196+1 tokens at 224px, width 768, 12 layers), unchanged. Text tower is the CLIP transformer (width 512, 12 layers) with positional embedding stretched from 77 to 248 tokens: the first 20 positions are kept and the other 57 are interpolated x4. Fine-tuned 1 epoch on ShareGPT4V long captions, with primary-component matching (PCA top-32) used for short-caption alignment.
row.image_params_M: ~86 (my calculation, not stated by the authors: the standard OpenAI ViT-B/16 visual tower is ~86.2M and Long-CLIP leaves it unchanged. The single checkpoint longclip-B.pt is 599,433,439 bytes fp32, about 149.9M params total, which fits ~86M image + ~63.5M text)
row.text_params_M: ~63.5 (my calculation: the OpenAI CLIP B text tower is ~63.4M, plus about 0.09M from the extra 171x512 positional rows. It includes a 25.3M token-embedding table)
row.image_gmacs: ~17.6 G at 224px (standard ViT-B/16 figure from open_clip's fvcore profile, which counts MACs. Not measured on this checkpoint)
row.in1k_zeroshot: 66.8% (Long-CLIP paper arXiv 2403.15378, Table 3, B/16). The base OpenAI CLIP B/16 scores 68.4% in the same table, so the fine-tune loses 1.6 points. IN-V2 61.2, IN-O 42.7, C10 90.7, C100 69.3.
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 2, B/16: COCO2017 5k I2T R@1 57.6 / T2I R@1 40.4 (base CLIP 51.8 / 32.7). Flickr30k full I2T R@1 46.8 / T2I R@1 34.1 (base CLIP 44.1 / 24.7). Long-caption retrieval (Urban-1k, ShareGPT4V-1k) is much better than base CLIP.
row.weights_license: Apache-2.0 tag on HF (BeichenZhang/LongCLIP-B, cardData license: apache-2.0). The GitHub repo LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 too. Two upstream sources carry restrictions: the OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 base weights and the CC-BY-NC-4.0 ShareGPT4V training captions.
row.license_notes:
The weights repo and code repo are both tagged Apache-2.0. The HF model card is empty: its README.md is 31 bytes, so it adds no restrictions of its own. It is a derivative with risks, though:
(1) The training captions are ShareGPT4V-PT, file share-captioner_coco_lcs_sam_1246k_1107.json. The dataset card licenses them CC-BY-NC-4.0, says they "should abide by the policy of OpenAI" terms of use, and names research as the primary intended use. The train.md image list also marks the WebData images "Only for academic usage".
(2) The base model is OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16. Its code is MIT, but the OpenAI model card says "Any deployed use case of the model - whether commercial or not - is currently out of scope". This is the same caveat that applies to every OpenAI-CLIP-derived model.
Whether an NC dataset license reaches the trained weights is legally unsettled. Treat it as high-risk for a shipped commercial app. Prefer models trained on permissively licensed data.
row.load_id: HF BeichenZhang/LongCLIP-B, file longclip-B.pt (599 MB, fp32, a single combined image+text checkpoint). Load it with the repo's own loader (`from model import longclip; longclip.load('./checkpoints/longclip-B.pt')`, github.com/beichenzbc/Long-CLIP). It is not a native open_clip or timm id. Some HF-transformers community conversions exist, but I did not verify them.
row.export_notes:
I found no official or community TFLite/LiteRT, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. The architecture is a plain OpenAI-CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU, standard MHA, LayerNorm), so the export path should match OpenAI CLIP B/16 (PyTorch -> ONNX or ai-edge-torch -> TFLite). The text side has a 248-length causal mask and positional embedding.
Expected costs versus the current TinyCLIP-45M/32: about 2x the image params, about 4x the tokens (196 vs 49) and roughly 4-5x the image MACs (~17.6G). Expect several times the ~73 ms/photo on an A54 and an int8 image tower of ~87 MB. The text tower is ~63.5M params (~64 MB int8).
It exceeds the ~50M target and sits near the ~100M ceiling. IN zero-shot is 66.8% versus the current 62.7%. Its real advantage is long free-text queries (248 tokens).
row.released: 2024-03 (HF repo created 2024-03-22, last modified 2024-09-30; arXiv 2403.15378; ECCV 2024)

row.name: TULIP-B-16-224 (SL1 and SL2 checkpoints)
row.org: UC Berkeley (tulip-berkeley; Zineng Tang et al.)
row.arch: A SigLIP-style ViT-B/16 built with timm 'vit_base_patch16_siglip_224': 224px input, 196 patch tokens, no CLS token, MAP attention-pool head, no projection layer, 768-d embedding. The text tower is a 12-layer, 768-wide, 12-head transformer with no causal mask, last-token pooling, a projection with bias, context length 64 and a 109,871-token GemmaTokenizer (HF repo ZinengTang/tulip-tokenizer). The model uses a sigmoid loss with logit bias init -15. Per the paper, the training-time extras (MAE-style image decoder, T5-based text decoder, image-image and text-text projection heads) are not needed for inference.
row.image_params_M: ~92.9M, computed from the config because the paper does not state it: patch embed 0.59M + pos 0.15M + 12 blocks x 7.09M + MAP head 7.09M. That matches timm's known 92.9M for vit_base_patch16_siglip_224 and is about 2x the current TinyCLIP 45M image tower.
row.text_params_M: ~170.1M, computed from the config: token embedding 109,871x768 = 84.4M + 12 blocks x 7.09M = 85.1M + projection 0.59M + pos/LN. Roughly half of it is the vocabulary table.
row.image_gmacs: ~17.7 GMACs, my own estimate computed from the config (12 blocks x ~1.45 GMAC + patch embed + MAP pool). No official figure is published.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 79.5% IN-val zero-shot (paper arXiv 2503.15485v2, Table 1, B/16 row; SigLIP B/16 is 76.2 and SigLIP2 B/16 is 78.2 in the same table). Caveat: the paper says all variants were initialized from SigLIP (v1), but the repo ships two checkpoints, SL1 (SigLIP init) and SL2 (SigLIP2 init), and does not say which one produced 79.5% or give per-checkpoint numbers.
row.other_zeroshot: Paper Table 1, B/16 TULIP: IN-v2 73.0, IN-ReaL 86.2, ObjectNet 74.2, IN 10-shot 73.8, COCO T->I 54.2 / I->T 70.1, Flickr30k T->I 81.8 / I->T 93.9.
row.weights_license: Not stated. No license is attached to the weights: the README, the project page and the paper are all silent, and there is no HF model card because HF hosting is marked 'Coming Soon'. The repo LICENSE is MIT text (UC Regents 2025 + OpenCLIP), and GitHub reports it as NOASSERTION/'Other'.
row.license_notes: 1) The repo LICENSE (github.com/tulip-berkeley/open_clip/blob/main/LICENSE) is the standard MIT permission text covering 'the Software and associated documentation files', with dual copyright: 'TULIP is Copyright (c) 2025 Regents of the University of California' plus the OpenCLIP authors. The README's 'modified licensing structure' line seems to mean only this dual-copyright MIT file; I found no extra restrictive clause. It is unclear whether the MIT grant covers the checkpoints, because the weights are hosted separately on Wasabi S3 with no license file beside them and no weights license is stated anywhere. 2) The project page (tulip-berkeley.github.io) licenses only the website (CC BY-SA 4.0). The arXiv license covers only the paper. 3) The HF tokenizer repo ZinengTang/tulip-tokenizer has no license and no README; tokenizer_config says tokenizer_class 'GemmaTokenizer' with Gemma special tokens, so it is derived from the Gemma/SigLIP2 vocabulary. SigLIP2 ships that vocabulary under Apache-2.0, but the TULIP repo itself states no license for it. 4) Training-data and provenance caveats: base weights come from SigLIP/SigLIP2 (Apache-2.0). Fine-tuning used 500M DataComp-1B samples (metadata CC-BY-4.0, images under their original copyrights), plus Recap-DataComp-1B captions made by a LLaMA-3-powered LLaVA-1.5, plus paraphrases generated with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The Llama 3.1 Community License says a distributed model trained on Llama outputs must have a name beginning with 'Llama', so that clause could plausibly apply. Bottom line: the code is MIT, but the weights have no explicit license. Treat commercial use as unclear unless the authors confirm, for example by email or a GitHub issue (the repo has no issues listed).

The architecture is plain ViT-B/16 plus a MAP attention pool (one learned-query multi-head attention), which converts to ONNX and TFLite like any SigLIP B/16 (LayerNorm, GELU-tanh, softmax attention), so I see no exotic ops; litert-torch/ai-edge-torch or ONNX-to-TFLite should work. Cost versus the shipped TinyCLIP-45M/32: about 2x the image params (92.9M vs 45M; int8 roughly 90-95 MB vs 46 MB) and about 4x the compute (196 tokens at patch 16 vs 49 at patch 32; ~17.7 vs ~4.4 GMACs). The text tower (~170M, int8 roughly 170 MB, about half of it the 109,871x768 embedding table) is a heavy on-demand download. The 697 MB checkpoint is smaller than fp32 of both towers (~263M params = ~1.05 GB), so it is probably bf16/fp16 and may hold extra training modules (decoders). row.arch:
Dual encoder, released 2022-11.
- Image tower: CLIP ModifiedResNet-50 (3-conv stem, avg-pool downsampling, attention-pool head). 224px, convolutional, no patch tokens. The final 7x7 grid feeds the attention pool, and the embedding is 1024-d.
- Text tower: RBT3, a 3-layer Chinese RoBERTa-wwm-ext. Width 768, vocab 21128, context length 52.
- Only the RN50 variant pairs a ResNet with a small text tower. The other variants are ViT-B/16, L/14, L/14-336 and H/14.
row.export_notes:
Weights format:
- The HF repo holds only the cn_clip-format checkpoint clip_cn_rn50.pt (fp32, ~308 MB for both towers). There is no transformers config or pytorch_model.bin.
- HF transformers' ChineseCLIPModel supports the ViT variants only, so load RN50 through `pip install cn_clip`.

Official export tools:
- cn_clip/deploy/pytorch_to_onnx.py supports RN50. It writes separate image and text ONNX files, FP32 and FP16, batch size 1, text context 52.
- onnx_to_tensorrt.py and pytorch_to_coreml.py (added 2023-11-30) also exist.

Measured latency (official deployment.md, T4 GPU, not mobile):
- Image: 12.93 ms PyTorch, 5.04 ms ONNX, 1.36 ms TensorRT.
- Text: 3.64 / 0.95 / 0.58 ms.

No TFLite/LiteRT export and no Android latency report were found.

Ops and size for a TFLite port:
- The ResNet body is fully GPU-delegate friendly (conv/BN/ReLU/avgpool).
- The attention-pool head is one small MHA over 50 tokens. It converts fine, but is the only non-conv part.
- int8 image tower would be about 38-40 MB, slightly smaller than the current TinyCLIP 46 MB.
- Expected A54 latency is in the same range as a ResNet-50 (~4 GMACs), probably similar to or slower than TinyCLIP-45M/32.

Fit for this app: poor.
- The text tower is Chinese-only, so English free-text search and the ~3,600 English concept vectors cannot be used without translating them to Chinese.
- Zero-shot quality (33.5% IN-1k, Chinese) is far below TinyCLIP's 62.7%.
- It is worth considering only for a Chinese-language UI, and even there CN-CLIP ViT-B/16 (48.3%) is much stronger.
row.image_gmacs: About 4.1 GMACs at 224px. This is not reported by Chinese-CLIP; it is estimated from the ResNet-50 conv body (~4.1 GMACs) plus a tiny attention-pool head, and the open_clip RN50 profile reports similar figures.

row.name: LY Corp clip-japanese-base (v1, 2024-04) and clip-japanese-base-v2 (2025-12)
row.org: LY Corporation (formerly LINE), HF org line-corporation

Expect ViT-B/16 class latency on a Galaxy A54: well above the current ~73 ms TinyCLIP/32, likely several times higher, since it has about 4x the tokens and about 2x the params. row.name: DiffCLIP ViT-B/16 (CC3M and CC12M checkpoints)
row.org: KAUST (Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud, Bernard Ghanem). HF user hammh0a, GitHub hammoudhasan/DiffCLIP
row.arch: CLIP dual encoder. Every attention layer in both towers is replaced with differential attention: two softmax maps are subtracted, with a learnable lambda and a per-head RMSNorm. Image tower: diff_vit_base_patch16_224, a ViT-B/16 (width 768, 12 layers), 224px, 196 patches plus CLS = 197 tokens. Text tower: 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, context 77, vocab 49408 (CLIP BPE). Shared embedding is 512-d. Training code comes from SLIP: 40 epochs, batch 4096.
row.image_params_M: ~86M. Not stated in absolute terms. This is my estimate from the config in diff_clip.py (standard ViT-B/16 size). The paper says DiffCLIP adds only ~0.003% parameters over CLIP-B/16.
row.text_params_M: ~63M. My estimate from the config (12 layers, width 512, vocab 49408, ctx 77), the same as the standard CLIP text tower: ~38M transformer plus ~25M token embedding.
row.image_gmacs: ~17.5 GMACs at 224px. My estimate for a standard ViT-B/16; the paper reports none and only claims "negligible" overhead.
row.in1k_zeroshot: CC12M: 33.8% (baseline CLIP 31.8%). CC3M: 14.4% (baseline CLIP 13.6%). Source: Table 2 of arXiv 2503.06626 (TMLR 2025). This is far below TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 62.7%.
row.other_zeroshot: Table 2, Recall@5. CC12M: Flickr30k image 62.2, MSCOCO image 42.3, Flickr30k text 77.4, MSCOCO text 55.5. CC3M: Flickr image 32.9, COCO image 20.9, Flickr text 44.7, COCO text 27.6.
row.weights_license: None declared (unclear)
row.license_notes: No license anywhere I checked. The HF repos hammh0a/DiffCLIP_ViTB16_CC12M and _CC3M have no README or model card, no cardData and no license tag; each holds only .gitattributes and checkpoint_best.pt. On GitHub, hammoudhasan/DiffCLIP has license=null in the API, and LICENSE, LICENSE.md and LICENSE.txt all return 404. The README has no license section. The paper states no license (only the arXiv paper license). With no license, the default is all rights reserved, so this cannot be shipped commercially without explicit permission from the authors. Data caveat: trained on CC3M/CC12M (Google Conceptual Captions). Those datasets carry their own terms, and the images belong to their owners. Moot here: accuracy and size already rule the model out.
row.load_id: No open_clip, timm or HF transformers ID. Use hf_hub_download('hammh0a/DiffCLIP_ViTB16_CC12M', 'checkpoint_best.pt') and load it into DiffCLIP_VITB16() from github.com/hammoudhasan/DiffCLIP diff_clip.py, stripping the 'module.' prefix from checkpoint['state_dict'], as test_models.py does. The text tower is included: the checkpoint is the full CLIP state_dict.
row.export_notes: I found no TFLite, ONNX or CoreML export, and no mobile latency report. The checkpoint is a 1.80 GB .pt per repo (1,796,192,519 bytes), probably including optimizer state. I estimate the int8 image tower at ~86 MB. Differential attention uses only standard ops (extra softmax, scalar-weighted subtract, RMSNorm), so it should convert to TFLite and run on the GPU delegate. Expected cost is about 2x the attention-softmax work of plain ViT-B/16. Latency should be well above TinyCLIP-45M/32: 197 tokens vs 50, roughly 4x the GMACs. Verdict: reject. It is weaker (33.8% vs 62.7% IN-1k ZS), about 2x larger, much slower, and its license is unclear. It is a research artifact comparing attention types at CC scale. The same author's sibling repos (hammh0a/ViTB16_CC12M, ViTB16_CC3M, SynthCLIP_*) are also unlicensed CC-scale ViT-B/16 baselines and equally unsuitable.
row.released: 2025-03 (HF repos created 2025-03-09; GitHub repo 2025-03-07; arXiv 2503.06626; published TMLR 2025)

row.org: KAUST + University of Oxford (Hammoud, Itani, Pizzati, Torr, Bibi, Ghanem)
row.arch: CLIP dual encoder built on the SLIP codebase. Image tower is timm vit_base_patch16_224 (ViT-B/16, patch 16, 196 tokens + CLS), 768-d, with a 768->512 projection.
