row.name: UniCL Swin-T (yfcc14m / in21k / in22k / in21k_yfcc14m[_half] / in1k_* checkpoints)
row.org: Microsoft (Jianwei Yang et al., "Unified Contrastive Learning in Image-Text-Label Space", CVPR 2022, arXiv 2204.03610)
row.arch: Image: Swin-T (embed 96, depths [2,2,6,2], heads [3,6,12,24], window 7, patch 4), pooled features 768-d, then a 768x512 projection. Text: CLIP-style causal transformer with 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, ctx 77, CLIP BPE tokenizer (openai/clip-vit-base-patch32, vocab 49408), 512x512 projection. Shared space is 512-d. Source: configs/unicl_swin_tiny.yaml, config.py, model/text_encoder/*.
row.image_params_M: ~27.9M, computed by me and not stated anywhere: Swin-T backbone without head is 27.5M (timm swin_tiny is 28.3M including a 0.77M IN-1k head), plus a 0.39M image projection.
row.text_params_M: ~63.4M, computed by me from the config and not stated: token embedding 49408x512 = 25.3M, 12 blocks x 3.15M = 37.8M, plus pos-emb, ln_final and the 0.26M projection. That is about 3.5x TinyCLIP's 18M text tower, and 40% of it is the embedding table. Total is ~91.3M. This matches the 183.4 MB release .pth files only if they are stored in fp16 (91.3M x 2 B). I inferred that and did not open the files.
row.image_gmacs: ~4.5 GMACs (standard Swin-T at 224, per the litert-community swin_tiny card), plus a negligible projection
row.in1k_zeroshot: Weak. True zero-shot IN-1k from the official README model zoo, Swin-T: yfcc14m 30.1%, in21k 28.5%, in21k_yfcc14m_half 36.4%, in21k_yfcc14m 40.5% (best true ZS). in22k shows 66.8%, but IN-22K contains the IN-1k classes and images, so that number is not zero-shot. The in1k / in1k_gcc3m / in1k_yfcc14m / in1k_gcc15m checkpoints report 79.9-81.8% "Top-1 IN-1K", but those models were trained on IN-1k labels, so that is supervised accuracy, not ZS. TinyCLIP-45M/32 (62.7% true ZS) beats every Swin-T UniCL checkpoint by more than 20 points.
row.other_zeroshot: README, average over 14 datasets ZS: yfcc14m 36.3, in21k 37.8, in22k 38.9, in21k_yfcc14m_half 45.5, in21k_yfcc14m 49.1, in1k 30.2, in1k_gcc3m 39.0, in1k_yfcc14m 40.0, in1k_gcc15m 45.1. No COCO/Flickr retrieval numbers in the README.
row.weights_license: MIT (repo LICENSE, "Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation"; GitHub API spdx_id MIT). The weights are GitHub release assets in the same MIT repo, with no separate weights license.
row.license_notes: Code and the weights distributed in the repo's v1.0 release are under MIT. Neither the README nor the release adds a separate weights license or use restriction; the only extra is the standard Microsoft trademark notice. The original Azure blob (projects4jw.blob.core.windows.net/unicl/release/) has no license file of its own, and the README says the old links are broken and points to the GitHub v1.0 release, which has 15 .pth assets including model_state_dict.pt. I mark this "unclear" rather than "yes" because of the training data. Every checkpoint uses ImageNet-21K/22K or ImageNet-1K labels (ImageNet terms limit use to non-commercial research), YFCC-14M (per-image CC licenses, some NC), or GCC-3M/15M (Conceptual Captions terms). Whether those terms carry over to MIT-licensed weights is legally unsettled. Of the checkpoints, yfcc14m.pth is the only one with no ImageNet labels, and it has the weakest ZS at 30.1%. On paper the license is as permissive as TinyCLIP's MIT; the data caveat is the same kind TinyCLIP carries via LAION/YFCC, plus ImageNet.
row.load_id: No open_clip, timm or HF model id. Load it with the microsoft/UniCL repo code (UniCLModel + configs/unicl_swin_tiny.yaml, tokenizer = HF CLIPTokenizer openai/clip-vit-base-patch32). Weights are at https://github.com/microsoft/UniCL/releases/tag/v1.0, e.g. in21k_yfcc14m.pth (183,403,308 bytes), yfcc14m.pth, in22k.pth, in1k_gcc15m.pth (183,465,563 bytes). The text tower is included in each checkpoint, so it is actually released.
row.export_notes: I found no existing TFLite/ONNX/CoreML export or mobile latency report for UniCL itself, and the HF CVPR demo Space (CVPR/unicl-zero-shot-img-recog) shows a build error. Two exports of the plain Swin-T backbone (IN-1k timm, not UniCL) give an idea of how the image tower would behave. litert-community/swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224 ships fp32 and static-int8 .tflite files, both listed as "Supported with CPU fallback" on the GPU delegate. In the int8 file, attention, LayerNorm and other ops stay fp32, and GPU needs fp32 precision. qualcomm/Swin-Tiny reports 110 MB float / 29.9 MB w8a16, with NPU latencies of about 4.7 ms TFLite float on Snapdragon 8 Elite and about 14 ms on 8 Gen 1. Those are NPU numbers, not the GPU/XNNPACK path this app uses, and there are no Exynos/A54 numbers. Swin's window partition, cyclic shift (roll) and relative position bias gather convert awkwardly; an HF forum thread reports trouble going PyTorch to ONNX to TFLite. Expect partial GPU-delegate fallback. A rough int8 image tower would be ~28-30 MB, smaller than TinyCLIP's 46 MB. The text tower would be ~63 MB int8 or ~127 MB fp16, larger than TinyCLIP's.
row.released: 2022 (arXiv April 2022, CVPR 2022). The v1.0 release assets are on GitHub, and the last push to the repo was 2023-11-10.

verdicts.corrections:
I tried to refute the row and could not. Every checked fact matches the primary sources.
(a) License: the repo LICENSE is MIT ("Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation") and the GitHub API reports spdx_id MIT. The v1.0 release assets add no separate weights license, and the README adds no research-only or non-commercial clause. Marking commercial_ok as "unclear" is the right call because of the training data: ImageNet labels are under non-commercial research terms, YFCC images carry mixed CC licenses, and GCC has its own terms. The MIT license itself allows commercial use.
(b) Numbers: the README true zero-shot table for Swin-T matches the row exactly: YFCC-14M 30.1 / 36.3, IN-21K 28.5 / 37.8, IN-22K 66.8 / 38.9, IN-21K(half)+YFCC(half) 36.4 / 45.5, IN-21K+YFCC-14M 40.5 / 49.1. The in1k* table header is "Top-1 on IN-1K" (79.9-81.8), so the row is right that those are supervised numbers, not zero-shot. Its 14-dataset ZS values (30.2 / 39.0 / 40.0 / 45.1) also match.
Architecture: the config matches. DIM_PROJECTION is 512, Swin embed 96, depths [2,2,6,2], heads [3,6,12,24], window 7. The text encoder is 'transformer' with width 512, 8 heads, 12 layers, CONTEXT_LENGTH 77, and the 'clip' tokenizer; vocab_size comes from the tokenizer.
Param counts: the parameter counts in the row are its own estimates; the README states none. My recalculation of the text tower matches: 49408x512 = 25.3M, plus 12 x ~3.15M, plus pos-emb, ln_final and projection, about 63.4M. The fp16 inference is supported by the release sizes. The Swin-T .pth files are 183,403,308 to 183,465,563 bytes (about 91.7M params at 2 B each). The Swin-B files come in two sizes, 604.5 MB and 302.6 MB, a 2x ratio, which fits fp32 and fp16 copies of about 151M params (Swin-B 88M + text 63M).
One small fix: the row names in21k_yfcc14m.pth as 183,403,308 bytes and in1k_gcc15m.pth as 183,465,563 bytes. Both are correct, but in1k.pth is 183,403,308 and in21k.pth is 183,465,563, so the two sizes alternate between checkpoints. This does not change anything else.
The repo's last push was 2023-11-10, as the row says.

I found nothing to refute. Each claim in the row checks out against primary sources:
(a) License. The repo LICENSE is MIT ("Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation"), and the GitHub API reports spdx_id MIT. The v1.0 release has an empty body and no separate weights license. The README has only the standard CLA and trademark boilerplate, with no research-only or non-commercial clause. The row's commercial_ok="unclear" (because of the ImageNet-21K/22K/1K label data) is a fair, conservative call. The weights license itself is MIT.
(b) Architecture. configs/unicl_swin_tiny.yaml matches the row: embed 96, depths [2,2,6,2], heads [3,6,12,24], window 7, DIM_PROJECTION 512, text transformer width 512 / 8 heads / 12 layers. config.py sets IMG_SIZE 224, CONTEXT_LENGTH 77 and TOKENIZER 'clip'. build.py uses CLIPTokenizer openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 (vocab 49408). model.py confirms image_projection (dim_out x 512) and text_projection.
(c) Param counts. These are derived, not stated anywhere, but they are arithmetically sound. Swin-T without its head is about 27.5M, plus a 0.39M projection, so about 27.9M. The text tower is 49408x512 embedding (25.3M) + 12 blocks (37.8M) + extras, so about 63.4M. Release asset sizes support the fp16-storage inference. The Swin-T .pth files are 183,403,308 to 183,465,563 bytes, which is about 91.7M params at 2 B each. The Swin-B files are 604,528,191 bytes (fp32) and 302,580,927 bytes (fp16 variants), which fits about 151M params (Swin-B ~88M + the same ~63M text tower). That also suggests the text tower is about 63M.
(d) Zero-shot. The README tables match exactly. True IN-1k ZS: yfcc14m 30.1, in21k 28.5, in22k 66.8 (not true ZS, since IN-22K contains the IN-1k classes), in21k_yfcc14m_half 36.4, in21k_yfcc14m 40.5. The 14-dataset averages are 36.3/37.8/38.9/45.5/49.1, and for the in1k* checkpoints 30.2/39.0/40.0/45.1. The in1k* table is headed "Top-1 on IN-1K" (supervised), at 79.9/80.2/81.1/81.8.
Minor nit: the release also includes Swin-B assets (in21k_swin_base, yfcc14m_swin_base, in21k_yfcc14m[_half]_swin_base, in21k_yfcc14m_gcc15m_swin_base). These are out of scope because the image tower is too large at about 88M.

row.name: OpenVision 3 ViT-B/2 (openvision3-vit-base-patch2-32 and -28)
row.org: UCSC-VLAA (UC Santa Cruz, with JHU, UNC, UC Berkeley and NVIDIA)
row.arch: A ViT-B (12 layers, width 768, 12 heads, avg-pool, 768-d projection) with patch size 2. It runs on 16-channel FLUX.1 VAE latents, not on RGB pixels. The -32 repo takes a 32x32 latent, which comes from a 256px image and gives 256 tokens (pos-emb 257x768). The -28 repo takes a 28x28 latent from a 224px image and gives 196 tokens. The front end is a frozen FLUX.1-dev VAE encoder (8x downsample). It is a diffusers AutoencoderKL with block_out_channels 128/256/512/512, mounted through the HF mirror Letian2003/black-forest-labs_FLUX.1-dev_vae. The paper's training has contrastive + captioning + pixel-reconstruction branches. The text_cfg in the config lists a 12-layer, width-512 CLIP text transformer, but no text weights are shipped.
row.image_params_M: 85.9M for the ViT only. I counted this myself from the tensor shapes in the -32 checkpoint's pickle index (150 tensors, 85,893,120 params), and it matches the 343.6 MB fp32 file size. The paper gives no param count. You also need the FLUX VAE encoder: the full AE is 167.7 MB fp32 (~84M params), and the encoder half is roughly 34M (my estimate). Realistic image-side total is about 120M, which is over the ~100M ceiling.
row.image_gmacs: Not reported. My estimate from the configs: the ViT-B at 256 tokens is ~22 GMACs. The FLUX VAE encoder at 256px is ~120-140 GMACs, because it runs 3x3 convs at 128-512 channels at full and half resolution. The total is roughly 40-60x the current TinyCLIP-45M/32 (~3-4 GMACs).
row.text_params_M: Not released. The config's text_cfg (12L, width 512, vocab 49408) would be about 63M params (my computation). But the HF checkpoints contain only vision keys (conv1, class_embedding, positional_embedding, transformer.resblocks.*, ln_post, proj), with no token_embedding, text transformer, text_projection or logit_scale.
row.resolution: 256px image -> 32x32x16 latent (-32 repo). 224px image -> 28x28x16 latent (-28 repo).
row.in1k_zeroshot: Not reported. The paper (arXiv 2601.15369 v1/v2) has no ImageNet zero-shot or retrieval tables. It only reports LLaVA-1.5/NeXT understanding: B/2 vs OpenAI CLIP B/16, e.g. SeedBench 63.1 vs 62.2 and POPE 83.7 vs 82.9. It also reports reconstruction (ImageNet rFID 0.187) and generation. Zero-shot can't be measured anyway, because no text tower is released.
row.other_zeroshot: None reported (no COCO/Flickr retrieval in the paper).
row.weights_license: unclear (no license on the HF weight repos; the code repo is Apache-2.0)
row.license_notes:
License status by source:
- All 3 OV3 HF repos (base-patch2-32, base-patch2-28, large-patch2-32) contain only .gitattributes, open_clip_config.json and open_clip_pytorch_model.bin. There is no README/model card, no license tag and no LICENSE file.
- The GitHub repo UCSC-VLAA/OpenVision is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file plus a README "License" section). Nothing there extends that license to the OV3 weights explicitly.
- The paper says it "will fully open-source" code, data and checkpoints, with no license named. The arXiv paper text itself is CC BY 4.0, which does not cover the weights.
- Training data is DataComp recaptioned with LLaVA-Llama-3 (Recap-DataComp). Its data license is not stated in the paper.

A bigger blocker is the required VAE front end:
- The project page and openvision3_test.py point to FLUX.1-dev (default vae_id Letian2003/black-forest-labs_FLUX.1-dev_vae, a third-party re-upload with no license tag).
- black-forest-labs' own README lists FLUX.1 [dev] under the "FLUX.1-dev Non-Commercial License".
- FLUX.1-schnell (Apache-2.0) also ships an ae.safetensors (16 latent channels). It is widely believed to be the same autoencoder, but I could not verify byte identity because the BFL repos are gated.
- If you used the schnell copy, the VAE could be Apache-2.0, but that is unverified.

Net: the ViT's license is unclear, and the documented pipeline depends on a non-commercial-licensed VAE.
row.load_id: Vision encoder only: hf-hub:UCSC-VLAA/openvision3-vit-base-patch2-32 (or -28), loaded via the repo's own src/convert_upload/open_clip factory create_vision_encoder_and_transforms (stock open_clip lacks in_channels/no_ln_pre handling). VAE: diffusers AutoencoderKL.from_pretrained('Letian2003/black-forest-labs_FLUX.1-dev_vae'). Latents use posterior.mean * scaling_factor 0.3611; the model takes inputs in [-1,1].
row.export_notes:
No TFLite/ONNX/CoreML exports exist, and there are no mobile latency reports. The only timing in the paper is TPU v4 training.
- The ViT part is plain and would export easily.
- The FLUX VAE encoder is a heavy full-resolution conv stack with GroupNorm (32 groups) and a mid-block self-attention over 32x32=1024 positions. GroupNorm is a known weak spot for the TFLite GPU delegate and int8 quantization.
- Expect several hundred ms to over 1 s per photo on a Galaxy A54-class device, versus 73 ms now (estimate, not measured).
- Download size: ~86M ViT plus ~34M VAE encoder is about 120 MB int8 / 240 MB fp16 before any text tower, versus 46 MB now.
- The model only emits patch tokens and a pooled 768-d feature with no matching text tower, so it can't do zero-shot tagging or free-text search.

Verdict: not a fit for this app. It is an MLLM/generation tokenizer, not a CLIP replacement.

row.name: NVIDIA C-RADIOv3-B
row.arch: An agglomerative ViT-B/16 (timm vit_base_patch16_v2_224: 12 blocks, width 768) with CPE (a cropped position-embedding table of 128x128 positions, so up to 2048px input) plus 8 per-teacher CLS tokens and 4 registers. It was distilled from four teachers: DFN5B CLIP ViT-H-14-378, SigLIP2-so400m, DINOv2-g/14-reg and SAM ViT-H. The teacher list comes from the checkpoint args and HF config.json. Note that the B checkpoint's SigLIP2 teacher is so400m, not SigLIP2-g as the README and the hint say. Text alignment works only through per-teacher MLP adaptor heads: 'siglip2' (1152-d) and 'clip' (DFN, 1024-d). The siglip2 summary head (fc1 + blocks + final) is about 7.5M params. At 224px there are 196 patch tokens plus about 12 prefix tokens. The preferred resolution is 512.
row.image_params_M: 98.25M in HF model.safetensors (counted from the safetensors header). That breaks down into about 85.7M for the ViT-B core and 12.58M for the 16384x768 CPE position table. To ship at a fixed resolution you would resample the table to the needed grid, for example about 0.2M at 256px, and add the siglip2 adaptor summary head of about 7.5M. A deployable image tower with text alignment is therefore about 93-94M params, roughly 2x TinyCLIP-45M, or about 95 MB at int8. The 7.5M head was computed by me from the checkpoint pickle and is not stated by NVIDIA.
row.text_params_M: No RADIO text tower exists. The only commercially usable text path is the unmodified Google SigLIP2-so400m text tower (google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-naflex). It is 707.8M params, of which 295M is the 256k-vocab Gemma-tokenizer embedding (computed by me from the HF safetensors header). The other text path, the 'clip' adaptor, needs the DFN5B ViT-H-14 text tower, which is about 350M and Apple-AMLR licensed.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 71.30% (kNN 81.22%), from the comparison table on the nvidia/C-RADIOv4-H HF model card. The resolution and adaptor are not stated. The C-RADIOv4 tech report (arXiv 2601.17237) says peak zero-shot is reached at 1024px with aspect-preserving resize, so the 224-256px figure is probably lower, though nobody reports it. The C-RADIOv3-B card itself gives no zero-shot number. For comparison: v3-L 79.95, v3-H 82.65.
row.other_zeroshot: None reported for B. The dense linear-probe scores on the C-RADIOv4-H card are ADE20k 49.79 mIoU and VOC 84.68 mIoU. No COCO/Flickr retrieval is reported.
row.weights_license: NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement (June 2024). HF metadata: license: other, license_name: nvidia-open-model-license.
row.license_notes:
The C-RADIOv3-B weights may be used commercially. The license PDF says "Models are commercially useable", allows derivative models (quantized or converted copies count) and gives a perpetual, royalty-free grant to sell and distribute. Conditions:
(1) A NOTICE file must ship with the copies and contain "Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Open Model License".
(2) The license terminates if you file copyright or patent litigation claiming the model infringes.
(3) NVIDIA may update the agreement for legal or regulatory reasons, and you must then comply or stop using it.
(4) No trademark rights.
The June 2024 PDF has no guardrail clause.
The GitHub repo code (NVlabs/RADIO) is under the NVIDIA Source Code License-NC, which is non-commercial. Older RADIO and E-RADIO weights are NSCL-NC too. Only the C-RADIO-prefixed weights are commercial. This does not matter much in practice: the HF repo ships its own copy of the model code under the model license, and the graph is a standard ViT you would re-export anyway.
The card's training data is the NV-CC-Img-Text-Dataset (about 700M images, "commercially viable").
The text path: the 'siglip2' adaptor pairs with Google SigLIP2-so400m, which is Apache-2.0, so commercial use is OK. The 'clip' adaptor pairs with apple/DFN5B-CLIP-ViT-H-14-378, which is apple-amlr (research-only), so it is excluded. The DFN teacher being Apple-licensed does not taint the RADIO weights, because NVIDIA licenses those itself.
row.load_id: torch.hub.load('NVlabs/RADIO','radio_model',version='c-radio_v3-b',adaptor_names=['siglip2']). The adaptor is named 'siglip2' because that is the teacher name in this checkpoint. The adaptor head weights are only in c-radio_v3-b_half.pth.tar (fp16, 547 MB, 173M tensors including all 4 teachers' heads and projections). HF AutoModel.from_pretrained('nvidia/C-RADIOv3-B', trust_remote_code=True) loads model.safetensors, which is the backbone only: no adaptor keys and adaptor_configs={} in config.json. The text tower is loaded separately from google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-naflex (AutoModel .text_model, max_length 64, canonicalized lowercase text).
row.resolution: Any multiple of 16, tested 256-2048. Preferred 512x512, max 2048. A fixed-res export at 224 or 256 is possible by baking the CPE crop.
row.image_gmacs: Not reported. My estimate from standard ViT-B/16 math: about 18-19 GMACs at 224 (about 208 tokens), about 22-23 at 256 and about 90+ at 512. That is roughly 4-5x a ViT-B/32 like TinyCLIP-45M/32 at 224.
row.export_notes:
No existing ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or mobile latency report found. Search turned up nothing, and the card lists only PyTorch, TensorRT and the TAO Toolkit 24.10 runtime on NVIDIA hardware.
The backbone is a plain timm ViT (LayerNorm, GELU, MHA), so it should be friendly to the GPU delegate and XNNPACK once you fix the resolution and bake the CPE position-table crop/interpolate into a constant. The siglip2 summary head is a small MLP.
I have not measured latency. Being about 4-5x the FLOPs of the current ViT-B/32 at 224, it would likely be several times slower than 73 ms on an A54. At the preferred 512 res it is far worse.
The text path is not practical on-device: the SigLIP2-so400m text tower is 708M params (about 700 MB int8) with a Gemma 256k tokenizer. It is far over budget for free-text search, though the 3,600 concept vectors could still be precomputed offline.
For context, C-RADIOv4 (Jan 2026) comes only in SO400M (431M) and H (653M) sizes, so it has no small variant.
row.released: HF repo created 2025-04-24, with a card release date of 2025-03-26. Publicly announced in the GitHub README on 2025-06-03. Superseded by C-RADIOv4 (SO400M/H only) on 2026-01-27.

verdicts.corrections:
I could not refute the row. Everything I re-checked against primary sources matches:
- **License:** HF metadata says license: other, license_name nvidia-open-model-license, linking the June 2024 PDF. The repo is not gated (gated=False). The card says "This model is ready for commercial/non-commercial use."
- **License PDF text:** it contains "Models are commercially useable", the Notice-file attribution requirement, termination if you file patent/copyright litigation, and NVIDIA's right to update the agreement for legal or regulatory reasons. I found no guardrail clause.
- **Image param count:** the safetensors total is 98,254,857, which is the backbone with the CPE table. The 16384x768 table is 12.58M, so the 85.7M core figure holds.
- **Teachers:** config.json lists dfn5b ViT-H-14-378-quickgelu ('clip'), siglip2-so400m ('siglip2'), dinov2_vitg14_reg and SAM vit-h. The backbone is vit_base_patch16_v2_224.
- **Zero-shot:** the nvidia/C-RADIOv4-H card's comparison table gives C-RADIOv3-B Zero-Shot 71.30 and KNN 81.22.

Caveats, which are not refutations:
- Resolution and adaptor for the 71.30 figure are unstated, so the number at 224-256px is likely lower.
- The 7.5M adaptor-head and 707.8M SigLIP2 text-tower counts are the row author's own calculations. I did not recompute them, but they are consistent with 256k x 1152 = 295M embeddings.
- The usable text path is the 708M SigLIP2-so400m text tower, which in practice rules out on-device free-text search.

row.name: TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-45M/32-Text-18M (LAION-400M checkpoint)
row.org: Microsoft (TinyCLIP, ICCV 2023; repo wkcn/TinyCLIP, mirrored from microsoft/Cream)
row.arch: Auto weight-inheritance (mask-pruned) ViT-B/32. The open_clip config is the full ViT-B/32 skeleton (vision: 12 layers, width 768, patch 32, 224px; text: 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads, ctx 77, vocab 49408; embed_dim 512) with "mask_image": true and "mask_text": true. The effective size (about 45M image, about 18M text) comes from learned masks. 7x7=49 patch tokens + CLS. Same architecture and config file as the shipped LAION+YFCC checkpoint.
row.image_params_M: ~45 (from the model name/README "half parameters of ViT-B/32"; not computable from the config, which is the unpruned ViT-B/32 skeleton ~88M plus masks)
row.text_params_M: ~18 (from the model name; config skeleton is the full 12x512 text tower ~63M, pruned by masks)
row.image_gmacs: 3.7 G (README table, which reports MACs, not image-only GMACs). The README lists 1.9 G for the identical-architecture LAION+YFCC checkpoint and does not explain the difference.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 61.4% (README model zoo table, LAION-400M row). The shipped LAION+YFCC-400M checkpoint scores 62.7%, so this one is a 1.3-point downgrade.
row.other_zeroshot: not reported in README for this checkpoint (paper reports broader results mainly for other variants)
row.weights_license: MIT (repo LICENSE: "MIT License, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation")
row.license_notes: The repo LICENSE is MIT. The weights are GitHub release assets in the same author's wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo, and the README shows no separate weights license or use restriction. This checkpoint has no HF model card, so there is no card that could add restrictions. Data caveat: it was trained only on LAION-400M (web-scraped, CC-BY 4.0 metadata). LAION-400M was later superseded by Re-LAION over CSAM findings, which is a reputational/data-provenance caveat, not a weights-license restriction. The shipped LAION+YFCC checkpoint has the same LAION exposure.
row.load_id: open_clip with the TinyCLIP fork: open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-45M-32-Text-18M', pretrained='LAION400M') (from inference.py in wkcn/TinyCLIP). Direct checkpoint: https://github.com/wkcn/TinyCLIP-model-zoo/releases/download/checkpoints/TinyCLIP-auto-ViT-45M-32-Text-18M-LAION400M.pt (HEAD check returned 200, 177,369,381 bytes). Not on the HF Hub: wkcn's HF models are only ViT-40M/32-LAION400M, ViT-61M/32-LAION400M, ViT-39M/16-YFCC15M and ViT-8M/16-YFCC15M.
row.released: 2023 (ICCV 2023 / arXiv 2309.12314; auto checkpoints in the TinyCLIP model zoo)
row.export_notes: Both the image and text towers are released in the single .pt. The model needs the TinyCLIP open_clip fork, because the masked/auto configs are not in upstream open_clip. Exporting to TFLite/ONNX means materializing the pruned dimensions from the masks first, the same pipeline as the currently shipped LAION+YFCC checkpoint (identical config), so the existing export path should apply unchanged. I found no third-party TFLite/ONNX/CoreML export or mobile latency report for this LAION-400M checkpoint. Expected on-device latency is the same as the shipped model (~73 ms/photo on an A54), since the architecture is identical. Verdict: not an upgrade. It is the same size and 1.3 points worse on IN-1k zero-shot than what is already shipped. List it only for TinyCLIP table completeness.

row.name: ProLIP-ViT-B-16-DC-1B-12_8B
row.org: NAVER AI Lab / NAVER Cloud (Sanghyuk Chun et al.)
row.arch: ViT-B/16 image tower (12 layers, width 768, patch 16, 224px: 196 patch tokens + CLS + 1 extra learned uncertainty token) plus uncertainty projection heads. Text tower: 12-layer, width-768 transformer with NO causal mask, context 64, vocab 32100 (SigLIP SentencePiece tokenizer timm/ViT-B-16-SigLIP), last-token pooling plus its own uncertainty token. Joint embedding dim is 768. It outputs a mean (L2-normalised, works as a normal CLIP embedding) and a log-std vector; the uncertainty heads can be dropped for plain CLIP use. Built on open_clip-style code with custom ProLIP modules.
row.image_params_M: 86.98 (computed by me from the safetensors header: total of all 'visual.*' tensors). That includes about 0.59M for uncertainty_proj and unc_embedding, which are droppable, so the mean-only tower is about 86.4M. This is about 1.9x TinyCLIP-45M and well over the ~50M target, though under the 100M ceiling.
row.text_params_M: 110.94 (computed by me from the safetensors header: all 'text.*' tensors). Token embedding alone is 24.7M because of the 32100-token vocab. Total checkpoint is 197.92M params, F32, 791.7 MB.
row.image_gmacs: About 17.6 GMACs at 224px. This is my estimate from the standard ViT-B/16 figure in the open_clip table (17.58) plus one extra token; it is not reported by the authors.
row.in1k_zeroshot: 74.6% top-1, from the official HF model card and the ProLIP paper (arXiv 2410.18857, ICLR 2025). Trained on DataComp-1B with 12.8B seen samples.
row.other_zeroshot: From the HF model card: ImageNet distribution shifts 63.0%, VTAB 63.7%, retrieval 59.6% (DataComp-eval retrieval average of Flickr/COCO), 38-task average 63.3%. Per-dataset COCO/Flickr recall numbers are not on the card.
row.weights_license: MIT
row.license_notes: The HF weights repo declares license: mit in its card metadata and API tags, and the card adds no use restrictions and does not mention research-only or non-commercial. The GitHub code repo naver-ai/prolip LICENSE is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2024-present NAVER Cloud Corp.", and the README License section is also MIT. The weights license and code license match. Caveats: (1) The HF weights repo has no separate LICENSE file, so the license rests on the card metadata only. (2) Training data is DataComp-1B: the metadata is CC-BY-4.0, but the images are web-scraped with their own copyrights. This is the same situation as OpenCLIP DataComp models, not a weights-license restriction. (3) The tokenizer comes from timm/ViT-B-16-SigLIP (Google SigLIP SentencePiece, Apache-2.0 per the timm/big_vision release; I did not re-verify it here), and the image processor config comes from openai/clip-vit-base-patch16 (MIT).
row.load_id: HF: SanghyukChun/ProLIP-ViT-B-16-DC-1B-12_8B, loaded via `pip install prolip`: ProLIPHF.from_pretrained(...); HFTokenizer('timm/ViT-B-16-SigLIP', context_length=64, clean='canonicalize'); CLIPProcessor 'openai/clip-vit-base-patch16'. Note that the card's own snippet has a typo (it uses ...12_8M); the GitHub README uses the correct ...12_8B. It is not in open_clip's pretrained registry or timm.
row.export_notes: I found no existing ONNX, TFLite, CoreML or mobile latency report for ProLIP; a web search returned nothing. Architecturally it is a vanilla ViT-B/16 (LayerNorm, GELU, standard MHA) plus one extra token and linear heads, so the usual PyTorch to LiteRT path (ai-edge-torch, or ONNX to TFLite) should work, with no exotic ops for the GPU delegate. The cost is the problem for this app: about 87M params gives roughly 87 MB int8 for the image tower (vs 46 MB now) and about 111 MB int8 for the text tower. About 17.6 GMACs per image vs roughly 4.4 for ViT-B/32-class models suggests a latency several times the current ~73 ms on a Galaxy A54; this is my inference, not measured. The ProLIP family has no smaller variant: the HF collection holds only B/16, L/16, SO400M and H/14 (fine-tuned), plus LongProLIP B/16. On compute and size it is strictly worse than OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 DataComp-XL (MIT, 72.7%, ~88M but 49 tokens) for a 1.9-point IN-1k gain. Its uncertainty output is a nice-to-have, for example as a confidence score for tagging.
